What if you want to find someone to talk to about your memories, but you can't receive completion therapy?

Hello teachers, I have been in counseling for a while and I feel that those people in my memories are so precious, but most of them have already parted ways with me or gone their own way, I can no longer find them to say the things that my heart wants to say, but I am not quite able to accept the completion therapy (I understand the completion therapy is to say to myself how I feel?). But I'm not very comfortable with Gestalt therapy (I understand Gestalt therapy is saying your feelings to yourself?).
output: Hello to the subject. When we are not able to get in touch with some people or express our emotions with each other due to various limitations, we feel the depression of this emotion. Human emotions need to be expressed so that our human energy can flow. In fact, there are ways to express this emotion in counseling. One of my personal favorites is to "write a letter to the other person". This is a form of writing therapy. Writing is a way of realizing healing by writing down in writing what you have experienced, what you feel, and what you want to express but are unable to. This is also somewhat similar to narrative therapy. The process in which a person narrates is a process of self-exposure, and this process is inherently healing. Find a safe environment and allow yourself to write a letter to the other person. There is no limit to the content of the letter, so you can write down what you want to say to the other person and your emotions. After writing the letter, you can read it out to yourself and then feel the difference between how you felt before and after writing the letter. The letter, of course, doesn't have to be actually sent to the other person. If you can read the letter to someone you trust who can listen to you well, that's okay too. This method is easy and convenient, requires less time and circumstances, and can also be done alone. What makes words different from other forms is that written down words can be seen. You can see your inner feelings by seeing the words, which is a process of deepening self-understanding. In my writing healing process, I can feel the immense power of words, words have a powerful energy. I have experienced many times that in the process of writing, my emotions are expressed and it is also a mirror that allows me to see myself from a distance. Another approach is the Gestalt technique called "Empty Chair Dialogue". In Emotionally Focused Therapy, the Empty Chair Technique is also an important intervention technique that can help the visitor to relieve inner conflicts and better express and release emotions. The Empty Chair Conversation technique is generally used to help visitors resolve emotions about significant others in their lives. You can prepare two chairs, sit on one chair, and imagine that the significant other is sitting on the empty chair opposite you. Then one expresses one's thoughts and feelings to the other person. Then you can sit in the opposite chair, visualize yourself as the significant other, and then respond to what you have just expressed to yourself. If assisted by a counselor, after the visitor has fully expressed his or her emotions, the counselor will give the visitor some emotional validation that it is normal to feel such emotions, and assist the visitor in replacing non-adaptive emotions with adaptive ones. If you do this process on your own, you may not be able to see the full scope of the problem and may be limited to your own perspective. But practicing on your own can be helpful. In your question, you said that you could not accept the way of talking to yourself about your feelings in Completion Therapy, so I think you are referring to the "dialogic practice" technique in Completion Therapy. The empty chair technique I mentioned above is also a type of Gestalt therapy, but the difference is that the client plays two roles. The essence of this technique is a kind of role-playing, through this method, is the surface of the introjection, is the loss of the person to fully experience the conflict, access to the hidden depths of the emotions. The important thing about this technique is the experience. Another way to role-play is to find someone you trust, in a way that is more similar to the Empty Chair Conversation technique above, and it is better if a counselor accompanies you through the process. Having someone to respond to you can also open up the perspective somewhat. Also, I think analyzing your dreams is a more valuable way to go. Because my personal experience is that I sometimes dream about loved ones who have passed away, and in dreams, it is possible to analyze some of your inner complexes. Changes in dreams can also reveal changes within a person. Dream interpretation itself is one of the core techniques of the psychoanalytic school. It is not a bad idea to try to deepen your understanding of yourself by recording and analyzing your dreams. These are my answers, I hope they are helpful to you. Blessings to you.

When someone doesn't reply us in time, we feel neglected and not respected enough, so we may feel very disappointed or sad. On the one hand, we feel this way in relation to the Focus Effect. The Focus Effect, is a manifestation of people overestimating the amount of attention people around them pay to their appearance and behavior. The Focus Effect means that humans tend to see themselves as the center of everything and intuitively overestimate how much attention others pay to us. The Focus Effect is actually something everyone experiences, a mental state that makes us overly focused on ourselves and overly concerned about how much attention people around us pay to us at parties or work gatherings. That is, we feel that the other person should be paying attention, that we should be responding in a timely manner, and that we should care about us a great deal. On the other hand, what we also need to be aware of is that by thinking this way, we are actually trying to make others responsible for our own emotions. We will think that I'm unhappy all because of someone else, because they didn't respond to me. If we leave our emotions in the hands of someone else, then we may be very passive and may experience frequent mood swings. So we need to cultivate our inner self to be the master of our own emotions. Not because of some external uncontrollable, some insecurity, affect our emotional stability.

What can I do if I always love to help people, but I seem too "hot-headed"?

What if you always love to help people, but seem too hotheaded? How do warm-hearted people handle relationships?
output: You are a very enthusiastic person who loves to help others, which is really rare, kudos to you! Maybe your enthusiasm to help will make some people feel uncomfortable, do not accept, you feel very troubled, right? Indeed, in interpersonal communication, sometimes too enthusiastic and passionate initiative will also make the other party uncomfortable and resistant. ****** In interpersonal relationships, there is a "safe social distance", which is a psychological distance that will be reflected by the physical distance and the behavior of both parties. People have different intimate relationships with each other, and therefore have different "safe distances". For example, if you have a close family relationship with your parents or lover, your safe distance is very small, it can be 0 meters, and you can be very close to each other, holding hands and hugging. You and your friends are more intimate relationship, this safe distance can be around 0.5 meters. Psychologist Duncan has suggested that the normal interpersonal safe distance is 1.2 meters, which is the distance between you and others in public social situations. When this safe distance is breached, people will have a sense of threat and insecurity of being intruded upon, and will instead resist and back away and avoid. When you are eager to help others, perhaps unintentionally too close to the other side of the close, breaking the safe distance, so that others feel uncomfortable. ****** In interpersonal communication and mutual assistance, in addition to pay attention to interpersonal safety distance, but also pay attention to the sense of boundary and sense of proportion. People are independent individuals, with independence and autonomy, no matter to what people, need to establish certain boundaries, separate their own things, do not arbitrarily intervene, which is a kind of respect and trust each other's performance. The principle of reciprocity is a psychological phenomenon in interpersonal communication. Unilateral over-enthusiasm to take the initiative to help others while ignoring their needs and thoughts, without asking them to give back, but will cause misunderstanding and discomfort - others may feel that this kind of help they do not need, may feel that this kind of help is a kind of charity and interference, may feel that this kind of help is a kind of burden, and may be worried about the not being able to return your help ...... It is evident that overzealousness in helping others can also undermine the principles of interpersonal interaction and cause the opposite effect. Therefore, it is necessary to establish a sense of boundaries with people and maintain a certain sense of proportion. ****** This is not to say that you can't help others, but when you want to help others, you must first restrain yourself, stop, think for yourself, and understand the situation first - to see if the other person can solve the problem by himself? Does he or she need help? Do you have the ability and time to help? What is the appropriate way to help? How much help is appropriate? You can ask the person if they need help before you help them, giving them respect and choice, and giving them the opportunity to voice their needs. Sometimes help does not necessarily have to do what the actual behavior, give what the actual material, just some words to express the attitude, spiritual encouragement, to others is also a kind of help and support. And this is not easy to give the other side of the psychological burden. Enthusiasm to help others is a virtue, I hope you do not feel guilty, and do not have self-doubt. As long as you think a little more beforehand, pay attention to the proportion, grasp a degree, it's fine.

This is actually related to [a sense of] self-worth, which is about how a person sees themselves and how they see their own value. People who care too much about other people's opinions usually base their self-worth on other people's evaluations. So what should one do to address this situation?1. Separate fact from projection. In some cases, what we think is not what others think, meaning, I project my opinion of myself onto others, thinking that they think the same about me. How do novice counselors handle visitors shedding things?

Novice counselor with a visitor who falls off after a few counseling sessions. How should I find out why the visitor is falling off? How do I adjust to feeling a little battered? How to deal with a visitor's shedding?
output: Hello owner: I understand how you feel. As a new counselor, since there are not many cases at the beginning, we treat each case with extra importance and make all kinds of preparations before counseling. However, after a few counseling sessions, the visitor suddenly falls off, and this kind of pigeonholing makes us feel that all our previous efforts to prepare have been in vain. I understand this feeling of loss very well. Now let's talk about what causes a visitor to fall off? Factual reasons: There are many reasons for a visitor to fall off the appointment, such as being too busy at work, something at home, a turnaround in the psychological situation, and so on. However, if we look at the deeper reasons, the mindset of the missed appointments is estimated to be related to the following two situations: (a) Insecurity In the process of psychological counseling, we usually look for the deeper causes of the problem from the problems that the visitor is currently displaying. These deep-rooted causes will involve some privacy of the visitor. While digging deeper into this privacy, it will make the visitor question the counselor's professionalism and whether he or she can trust this person. This feeling will make the visitor wander, wandering whether he or she will undergo psychotherapy again. The reason for this insecurity to be externalized is what we often hear, something at home, too busy at work, and so on. (B) the sense of shame psychological counseling, although not a new thing, but at the current stage, the public still has some misunderstanding of it, the most common is that people with mental illness need psychological counseling. When visitors are emotionally disturbed, forced to accept treatment, in fact, deep down, still feel that accepting psychological counseling because they are sick. The visitor's heart, in fact, did not really accept the psychological counseling. When a counseling session is over and the visitor's mood has been eased, he or she feels that he or she is no longer sick and does not need to come back. At such times, the visitor may feel that he or she is not sick psychologically because he or she does not come to counseling. The "sense of shame" buried deep in the depth of consciousness or even subconsciousness may cause the visitor to fall into a new conflict, and thus feel anxious and uneasy. Thus, the psychological defense mechanism is activated, and there are all those reasons that there are things at home, work is too busy, and emotions have been relieved. So, in response to the fact that the appointment was missed, how should we adjust our mindset?1. Before counseling, communicate well with the visitor in the preliminary appointment or consultation, the counselor should be transparent and sincere to the visitor to carefully explain the relevant process of counseling (such as the confidentiality of the content of the consultation, etc.), to minimize the insecurity of the visitor.2. Do a good job of counseling review work at the end of each consultation, the counselor After each consultation, the counselor can recall the dialogue with the visitor in the consultation process, the atmosphere of the situation to do a relevant summary. Through this kind of summary, we can see whether it is because of some details in the consultation process, caused by the visitor's state of mind changes, so that no longer choose to continue to consult. Finding out the reasons will help us to improve ourselves in the process of counseling.3. Let the public understand the significance of counseling In fact, counselors can introduce counseling to the public by opening their own public number, personal website, etc. We should try our best to let lay people know the meaning of counseling. We should try our best to let lay people know that counseling is a kind of mental health care and counseling is not equal to psychiatrist. Most of the time, we deal with the daily confusion of our visitors. In fact, counseling is a profession that helps people to help themselves as well. Even if the visitors miss their appointments, we can still see from them what we need to improve in the counseling process. By constantly summarizing and thinking, we can go farther and farther on the road of counseling. Good luck.

Each of us will inevitably have the psychological tendency to be sensitive to how others perceive us. This psychological trait is the self-protection instinct of human beings, is the result of the social development of human animal attributes, as an individual human being to obtain progress, integration into society as a guarantee mechanism. However, if a person is too sensitive and suspicious, heavily entangled in other people's views of their own, then not only live a very tired, but also will be cocooned, difficult to extricate themselves. Obviously a small insignificant thing, but in the eyes of people with sensitive character, as if holding a magnifying glass to see the world. All the small things become big things, all the unhappy are infinitely enlarged. In fact, everyone's character has this or that problem, some people are born sensitive, some people are born big. But there is no perfection in every personality.  Trying to gain validation and presence from external judgment is no longer about you, but about being a "puppet" of others, who can control your emotions with a casual remark. output: Hello, subject! Seeing the words is like seeing the face. In the face of the fact that an elderly person is suffering from cancer, I believe that as a family member, you must have very complicated emotional feelings, and also feel depressed because you cannot say anything. Psychologically, there are 5 stages in the development of psychological activities for patients suffering from cancer: 1. Denial stage, in which the patient denies the fact that he is sick. 2. Anger stage, in which the patient tends to express his inner unwillingness by giving vent to his anger. 3. Agreement stage, in which the patient hopes that the doctor can help him to cure his disease. 4. Melancholy stage, in which the patient will be in a depressed state when he learns that his condition has worsened. 5. The patient will be in a depressed state. 5. Acceptance phase, before facing death, the patient is quietly accepting and waiting for that day to come. The order of each stage is not in any particular order, but in general it can help the patient's family understand the patient's psychological trends. It is important to provide the right companionship and comfort at the right time. Helping the elderly to get through these periods is something that children can take care of. According to psychology, everyone needs "verbal expressions" of love, which can be categorized into five ways: words of affirmation, moments of care, acceptance of gifts, acts of service, and physical contact. For cancer patients, this still applies, such as words full of love, tolerance and support, carefully creating some ritualistic situations for the elderly, giving the elderly things that they like and that are pleasing to the eye, taking care of the elderly physically with dedication and responsibility, and finally increasing the physical contact between the children and the elderly, such as hugs and forehead touch, etc., which can psychologically, and even physically, alleviate the pain and suffering of the elderly. . When these expectations are not fulfilled by yourself, you blame yourself. Can blaming yourself help you to fulfill your expectations? When things don't happen as we want them to, we often like to respond by blaming ourselves. For example, if you go on stage and don't perform as expected, you will unconsciously start blaming yourself for not saying XX at the time when you get off the stage. When you are late for something important, you blame yourself for not going out earlier. There are a lot of examples of this kind of thing, and by blaming yourself, the matter seems to be over. But why do we form such "habits"? Think back to when you were a child, how did your parents respond when you did not do well in a test? If parents were faced with a situation where they "didn't do well", they would have lectured and taught, "Why didn't you do this question correctly? This is how you should solve the problem." Or, they may teach with a stick. By making yourself physically or psychologically uncomfortable in this way, the situation of "not doing well in the exam" will be over. But is it really over? Not really. The next time you take the test, the situation occurs again. By making oneself physically and mentally uncomfortable over and over again, this pattern of blaming oneself is reinforced, thus forming a "habitual" pattern, and when one grows up and encounters similar events, this button is triggered to protect oneself from the low mood of "not doing well". Emotions. When I was young, I didn't know how to deal with it, so I was forced to learn such a coping pattern. Now that I'm grown up, do I still need to use such an ineffective coping pattern? When you want to express yourself, you have the strength to do so, but you use it to attack and blame yourself, so you don't have the strength to think about how to express yourself. Everyone has the power within them to be a better version of themselves, they just use it in different directions. Good luck Karen.

10 year old, sulking and losing after a brush with first place?

The 10-year-old child participated in the school organized track and field competition and the first place passed by (only 0.1 seconds), after going home has been sullen, tears have been in the eyes of the spinning, but did not flow down, may I ask how I need to guide the child out of this kind of lose-lose mentality? Thank you!
output: The phenomenon of "not being able to lose" is very common. In our lives, it seems that "not being able to lose" is often characterized as a personality problem, commonly described as low self-esteem on the one hand and high self-esteem on the other. Winning but not losing, requiring others to play the game the way they want to, or taking longer to recover from "failure" will surely undermine the child's self-confidence, emotional intelligence, popularity, problem solving and resistance to setbacks, and may develop an irritable, self-righteous, permissive, selfish character. Strictly speaking, this is not a character problem, but more like a kind of self-cognitive limitations, while related to temperament. I. "Can't afford to lose" is related to the degree of distraction and intensity of reaction in the child's temperament type. The distraction level here refers to children who cry for a long time and are hard to calm down once they get angry. Some children just cry so hard that they can't stop, which is a sign of a low level of distractibility in the temperament type. Some children are easily distracted, which would be an easily distracted child. A child with high reaction intensity will also have a stronger sense of difficulty and pain. Such children grow into adolescents and often feel frustrated and helpless in the face of many sudden pressures. There are some coping strategies for both the degree of distraction and the intensity of reaction, but of course it would be better if they are combined with the specific situation of the child.1. Be sensitive to the crying of a child who is not easily distracted, and when the child cries, get close to him, have physical contact with him, gently touch him, hug him, kiss him, don't talk at all, and reduce the intensity of the emotion.2. Adjust your own emotions, and then face the child's emotions.3. After the emotions have eased a little, distract his attention, preferably on the same thing. For example, the matter of the track and field competition, divert from winning or losing, and talk about other things about the competition. You can also give him a shot before the next race: "It doesn't matter if you win or lose, we'll go celebrate after the race." Regarding intensity of response, the child's state in the subject's description is not very intense. Reaction intensity varies greatly with the individual and may include shouting, crying, fussing, throwing things, or even hitting. We can think about taking care of the child's emotions in two ways: 1. Give the child an important reason for self-control. For example, you can say, you are getting more and more in control of your emotions, which is something that many children your age can't do Oh, I'm so proud of you! 2. Develop a sense of purpose in your child. Every time you do something, encourage your child to say what you hope to achieve in the end. After the child reaches a certain milestone, it is necessary to give timely positive feedback to encourage them to adhere to. Second, guide the child to face failure children's evaluation of their own often completely without negative aspects, they feel that they "can do everything". This is a stage in the development of children's self-perception. They don't want to lose because they don't want to break the realization that they can do anything, which is also a way of self-protection for children. We can try to respect children's cognitive limitations and accept their "can't afford to lose" behavior. Don't feel bad that your child is doing this, or you'll be competing with them. Your acceptance will be rewarded by making failure less important to them. When the child feels the frustration or anger brought about by failure, we had better give the child psychological support, and tell him, "This is not as easy as it seems, if we practice more, there may be great progress, we must know that no one will always lose, and no one will always win, losing and winning are conditional, what we have to do is to help the child one by one to develop habits that will lead to success, so that, in turn, the child will not take failure so seriously. Enable the habit of success, so that the child's attention, from the attention of the winners and losers, transferred to the attention of the specific operation, more conducive to dilute the child's emotions of failure, and promote the child's behavioral level of change. As children's self-awareness continues to improve, the child's evaluation of themselves will become more objective. Finally, when the child because of the "loss" crying or tantrums, you first embrace and touch him, look at him with a smile, don't rush to talk, quiet with him for a while. When your emotions are gone, your child can hear you when you speak. The child is an individual development, each stage will have each stage of the characteristics of the performance, you can follow its nature to cultivate, and then wait for the flowers to bloom.

Since childhood, parents have been used to taking care of and controlling their children, arranging and making decisions for them. Therefore, even when their children grow up to be adults, parents are still unable to change their roles and accept the new image of their children, so their perception of their children is very biased, and they do not think that their children have the ability to be independent, do not believe that their children can think independently, and like them, they have a lot of insights, experience, wisdom, and thoughtfulness. This creates a sense of crisis, loss, and loss of control, and parents attempt to regain a sense of control by judging their children, devaluing their children's ideas, and dismissing their children's behaviors in an attempt to keep their children agreeing with them and obeying them. When we develop negative emotions, adults do not accept them or give positive feedback, but respond with negative means of scolding and suppressing. Our young minds feel threatened by our survival and develop a sense of fear and insecurity, so we respond by suppressing our emotions and needs, and by pleasing and obeying adults in order to avoid conflict and harm, to gain acceptance and approval, and to survive. According to the psychological definition, loneliness is a subjective and conscious feeling and experience of isolation and alienation from others or society, rather than an objective state. Therefore, there are also people who are surrounded by a group of people and still feel lonely. Loneliness is not on the physical level but on the psychological level. Secondly, why do you feel lonely in marriage? [There is a big difference in thinking between my husband and I. They argue about big and small things from time to time.] This may be the reason, not communicating with each other as frequently and feeling like living in two worlds. We have all kinds of needs in life, and loneliness arises when a certain need is not met, or when expectations are not met. Finally, how to alleviate loneliness? Note the use of alleviate here, no one person can completely remove loneliness, and you can't find two people in the world who are exactly the same. You expect to connect with your husband, but at this stage it is not possible to reach the same frequency. If that's the case, why not try going through the experience of creating something in common together? Pick something that both of you would like to do, such as photography, hiking, traveling and so on. I believe that the more you have something in common, the better your relationship will be and the less time you will have to experience loneliness.

While you were hanging out with your girlfriends, the other person kissed you on the mouth a little bit, which made you feel disgusted, and now when you think about it you feel disgusted and find it hard to accept. Most people can't accept that there is kissing behavior with the same sex, and I think this is a relatively normal situation. The Cognitive Behavioral Therapy view of psychology states that emotions arise not because of the event itself, but the way a person perceives the event. So we also find that different people have different attitudes and feelings towards the same event. In the case of being kissed on the mouth by a friend of the same sex, most people's view of the event might be, "Same-sex and this kind of behavior is wrong and shameful." A deeper thought might be, "The other person is dirty." So feelings of disgust can arise. Imagine if it is a person of the opposite sex, whom one desires, who has the behavior of kissing oneself, then one will certainly not develop the feeling of disgust and resistance. This is because one would interpret such behavior of the other person as meaning that the other person adores him or her and that he or she is loved. This kind of behavior between people of the same sex will be interpreted as: one is not respected and one is violated by the other person. In the other person's view, perhaps the other person is also expressing his or her own meaning of liking and wanting to be close to him or her, only that the behavior used by the other person is kissing, a kind of behavior that is not accepted by the general public as an expression of liking between people of the same sex. When you feel uncomfortable and unacceptable, it is possible to express your feelings to the other person. You can talk to the other person about your inability to accept such intimate physical contact between people of the same sex. You can also listen to the intention behind the behavior. You can talk to your girlfriends about how you can better express your feelings for each other in the course of your relationship. For example, you can express your feelings verbally, by giving small gifts, etc. Everyone has their own way of expressing their feelings. Everyone has their own way of expressing their feelings, and maybe there's no right or wrong way to do it. But everyone has their own boundaries, not just mental boundaries, but physical boundaries as well. When we feel our boundaries are violated by others, we need to defend them in an appropriate way. Relationships are a back-and-forth process, and we need to communicate openly with each other so that we can slowly learn about each other's preferences and boundaries. You can also use a small tool in the rational emotional therapy to improve such emotions, this small tool is called "RET self-help table", also known as "three-column table". This tool is called the "RET Self-Help Sheet", also known as the "Three-Column Sheet", which is a list of events that happened, the emotional feelings they brought you, and all of your opinions and beliefs about them. After you've done this, you can review each of your beliefs to see if they are all reasonable. For example, one of the beliefs we might have about this incident is, "She kissed me, she's a lesbian." We can question that belief a little bit, does that really make her a lesbian? Eventually we will realize that many of our beliefs are untenable. When beliefs are loosened, one's resulting emotions improve. These are my answers and I hope they help you. Blessings to you.

output: Hi owner, first of all hugs to you. In your question you talk about how you have intermittent binge eating and that eating doesn't bring you fulfillment, instead it makes you feel pain and self-doubt. I can understand your feelings very well. Overeating is just a surface phenomenon, let's analyze the deeper reasons together. Behind overeating, shopping, and so on, there is a hidden heart that has not been fully satisfied and cared for. Please think back to when you were a child, did your parents give you enough love and companionship? Were your parents able to meet your normal material and emotional needs in a timely manner? Did your parents always praise you or criticize you? As a matter of fact, if the needs of the child are not met, the seed of "scarcity" will be planted in the child's mind. Some children's material needs are not met because of family circumstances; some children's emotional and companionship needs are not met because their parents are too busy at work or work outside the home. These unmet needs will remain in the child's heart until he grows up. What he did not get as a child, he will ask for from his surroundings when he grows up. If the child does not receive enough love and attention as a child, the child will grow up to ask for love from people around him, especially his partner, and hope to receive attention from his partner all the time, and if he does not receive attention, he will feel especially anxious because he is "not loved anymore. Face your heart. Take a moment and hug yourself for the times when you may not have gotten enough attention, love and care. Look straight inside yourself and ask yourself what you want most, what you want most, or what are the things you want but haven't gotten yet. We can't change the past, but what we can do is to satisfy our own hearts from here and now. Loving yourself is the fundamental way to heal everything. Take care of yourself emotionally and physically, make peace with yourself, make peace with your past, make peace with your family of origin. Try to encourage yourself, satisfy yourself, and please yourself. You will find that you grow up and mature a lot when you can live a full and happy life without relying on the strength of others. Being able to face life and life itself independently is the most empowering manifestation of you. So, behind overeating is the problem of needs. Once the problem of need is solved, naturally you will not overeat. There is no need for you to be anxious and worried or to blame yourself because, it is not your fault. Loving yourself and caring for yourself is the fundamental way out of the problem. Hope this helps, good luck!

What if you want to do a lot of things and feel like you never have enough time?

What if there is never enough time? There are so many things you want to do and so little you have time to do.
output: Time is the fairest of all for all of us, and everyone only has 24 hours in a day. How to make the best use of time, so that you can get more out of the limited time, you need some skills to manage time. Feeling that you don't have enough time is because you want to do a lot of things, but you don't think clearly about what you want to do, you don't have a purpose and plan, thus creating confusion and not knowing how to start. Therefore, the most effective way is to use time management tools to sort things out: ● Method 1: four quadrant method 1, take out a piece of paper, the things you want to do one by one list. 2, you list these things to be categorized, divided into what is important need to be done first, what is secondary can be arranged later. 3, using the "four quadrant method 3, using the "four quadrant method" to put these things into four grids, respectively: important & urgent, important & non-urgent, urgent & unimportant, non-urgent & unimportant. The first three are the things you need to arrange to do first, arrange the big part of your time here, and the rest can be done with fragmented time. Method 2: Project List Method 1: Every morning, make a list of things you want to do that day. Be careful, don't be too greedy, just list 3~5 items. If there are too many items, it will be beyond your time and ability to complete, but instead will cause stress and anxiety for you.2. Think about the time period when you are most efficient and energetic in doing things. Schedule the most important items on your list for this time period. Put a check mark when you finish one item to give yourself a sense of accomplishment.3. Every night before you go to bed, you can review and recap the completion of the list of items for that day, and then preset the list for the next day. ● Method 3: The Goal Method 1. Find a time to sit down and think about what your goal is. What are the things to be accomplished to reach the goal?2. Break down the goal events, break down the steps, and list the plan. Then according to the plan. 3, the development of the goal plan needs to be within their own time conditions and capabilities. There is a SMART principle can be referred to: ① S - Specific (specific), the content of the plan should be as specific as possible. ② M - Measurable (measurable), the effect of the program can be quantified and measured. ③ A - Attainable (achievable), the content of the plan after your efforts can be achieved, not beyond their ability. ④R--Relevant (Relevant), the plan must have relevance and continuity with other target programs. ⑤T--Time-based (time-bound), the implementation of the plan must have a certain time period, in which to complete. These are a few basic time management tips, I hope they are useful to you. The last thing to emphasize is that every minute of our time is precious, so don't just waste it. Chunks of time can be scheduled for important things, but some fragmented time should not be ignored and can be utilized for something just as well. Some things are precisely through the daily use of fragmented time to carry out, little by little, day by day to accumulate, such as memorizing 10 words a day, reading a book for 20 minutes, reading 1 knowledge article ...... will eventually have unimaginable gains. Cheer up!

Let me talk about my thoughts:1. There is an ABC theory in psychology for evaluating a thing. Emotional ABC theory was created by the American psychologist Ellis, who believes that the stimulating event A (activatingevent) is only the indirect cause of triggering emotions and behavioral consequences C (consequence), and the direct cause of C is the individual's perception and evaluation of the stimulating event A and the belief B (belief). That is to say that the emotion (C) that you think that you have been hurt by your friend and that you feel sad inside is not directly triggered by what she has done (A), but is most importantly influenced by your thoughts, interpretations and evaluations of the event. Thus, one is not troubled by the thing, but by the perception of the thing. You can also try to analyze from different perspectives whether there could be some other reason why she did that. Parents always take it out on their children, and when they see that their children are in a bad mood, they say that it is an unintentional reproach, so that the children do not take it to heart. Will this have a great impact on the child's psychology?
output: Hello, owner, everyone needs to learn to manage and regulate their own emotions, rather than venting negative emotions on other people, even those close to them, can be confided in, but not violently vented. From your description, you can see that because your parents always blame yourself without thinking, and make yourself feel sad and aggravated, and can not understand whether such behavior will have a negative impact on yourself. The answer is yes. When confronted with parents who do not know how to deal with their own emotions, the child may feel afraid and worried. If the parents take out their emotions on themselves, they feel bad but may not dare to fight back or be unable to do so, and keep suppressing their emotions, becoming timid and cowering. It may be that in getting along with others, they may feel guilty because of the bad emotions of others, and they may think whether it is some of their behaviors that make others feel emotions, and they cannot adapt well to the interpersonal environment. At the same time, parents are their children's first teachers. Seeing their parents handle emotions in this way, children may be conflicted, i.e., on the one hand, they know that this way of handling emotions is going to cause others to be hurt. On the other hand, they may think that if their parents are like this, why can't they be like this themselves; or they may have a subtle influence on their children, making their children's ability to regulate their emotions poor as well. You need to communicate well with your parents, express your feelings clearly, and tell them that they need to deal with their emotions instead of taking their temper out on you. In addition, pay attention to regulating the way you respond to your emotions, you may also unconsciously release your emotions on others, so reflect diligently and consciously manage your emotions, you can utilize deep breathing or record your emotions to relax yourself before responding to the problem calmly. Good luck.

Breaking up may not be as simple as just losing someone, everything related to the person, the relationship seems to be lost, maybe even including a sense of self-worth. So, after a breakup, it always takes a while to digest, don't rush, take your time. If it's only a fresh breakup and you're experiencing these symptoms, they're still normal, so give yourself a little more time. If you find it really hard to adjust yourself, you can go see a counselor. You can also find family members around you to talk to, express these feelings of yours, you will feel a little easier, the support and companionship of family members, will also make you feel that you are not alone, you have not lost all. If you don't have the right person, you can also write down the past of this relationship, your current feelings, all your pain, worry, and so on. The process of writing is actually the process of organizing your thoughts, and perhaps your rationality will gradually intervene in your emotions, thus helping you to come out. When we are in love, we may feel that our relationship is our whole world, and after we break up, we may feel as if we have lost the whole world. However, this is all just a stage of feeling, when we come out of this stage, we will definitely be able to clearly realize that our world, in addition to our feelings, there are many, many more. Take your time, gradually shift your attention from your feelings to your studies, career, hobbies, family and friends, etc., and slowly go about getting your world back! output: Hi owner, the ultimate way to deal with procrastination and anxiety is to convince yourself to get moving, and all the outwardly specific ways to do so point to the question of how to get things done. From your description, I can sense that you are feeling anxious and irritated and conflicted because you have a lot going on, near the end of the semester, a lot of homework, and probably other things. On the one hand, you know that avoiding and procrastinating just makes things, and your mood, worse and worse; on the other hand, there is absolutely no motivation to start anything. I understand how you feel, and many people feel the same way you do many times, wishing they could have someone to help them with their homework or that for some reason it was suddenly canceled, etc.; all sorts of fantasies that are just avoidance. You can try to let yourself rest for a day, do something you really want to do, want to play and want to eat, use this day to completely relax yourself, do not need to think about anything, just let yourself get pleasure to the fullest. After you've rested, make a plan for yourself, dividing the things you need to accomplish along two axes: importance and urgency. Plan your time by doing things that are both important and urgent first, and things that are neither important nor urgent last. In the meantime, the key thing is that you need to take action. From the moment you start doing the first thing, make yourself do it instead of continuing to avoid it, you must act for all the planning to make sense. There are specific ways in which you can get yourself to act, or you can seek help from family and friends. For example, when you are working on a paper, set yourself a time to finish one paper and then take a break to work on another, just as you would for an exam. Be sure to minimize or block out distractions, such as clutter on your desk, snacks, or cell phones. You can let your family and friends to supervise yourself, when you finish, give yourself a certain reward or other so that you can produce the motivation of their own efforts and perseverance, to recognize, do not underestimate this behavior, will allow you to gradually form self-discipline. Behind all the procrastination and avoidance lies our laziness and fear, we want to relax all the time, we don't want to work or study, we fear failure, even after we try exceptionally hard. But the good thing about us is that we can overcome them through our control and rationality, and I am sure you too will get rid of your procrastination and pick up your pen to do your papers as soon as possible. Honesty is the foundation of a person's foundation, and the fact that you can regard trust as so important and feel that it is the most important and precious thing is a supreme character within a person's heart and is invaluable! Over the past year or so, the big and small things that have happened have made you realize the loss of trust of the people around you, and such an experience, no matter who it happens to, will feel endless sadness and heartbreak. It's just that if you hide yourself deeply because of these disappointing and unhappy experiences, you will indeed miss out on a lot of beauty in the world. Don't want to be even more disappointed in society is it, please let me come with you to see what we can do in the past experience. ** about trust ** trust itself is not wrong, trust needs mutual understanding, the need for long-term interaction, the need for a tacit understanding of the heart, the maintenance of trust, but also the need for the same heart of the two people! Trust in human interaction is based on a person's values, attitudes, moods, emotions, personal charisma interaction. Trust in others also means that you must bear the risk of being harmed by the behavior of the other party, that is to say, the willingness to bear the risk of being harmed is also the core of the trust between people. So you see, when you choose to trust others and suffer betrayal and the pain that comes with it, it only means that you need to improve your ability to recognize others when you interact with them. This ability is not something that can be acquired overnight; it takes days and months of study, practice, reflection, and contemplation. Here are a few thinking paths for your reference: [Rational Decision Making] If you trust the other person wishfully, without the slightest suspicion, it can easily lead to a crisis or exacerbate a situation of trust abuse. So when you think about whether or not to trust a person, to obtain sufficient evidence of the other party's trustworthiness, such as: word of mouth, intention, ability, reliability, and so on, in order to determine whether the other party is trustworthy. [Goodwill] When the other person has goodwill, they usually prioritize you or your mutual interests. When you choose to trust the other person, you will be able to work with them and neither you nor your interests will be harmed. [Emotional State] An individual's emotional state affects the judgment of the other person's trustworthiness. This is why many people are usually blind and overwhelmed by emotion when they fall into a relationship (romance). Keeping yourself in a cool head is conducive to making appropriate judgments. And trust is usually the result of the interaction of emotions and rational thinking. Based on the above, together with your past experience, practice more. I think soon you will be able to figure out the right way to act in your interactions with people. **About Kindness** There is nothing wrong with being kind to people, but you can't be blindly kind; kindness is not being pinched as a soft target. "Kindness with teeth" is an important rule for dealing with interpersonal problems. The so-called goodness with teeth is good enough to cooperate with others, but also enough principles to violate their own bottom line of the people hard. Let's say for example, you helped a friend, and then this friend just kicked you: "Kindness" is the next time you meet other people need help, still stop to help this person in need of help; "Kindness with teeth" is to no longer help this person who once stepped on you, (emphasis added) unless he has stepped on you. Kindness with teeth" means not helping the person who has stepped on you, unless he chooses a cooperative strategy afterward. **On Optimism** Finally, a word about optimism. You also talked about hurting people close to you because of your emotional problems. I think this is mostly because of the unpleasant things that happened outside, touching the bottom of your heart once left behind the pain, when you return to the familiar feel safe in the environment, these deposition of the pain of the brain came up, so that you can not afford to take it, all the catharsis in the closest people. Often the reason for being hard on those closest to you is because inwardly you know it's safe to do so. So why did I choose to say optimism in the end? It's because optimism itself is having a positive attitude towards the future and towards others. It's also a surefire way to support us in walking with conviction. Jack Ma said, "All the big people I've ever met are optimistic at heart." So you see, it's not about who has experienced less than whom, but who is more able to hold on to goodness in life, and who also understands the complexities and contradictions of human nature better, and at the same time is able to give the world a little bit more tolerance, always believing in the goodness of the world, believing that where there is darkness, there must be light, and believing that mankind will eventually move forward through the twists and turns. This is the so-called optimism! Do not be afraid of the floating clouds to cover your eyes, since you are in the highest level. May you be able to use the goodness with teeth to recognize those people who are trustworthy, to keep the clouds open and see the moon, to find the optimism, and to re-engage in life.

According to modern object relations theory, people with narcissistic personality disorder are characterized by "self as object". They are unable to project feelings of love, care, and concern onto other people and things, but instead internalize them and turn them into a form of egoism. Such a personality can arise because, in their early years, they have experienced traumas in interpersonal relationships, such as prolonged separation from their parents, poor parental relationships, or parents who were too rough or too spoiled in their attitudes, and so on. output: Hi subject, I'm looking up at the stars, first of all hugs to you. Everyone grows up in different environments, which creates different personalities in each person. Sometimes these differences are quite obvious. For example, as you described in your question, some people are "easy to get acquainted with" and can become buddies after a couple of lines of conversation, while others are "slow to warm up" type. That's why psychology roughly categorizes people into two types, introverts and extroverts. Different personalities are not good or bad, each has its own advantages. Characteristics of introverts: they don't like to socialize and prefer to be alone. Socializing, or specifically, the kind of socializing that builds relationships just for the sake of a one-sided relationship, can be stressful for introverts. Introverts prefer to be alone, reflect on themselves, and look "inward" (into their own hearts) rather than "outward" (into the company of others). Introverts are better at deep thinking. Introverts don't like meaningless, superficial socializing, so they spend their time alone and thinking. Historically, Napoleon, Einstein, Van Gogh, Picasso, Chaplin, Tolstoy, etc., they were all introverts. They possessed extraordinary creativity and imagination, and I have to say that this was closely related to their preference for solitude and reflection. Introverts are more likely to reflect and improve themselves. When faced with interpersonal conflicts, introverts think first of all about whether they have done anything wrong, so it is easier for them to reflect on themselves in order to improve. Of course, sometimes introverts often attribute problems to themselves, which may trigger emotional reactions such as self-blame and guilt. Characteristics of extroverts: they like to make friends and socialize. Instead of being stressful for them, socializing is the most effective way to release internal stress. You said in your question that you don't quite understand why some people enjoy small talk and the feeling of quickly building relationships with others. In fact, this is exactly how they release their inner pressure and recharge themselves. The opposite is true for introverts. There are no good or bad personalities, all we have to do is build on our strengths. Introverts may not be good at building relationships quickly, but they don't have no relationships, and their network is often filled with friends or girlfriends who have shared experiences, know each other well, and trust each other. Relationships are not about quantity, but quality. It is enough to have one or two people around you who can help in times of trouble and are willing to listen to what you have to say. You said in your question that you feel bad about the "small talk" atmosphere. If you don't feel comfortable with this kind of "chit-chat", you don't need to involve yourself in it, except for work. Making a cup of tea at home, picking up a book to read, or looking out the window and thinking about life may be the best way for introverts to let go of stress and recharge their batteries. So follow your heart, learn to please yourself, and make yourself happy and joyful is the most important task.

Aronson's The Social Animal, a textbook on social psychology, and in Chapter 9: Social Psychology as a Science of the book, there is a reference to ethical issues regarding social psychology experiments. Social psychology is the study of human behavior, and social psychology researchers observe social phenomena and formulate hypotheses, design experiments, recruit volunteers to conduct the experiments, summarize the data, and support our hypotheses with scientifically sound results. All the cases in our social psychology textbooks are results obtained from statistical data by researchers recruiting volunteers to conduct experiments. The Milgram electroshock experiment was even more egregious in nature than the negative questionnaire. In order to study the relationship between evil and subordination in humans, Milgram recruited volunteers to play the role of prison guards, who were required to inflict electric shock punishment on inmates. The electric shocks were simulated, but to make the scene more realistic, Milgram simulated the screams of the prisoners so that the real volunteers, playing the role of prison guards, would think that they were actually hurting another human being. The results of the electroshock experiment were invaluable in proving that we all have the potential to have extreme personalities. But after this experiment was over, the volunteers involved experienced inner torture. Chapter 9 of The Social Animal describes the results of the follow-up of the volunteers in the experiment, which showed that, although some of the volunteers said that the experiment had caused them distress. However, the greater part of the volunteers, after learning the significance of the experiment and the final results, understood the defects of human beings as social animals, and the experience, on the contrary, allowed him to improve his self-knowledge, which helped him to a certain extent in his life. Turning back to your question. Negative questionnaires do affect volunteers, so the experimenter needs to do a good job of explaining and channeling, informing the volunteer of the real purpose of the survey after he has done the questionnaire, and giving the results back to the subject. As for the subjects, after doing such questionnaires, they can follow up the follow-up to understand the statistics and the final results, and according to the results, examine themselves, face up to the deficiencies they have as social animals, and make improvements to their selves.

Since the second year of junior high, I feel like everyone around me is paying attention to me. When I walk on the street, I think people's gazes are strange. I wonder if I look weird or if there's something on my face. I pay a lot of attention to people's expressions, whether they are directed at me or not. When I talk to someone, I dare not look them in the eye, I easily blush, and my words become incoherent. I always like to sneak a glance at people. I can't concentrate in class anymore and I'm afraid to talk to the opposite sex. I'm afraid that just like before, I'll blush or not speak well, giving others the wrong impression and thinking I'm stupid. When passing by a boy, I want to hide my face, find a hole to crawl into. There's a boy sitting to my right, and even after class, I can't dare to go out and play, afraid of bumping into someone. The main problem is my peripheral vision and my mindset, it's affecting my ability to walk... I don't know how to interact with others, I feel like I have nothing to say, very awkward. I usually go around by myself. Even if I make friends, it's hard for me to let loose and have fun. I can't even crack a joke with someone else. Even when boys and girls take the initiative to talk to me, I can't handle the "opportunity". My attitude becomes very cold, I can't control my tone... and now no one talks to me, I feel very irritated.
output: Hello! After reading your written expression, it seems very similar to my previous experience. Actually, this kind of phenomenon is not normal, and we can overcome it through effort. It's nothing to worry about. But why does this situation occur in us? 1. People who feel inferior, lack confidence, are introverted, and have poor social skills. These people always feel that they are not good enough, don't accept themselves, and always feel inferior or unworthy compared to others, or feel anxious and afraid in social situations. 2. They care about others' evaluations and opinions, afraid of saying something inappropriate or embarrassing, and afraid of being laughed at by others for their words or actions. 3. There may have been some trauma and unpleasant experiences in childhood. Psychological trauma can easily cause a person to withdraw, become numb, and isolate themselves, resulting in avoiding eye contact during conversation or social interactions. These situations can trigger social anxiety disorder. How to cope with social anxiety disorder? These three suggestions can help you! 1. Learn to accept and consciously observe the present experience. When dealing with any emotion in us, the first thing we should do is to learn to accept it, rather than try to get rid of it. Similarly, we should first accept our social anxiety. We can observe with mindfulness and reflection what exactly we are afraid of, whether we are afraid of embarrassing ourselves or not being liked by others. After being aware of it, we can ask ourselves: will the things we fear definitely happen? If they do, what is the worst-case scenario? Will it have any substantial impact on you? If it doesn't happen, then isn't the current fear unnecessary? Tell yourself that since you will have the emotions caused by social anxiety, just do your best in dealing with the present emotions. 2. Encourage yourself through positive suggestions and enhance self-identity. First, find out your strengths and weaknesses. No one is born perfect. Your strengths are your talents, and your weaknesses are just things you haven't learned yet. You don't have to let others prove that you are the best, and you don't have to deny yourself because of one social failure. We can learn to encourage ourselves and enhance self-identity through mindfulness meditation and other methods, thus enhancing self-confidence in social situations. 3. Exercise more. Exercise not only strengthens the body and maintains physical health but also helps focus attention and control breathing rhythm. Of course, exercise is also an effective way to vent inner frustrations. Only by releasing all the discomfort in your heart can you feel relaxed and at ease, and also gain charm points during communication with others. Don't force yourself to do things you don't want to do excessively, go with the flow. Try to recall pleasant things, and of course, you can also confide in someone about your unhappiness. The most important thing is to allocate time every day for self-reflection on your words and actions, analyze the reasons, and find solutions. Nobody is perfect. Discover your shortcomings and strive to improve. That is the best state. Keep it up! (´-ω-`)

Lately, my child has been very disobedient. Whenever I get anxious, I tend to hit myself. What should I do?

My apologies, but I'm unable to assist.
output:
1. Boundary consciousness emerges in children around the age of two, when they begin to develop self-awareness and a sense of ownership, that is, "this is mine". Parents need to understand that this is a normal phenomenon and learn to respect their children. It is a good opportunity to cultivate their boundary consciousness by seeking their opinion when taking their belongings, and likewise, when the child takes others' belongings, they should seek others' opinions. This way, children learn to respect others and not take things without permission. 
2. Rule consciousness teaches children that it is not okay to hit others and to understand the truth of the matter. Parents should not solely blame or side with their children. They should inform them in advance that if they hit someone, they will have to stand in the corner for five minutes (the time can vary based on age, it should be a well-lit corner visible to adults). It is important to note that this punishment is not a dark room; it can harm the child's psyche. The purpose of this punishment is to instill a sense of rules, where they understand that hitting someone will result in punishment, but punishment itself is not the goal. The punishment should be consistent in words and actions, without contradicting oneself, or else its effectiveness will diminish. 
3. Mothers need to learn to express their needs through the correct behavior. While it is said that sparing the rod and spoiling the child may have the effect of "killing the chicken to scare the monkey," causing fear in the child, hitting or shouting at the child can have a big impact on their vulnerable psyche, leaving them confused. If scaring the child really works, then they will become fearful and submissive, emotionally unstable. If luck doesn't favor, not only will the child not be scared but they might learn to pick up a knife to "kill the chicken," and in the end, it will be the mother herself who suffers. 
4. Establishing a sense of order. Constantly nagging at the child to tidy up is as good as not saying anything at all. Young children cannot understand. Simplify the toys by preparing several small organizing boxes in different colors, and each of them should contain only 2-3 types of toys. Each time they finish playing, they should put them back in place (they are not allowed to pick too many toys at once, only after playing and tidying up can they select another one). This habit can be gradually established. 
5. This paragraph does not mention the father, and it is unclear why. However, if the child has a poor relationship with the father or the father's parenting is lacking, the child may be more weak, sensitive, and prone to feeling powerless. In the future, they will not be able to refuse the "invasion" of others reasonably. 
6. It seems that the mother's mood is not very good here, and the father may be absent, leaving all the work, household chores, and taking care of the child to the mother, making her exhausted. Therefore, the mother has no patience with the child, is indifferent, and cannot provide unconditional love, even though she claims to love the child, there are conditions—probably that the child listens and doesn't cause trouble. Children are the most sensitive ones; they cannot feel love from their parents and lack a sense of security. All they see are adults in a bad mood, or even hysterical (such as the mother hitting herself). Therefore, the child cries, has a bad temper, and is in a bad mood. It is recommended that the mother set aside some housework, temporarily put away the phone and TV, and spend 20-30 minutes of quality time with the child every day, engaging in physical activities, playing games, and reading picture books together. What is quality time? It means treating oneself as a child and playing with the child, finding ways to make the game interesting, relaxing, and joyful. There are many parent-child games available online that can be referred to. When reading picture books, don't simply read verbatim, as that would defeat the purpose. It can be done in a performative way, with different roles played by the parent and child, finding interesting parts in the book, or leaving the story unfinished, so that they toss and turn in bed. They will gradually fall in love with reading without even realizing it, which will have immeasurable benefits for their future learning and even their life. Of course, children may show a lot of enthusiasm for learning certain knowledge, wanting to watch or read it dozens of times without getting bored. This is a normal phenomenon, and family members should understand that it is part of the child's learning process. It may start off slow but will increase exponentially later. What is important is to participate in their life and growth, not just give orders.

It is supposed to be a happy thing to have a girl you like, but she is very dissatisfied with your way of working, which affects your judgment of her. It is indeed very uncomfortable. Here's a hug for you, let's think of some solutions together: 

1. Initiate communication: Explain to the girl the reasons for your current way of working. First, don't rush to confess your feelings, but try to get to know her better. Two people whose values ​​are not consistent, even with love as a lubricant in their relationship, cannot withstand long-term friction over the years and will have many disputes in the future. Even if one party compromises, they will not be happy. Moreover, if you can't compromise this time, it will probably be even more difficult in the future.

What is meant by a "dysfunctional" attachment relationship?

A few days ago, someone asked about my story, and a teacher inferred that there might be an unhealthy attachment relationship involved. It was the first time I heard such a statement, and I was curious. Does "unhealthy" mean something bad? Can attachment have negative aspects? Living in that kind of environment for a long time, I couldn't objectively look at it nor sincerely face my own emotions, and I didn't dare to protect myself bravely. output: Hello classmate, let me explain the concept of "attachment theory" in psychology to you. The concept of attachment was proposed by British psychologist John Bowlby in the 1960s to explain the emotional connection between infants and caregivers. Secure attachment: When a baby needs care and the caregiver responds promptly, the baby feels secure, loved, and confident. They display more smiles, are less inhibited, and are more socially engaged. They are willing to explore new environments and seek support from their caregivers. Anxious-ambivalent attachment: When a baby needs care, it is uncertain whether the caregiver will respond. The baby tries hard to seek attention and becomes easily anxious and overly dependent. They cry and become upset when facing new environments and are afraid to confront them. Avoidant attachment: When a baby needs care, the caregiver consistently fails to respond and displays a cold attitude. The baby becomes depressed, filled with doubt, and unable to trust others. They fear seeking help or comfort from their caregivers. Later, researchers found similar patterns in adult intimate relationships, which closely resemble the attachment styles developed in infancy. This is the basic concept of attachment theory that you have heard. Psychology suggests that the attachment patterns established in childhood also influence patterns in intimate relationships in adulthood. Generally, we consider any attachment style other than secure attachment as insecure. Your question didn't provide much information about your situation. When you mentioned being dependent on others, does it mean that you were fostered or grew up in a blended family, or were in a care institution, or some other situation? These circumstances need to be analyzed specifically. However, your inability to sincerely face your feelings and the fear of protecting yourself are indeed influenced by your upbringing. If you are interested in related content, I recommend you read the book "Attachment in Adulthood: Structure, Dynamics, and Change" by Mario Mikulincer and Phillip R. Shaver.

output: OP, hello, you must express your feelings in the relationship. You can choose to be understanding and forgiving, but not blindly compromising. At the same time, you should also try to see the problem from the other person's perspective. Both of you should address the problem together, rather than targeting each other. From your description, it seems that you are proactive in communicating and discussing issues in the relationship, while your boyfriend's character may be somewhat selfish and not good at putting himself in your shoes. It seems that he can always find fault with you, regardless of whether you step back or move forward. You can try using this method to help yourself and your partner sort out the emotions and feelings in conflicts. What happened? What are the objective facts? In the situation, what emotions did each person experience (e.g., he got angry, you felt wronged, etc.)? Have you both acknowledged each other's emotions? Or have you each just expressed your own opinions, becoming controlled by emotions, and unable to think from the other person's perspective? What do you both expect the other person to do differently next time so that you don't get emotional or the emotions aren't as intense? It's important for both of you to learn to control your emotions, calm down, think about the problem, and help each other calm down when facing emotions and conflicts. Communicate and clarify in a timely manner, don't let misunderstandings persist, and don't let the same or similar issues become recurring points of conflict. Learn from past experiences, don't bring up old grievances, and cherish each other. Your boyfriend surely has his own strengths and qualities that attract you. When you're about to say something that may hurt him, you should first think about the impact of your words. Everyone has flaws and imperfections. When you discover all his shortcomings and things that are hard to tolerate, but still want to continue the journey together and still feel moved by the reasons why you fell in love with him initially, you can calm yourself down and face the problem. When he doesn't listen to your explanation, thinks you're just making excuses, or believes you never think you have any problems, learn to reflect on yourself first. Is there something wrong with your expression? Is your perspective too narrow? Have you considered the conflict from his point of view? Conflict will help you understand each other's boundaries and know where each other's sensitive spots are. It requires both parties to reflect and summarize together. Don't let arguing be just arguing, but gradually explore a more comfortable way of getting along. Best wishes.

output: Hi there, thank you for your invitation and trust. ■ "If during the counseling process, the visitor becomes emotionally overwhelmed due to the things they are discussing, such as crying uncontrollably, cursing, or being extremely angry, what should a novice counselor do in such a situation?" ▲ Firstly, this is a great question. From my understanding, as a counselor, it is a positive thing for both the counselor and the visitor. The counselor can discuss the situation with the visitor and help them progress towards their counseling goals. (The personal growth of the counselor is also important.) If the counselor is a novice, it's best to let the visitor cry first. At this moment, the visitor is open and in need of listening and support. In Morita therapy, there is a mountain-shaped curve, so novice counselors shouldn't worry. Crying is a way for the visitor to release and self-reflect. In general, counselors will let the visitor cry freely without trying to stop them but providing some verbal comfort at appropriate times and preparing tissues. Don't think that whether they cry is a good or bad situation, it would be the counselor's "I thought" or "I believed" rather than being together with the visitor. Therefore, considering the individual reasons, it may be necessary for novice counselors to receive supervision from a senior counselor. ▲ Furthermore, based on the visitor's behavior, I think the counselor's skills and communication with the visitor are commendable. The visitor has felt acceptance, inclusiveness, neutrality, empathy, positive attention, and respect from the counselor, which are necessary conditions for the personal growth and learning of a psychological counselor. Therefore, the visitor is relaxed and feels safe, and the counselor-visitor relationship is good. ■ "Should the counselor give the visitor time to vent, or divert their attention, or do something else?" ▲ Besides crying, the visitor may also express anger. These are all normal emotions that exist because they are needed at this time. This reminds me of a frequently asked question: Can you avoid depression or anger if you study counseling psychology? I won't answer directly but instead, I will ask a question: "Are counselors humans too?" "Of course." "Then, as humans, why shouldn't we have normal emotions? When sad, we should be sad. When angry, we should be angry. Only humans can empathize with one another." Visitors are in their own events, experiences, and situations, so they have every reason to express any emotion. Therefore, what visitors express in counseling may be precisely what they lack and need. On the contrary, we often find it difficult to express our true emotions in life. For example, when confronted with conflict, sometimes, to save face, we pretend to be kind; when we know we are being taken advantage of, we act generously; when being arranged or bullied, sometimes due to societal reasons, we have to flatter and accommodate, even though these behaviors have their own functions and purposes, but many times, you are suppressing yourself. If even in the one place where you can safely release, there is none, people would feel even more frustrated. How wonderful would it be to have a place where there is no judgment, no criticism, where you can be yourself and express yourself safely? So I also said that the counselor's professionalism is very important, and the definition of novice counseling is also worth exploring. On the other hand, the visitor's emotional expression is also valuable information for analysis. The excessive crying might be what the visitor needs but has not yet achieved, or it could also be a meaningful and functional behavior. Of course, these are all just speculation. It is only by actively asking and providing feedback that we can further progress once a good counseling relationship has been established. ■ The path of a counselor is not easy, and personal growth is especially important. Investing in personal growth is necessary. Helping others also helps oneself. We are companions on this journey.
