output: Hello! In fact, staying up late is more like a kind of healing for young people. After experiencing exhaustion and anxiety during the day, lying in bed at home is the most relaxing time of the day. Whether it's browsing Weibo, watching dramas, or playing games, the feeling of being in control of your own time always keeps people addicted. Every person who stays up late actually has anxiety about tomorrow and fear of the future. In today's fast-paced life, most of our time is occupied by work, and we have very little time for ourselves. For us, nothing is more healing than quietly staying still and having a space for solitude. We all understand that staying up late is bad for our health, makes us look ugly, and affects our work the next day. But the pleasure that staying up late brings makes these things seem insignificant. Staying up late has become a normal thing for people nowadays. Before we know it, it's already eleven or twelve o'clock at night, and we only realize we should go to sleep, but we keep thinking of playing a little longer. The reasons for staying up late may be playing with our phones, using computers, reading books, or working overtime, etc. We just can't fall asleep, even if we want to. If possible, avoid using your phone before going to bed. In the half hour before you plan to sleep, stop playing with your phone, put it away from yourself, and take care of everything related to sleep, such as adjusting the air conditioning temperature, going to the bathroom, and washing up. Once you've taken care of everything, lie down on the bed, and try not to think about anything that happened during the day. Because this will make it even harder for you to fall asleep. Reading books at night is a good idea. Read a dozen pages or so and gain some knowledge. Gorky once said, "Books are the ladder of human progress." So, if you have time, try to read more books. Don't read novels because they will make you more engrossed. Read some classics, sometimes it will make you sleepy, and then you can go to bed. This way, you not only gain knowledge but also successfully bring the desire to sleep. Many people may have the habit of taking a nap, and then they find it difficult to fall asleep at night. So, it is best not to have the habit of taking a nap. No matter what you do psychologically, if you can't overcome it, then it's useless. So we should try our best to overcome our own psychology. Whatever we say, we should stick to it and not let the various psychological problems disturb our sleep. Finally, I hope you have no fear, no panic, and in every corner of the big city, in every quiet late night, you can still see hope and live a fulfilling life.

Always disgusted with one's gender, including one's own body. Will be very happy when someone says they look like a girl.
output: Dear friend, hello! Thank you for your trust, allowing me to see your inner confusion on this platform. I also value the opportunity to communicate with you and hope to be of help to you. [1. Why seek help?] You mentioned that you dislike your gender and wish to be perceived as a girl by others. It is everyone's right to dislike or like something. At first glance, it may seem simple to dislike something, and there doesn't appear to be any internal conflict that would cause you distress. Upon further reflection, there seems to be an internal conflict of wanting to be a girl, but in reality, you are physiologically male. This almost unchangeable physical structure has created obstacles for you to fulfill the "female" role, and perhaps your inner turmoil is caused by this, leading to feelings of hatred towards your own sexual organs. So, I would like to know what answers you expect to get through this inquiry? Why do you detest your male identity? Or, how can you adjust the feelings of hatred towards yourself? [2. Why detest your male identity?] Dear, do you know? There are many reasons for your confusion about your gender role. So, what are the reasons that make you more inclined to be a woman? I would like to attempt to explore this dilemma with you from the perspective of family relationships. Do your father's contributions to the family stand out? If your father is lazy, it may lead to a deep-rooted resentment towards males from within you. In this case, if your mother happens to exhibit many qualities that appeal to you, it is also understandable that you would prefer the female role. If your father is hardworking and works very diligently, and if your mother is a more dependent woman, it may lead to a sense of compassion towards males from within you, feeling that the pressure of being a male is too great, and it is easier to fulfill the responsibilities of being a female. Remember to make a comprehensive assessment, as both genders have their advantages and disadvantages. [3. How to adjust feelings of self-hatred] According to psychological research, children form their gender roles in two steps: the first step is distinguishing between males and females, and the second step is categorizing themselves into one of these groups. You are clear about the first step, but now you are having confusion in the second step. It seems that you are unsure which category to belong to. In response to this situation, you can approach it with a more relaxed mindset. You are currently at a critical period of forming gender identity, and many adolescents have similar concerns. It's not shameful to want to be a girl; it is your true feeling. The fact that you are aware of this confusion is already valuable. In regard to your aspiration for the female role, you can gain some insights from the second point, the causes, and examine the motivations behind your desire for the female role. Finding adjustment strategies based on the causes will be more effective. Understanding the causes can also lead you to further and more comprehensive exploration of the responsibilities and benefits associated with being male or female in society, allowing you to make your own choices. In the past, psychologists have assumed that masculinity and femininity exist on opposite ends of a single dimension. These rigid definitions of gender roles have limitations because they restrict male and female behavior. In modern theories, masculinity and femininity are considered independent dimensions of personality. Each of us has a gender identity. When an individual scores high in both masculine and feminine traits, this gender identity is referred to as androgynous. Under current pressures, androgynous individuals are actually more common, and compared to individuals who conform to traditional gender roles, they exhibit more flexibility and adaptability in their behavior. For example, androgynous males may display "masculine" characteristics such as resistance to pressure and having unique perspectives, as well as "feminine" traits such as actively engaging with a baby. This has led to the emergence of a range of gender roles such as "tomboys" and "nice guys" in different individuals. The above is my thinking on your concerns. I hope it can be helpful to you. If you have any further confusion, feel free to ask. Best wishes!

The online loan is now three months overdue, and I receive daily phone calls and text messages threatening and harassing me. If it weren't for the money I owe to my friend and the fear of debt collectors bothering my parents, I might have died a long time ago. Nowadays, every day is spent in anxiety and panic. I feel that life is not worth living, but I can't afford to die either. I feel like a walking dead, working overtime until late at night for a meager salary that is not enough to pay off my debts. It's too painful. When I walk on the road, I have the impulse to run into the middle of the street, and when I stand on a pedestrian overpass, I have the impulse to jump off. I feel like I can't hold on any longer.
output: Hello, I feel sorry for what you're going through. You are working hard and have a lot of courage, it's just that luck hasn't been on your side. I understand how stressed you must be, but you need to know that no matter how much debt you have, it doesn't compare to the value of your life. Your life is priceless. This difficulty you're facing is only temporary, as long as you keep going and keep repaying your loans, your days will definitely get better. I recommend you watch a movie that I believe will give you courage and strength to keep going. It's a classic movie based on a true story called "The Pursuit of Happyness". The protagonist also faced difficulties similar to yours. He used to sell medical equipment and invested all his savings in buying a lot of instruments. One day, he passed by a stock brokerage firm and saw people there seemingly successful and living the life he desired. Through his efforts, he got an internship opportunity, but it didn't pay a salary for six months, and after that, only one person would be kept on. He persisted and during this time he even slept with his son in a subway station restroom and sought help from a shelter. He went through many hardships, but in the end, he succeeded and became the only one who was kept on. I believe you are currently facing a similar situation to the protagonist, but you have to believe that this problem is temporary. As long as you don't give up, you will overcome this difficult situation sooner or later. Work hard, and if possible, take on part-time jobs to tackle the loans. I believe you can do it! Sending hugs to you, the world and I love you! (^_-).

How can we help children maintain their enthusiasm for learning as they continue to take online classes?

Given the current situation of the epidemic, online classes will continue for a period of time, and even exams that usually have a sense of ritual will be canceled. Children may encounter difficulties and have poor performance in online classes. How can we help them get through this stage of online learning?
output: I don't know what age group you are teaching. Let me share my teaching experience this semester first. I teach a professional design course for freshmen. Most of the time, we use audio and screen sharing to conduct online classes. I found it difficult to achieve the same process and effect as offline teaching. Especially for our design major, it is challenging to provide detailed one-on-one guidance and interaction. At this point, I remembered someone saying, "What makes a good teacher? A good teacher is someone who can make students feel like they are at the forefront in the shortest time possible." I think it is about enabling children to quickly gain a sense of self-efficacy and make them feel that they can do it. So, I adjusted the teaching goals and process, not strictly adhering to previous professional requirements, but constantly seeking and affirming the strengths of the students. For the issues they encountered, I encourage them to make improvements little by little and then acknowledge their progress. As a result, the students gave very positive evaluations at the end of the semester, and they presented better assignment results than previous years. Each of them saw their own progress in this teaching process and outcome. I cannot see them for most of the class time, and I know they are not always completely attentive, but they did make efforts to complete assignments and made progress, which is enough. In the end, they were very reluctant to leave and ended this semester of learning with affirmation of their profession and themselves. I think this is a satisfactory teaching process. As for the knowledge points that may have been overlooked, they do exist, but with self-efficacy, any knowledge and skills can be learned in the future. So, my advice is twofold: 1. Do not overly emphasize discipline. It's normal for children to be less attentive during online classes and not fully engage. I experienced this myself when holding online meetings. I cannot sit quietly and listen to the leader's speech, and I am constantly distracted doing other things. So how can we expect children to sit still all the time? Let's look at them with understanding. Of course, we can demand discipline, but we should not blame them. 2. Provide timely feedback to students so that they can see their own progress. Why can exams promote student learning? Because they provide feedback on learning activities. Why are games so appealing? Because games provide feedback within minutes or seconds, showing the consequences of your actions, whether you win or lose. This feedback continuously stimulates you to take the next action. Therefore, in online teaching, if every student can receive timely feedback, their motivation will be greatly enhanced. The reason why students enter a period of exhaustion during long hours of online teaching is that they do not receive feedback for a long time. It is challenging to stimulate students with only persistence, lectures, and requirements. The feedback we provide to students can be positive or negative. But try to let each student see their own progress. After all, if you can't move forward in a game, you won't want to play anymore. Allowing students to see their own progress and feel that they can do it is a more valuable asset than any knowledge, which can stimulate their current learning enthusiasm and facilitate their future learning.

Is it wrong for me to just want to be a smart person, playing the role of a good person?

I used to be the class leader in elementary school, but later I found out that many classmates did not accept me, but had no choice because of my abilities and academics. I also had the support of the homeroom teacher. Afterward, I was afraid of getting on the bad side of both the teachers and students, so I focused on studying and didn't run for class leader again. In high school, my confidence was shattered and I suffered from depression. In college, I didn't dare to run for class leader and chose to focus on cultural and sports activities instead. In the recent chorus competition, I often gave advice to the class leader, but I felt that her way of handling things seemed too dominant and caused dissatisfaction among many people. It reminded me of my past. I made suggestions behind the scenes and discussed the division of labor with her, even though it wasn't my responsibility and I wanted to distance myself from it. When classmates asked if I was afraid, I just said that it was what the class leader said, and I even advised them not to waste their efforts. But when someone asked me, I explained myself and made sure not to criticize the class leader. Am I a bad person? I just want to be a smart person, but I feel like I'm being a troublemaker. I didn't speak ill of the class leader, but if you ask me, I won't say it wasn't me. I just think that I have strong organizational abilities. After all, I was one of the top ten squad leaders in elementary school. Moreover, the chorus competition falls under the category of cultural and sports activities, which I'm supposed to handle. I just gave the responsibility to the class leader and took on the role of conductor myself. Am I a bad person?
output: Hello! I understand your concerns. You were a class monitor in elementary school and stood out, which caused some students to resent you. In high school, you lacked confidence. Now that you're in college, you didn't run for class monitor, but you're always willing to give advice to the monitor. However, you're too afraid to show your abilities and hide yourself. You want to be a good person and doubt if you are a bad person. Hugs to you, dear child. Each of us encounters various problems in the process of growing up. By seeking help here, you have given yourself the possibility to become a better version of yourself. You are currently at a crucial period of self-identity formation. Self-identity develops through interactions with peers because we need to identify our social roles, such as how we appear to friends or classmates. It is normal to have doubts. You both want to showcase your abilities and fear drawing dissatisfaction from classmates. Acting differently in front of classmates and the class monitor makes you wonder if you are a bad person. Children who cannot obtain sufficient self-identity often dwell on past grievances, but in fact, our past experiences are meant to surpass them. The more a person understands how their early years were limited, the less constrained they are by those experiences. You may have fallen behind later, leading to a lack of self-confidence. As we grow up, we realize that we can gradually take responsibility for ourselves and accept contradictions and imperfections. There is no need to strive for perfection or for everyone to like us. The key is to learn to like ourselves, firmly believe that we are good people, willing to contribute to the class with a good heart. You are a young person of the new era and you want to live as yourself. You can try to find things that interest you and constantly practice. Also, learn to develop a strong sense of self, self-reliance, and dare to express your opinions bravely. See what changes occur. In this process, try to separate others' desires from your own and discover your strengths, such as your organizational and communication skills. Develop a sense of competence from small things. Competence represents our sense of value, feeling capable of achieving what we want when faced with difficulties and challenges in life, and feeling confident and happy. For example, being the conductor of a choir is great! I always admired our conductor when I was in school. Now let me share with you about the issue of people-pleasing. In our cultural background, we have been instilled with various concepts of "pleasing others" since childhood, such as "being a likable child will make you more popular." So I often use social networking apps to meet new people, but most of them are just one-time encounters and not long-lasting. And recently, the pandemic has worsened, and I have to stay indoors. I live alone, so the feeling of loneliness becomes even stronger. When I see others posting on social media, like having friends over for dinner or going on trips, I feel really envious. I start wondering why no one invites me, why do I have to actively ask others to do things with me. Sometimes, I just feel tired, lost, and I don't have many channels to make friends... I read some advice telling me to find something I enjoy doing, but even when I do, these problems still come to mind and it's really frustrating. What should I do?
output: Hello there, classmate. Regardless of which stage of life we are in, we must face and understand the meaning of "loneliness" as a topic for personal growth. Loneliness is not entirely negative or scary. When we no longer reject or fear it, and choose to enjoy loneliness, it can bring surprises. It may help us see ourselves more clearly, or inspire creativity, or make it easier to understand the lessons of growth. Furthermore, the existence of loneliness does not disappear just because we have friends. I hope you understand that. "I am an international student studying abroad. It may be that there were some issues with my socializing methods before, and I feel that there aren't many people I can meet up with and hang out together, maybe one or two at most." What I am even more curious about is what you mean by "issues with socializing methods". In fact, maintaining interpersonal relationships can sometimes be simple and sometimes complex. It depends not only on whether personalities, upbringing, and values align, but also on whether both parties have the same level of commitment to maintaining the relationship and whether they can accept the costs of maintaining it. In terms of your circle of international students, most cities have channels for Chinese students to meet and organize gatherings and activities. So, if you really want to have friends, you can also proactively make friends through these channels. You have one or two companions, but no one to share your innermost thoughts with. I suggest you think about what is preventing you from establishing deeper connections with others. "So I often use social networking apps to meet new people, but most of the time, it's just one-time encounters, and it's not long-lasting. And recently, the pandemic has worsened, and I have to stay in my room. I live alone, so the feeling of loneliness has become even stronger. When I see others posting on their social media, hanging out with their friends or going on trips, I feel envious and wonder why no one invites me or why I have to ask around to find someone to do something together. Sometimes I feel tired and lost, and I don't have many avenues to make friends." The reason why the people you meet through social networking apps are not long-lasting is because neither party has the intention to continue the relationship. In other words, your desire for friends may not be as strong and urgent as you imagine. This is something you need to think about. You envy the friendships of others and want to passively receive the kindness of friends. But have you realized that every relationship requires effort and maintenance? When you see others with companionship, it's because both parties have sacrificed their own boundaries to maintain that relationship. Perhaps they have sacrificed their time, energy, or money. If these sacrifices are inevitable in any interpersonal relationship, would you still choose to make friends? You can ask yourself that question. You mentioned that you need someone to accompany you in doing things, but you should also recognize your own abilities. In life, 90% of things can be done independently, and in case it's not possible, businesses now have amazing customer service. Many needs can be met just by speaking up, and there are plenty of people who can help. Of course, what I want to express is not a rejection of making friends but to tell you that you have great potential within yourself and there is plenty of support in society. You don't have to be overly anxious just because you don't have friends and let it affect your self-worth. Interpersonal relationships are indeed important, but they are not the most important thing. Having companionship can enhance happiness, but every thing has its pros and cons. Maintaining relationships comes with its own troubles, and so does loneliness. It's hard to say which is better. Which one do you think is better? "I see suggestions about finding things I enjoy doing, but even when I do those things, I still think about these problems and it bothers me. What should I do?" You have things you enjoy doing, but even when you do them, you are not fully focused because you are bothered by "not having friends". What is the root cause of this bother? Is it because I don't have friends, so I am not as good as others? Or is it that I don't have friends, so it must be my own fault, and I am just incompetent? Do you truly want friends, or do you simply not want to face life's challenges alone? I hope you can think it through. Loneliness is a constant in everyone's life. Sometimes it's internal loneliness, sometimes it's a lack of people around us. Acknowledging it is the first step, and embracing rather than fighting it is the second step. By embracing loneliness, we can receive its gifts and feel more fulfilled internally. Keep going! Best wishes~.

In most cases, being overly concerned about what others think is a manifestation of lack of self-confidence and insecurity. Therefore, I have summarized some methods to help you alleviate the current situation: (1) Learn to shift your focus by developing your interests, engaging in physical activities, or reading books, among other things. (2) Confide in close friends or family members who you have a good relationship with and express your concerns, which can help you release your emotions. (3) Try to reasonably filter out opinions that do not align with your own. For opinions that are useful to you, consider making changes, but do not put too much pressure on yourself during this process. (4) Objectively recognize your strengths and weaknesses. Embrace your strengths and develop plans to improve on your weaknesses, as nobody is perfect in this world. (5) Practice positive self-affirmation, and try to approach situations with a positive and optimistic mindset. (6) Accumulate knowledge and experience to enhance your reservoir of knowledge. This way, the degree to which others can influence you will greatly decrease. (7) Establish boundaries between yourself and others. When someone's emotions affect you, remind yourself that it is their emotions, and while you can offer help and comfort, resolving their emotions primarily depends on them. You are not responsible for other people's emotions. When we can distinguish between our own emotions and those of others, we can reduce unnecessary emotional exhaustion. The world and I love you. Since I was very young, I have always wished for my mother to become pregnant... Is this a sickness?

I probably had such thoughts when I was in third or fourth grade, and I still have them now. I want to have a baby with my mom through AI... I don't know if anyone else has such thoughts, or if it's just me being ill.
output: Hello there~ In psychoanalysis, there is a very important concept called the Oedipus complex, also known as the love for the mother. It originates from the Greek mythological character Oedipus, who accidentally killed his father and married his mother. Your current psychological state can be explained using this story. The Oedipus complex originally refers to the mixed emotions of a boy's affection for his mother and resentment towards his father. According to the ancient Greek myth, Prince Oedipus unintentionally killed his biological father and married his mother due to a prophecy. Freud used this to illustrate the characteristics of children's sexual psychology. He believed that during the phallic stage (around 3-5 years old), boys develop feelings of love for their mother and jealousy towards their father, as they subconsciously desire to replace their father and have exclusive love from their mother. However, because the father is more powerful and stronger than the child, the child tends to identify with the father and imitate his behavior and attitude. This impulse may still arise during adolescence, and it is only resolved when the individual finds a sexual partner. Freud believed that boys have a fear of castration from their fathers, which gradually eliminates the Oedipus complex. For girls, the development of the Electra complex signifies a shift of love objects from the mother to the father, and this complex reaches its peak when girls become aware of their lack of a "phallus". If not resolved effectively, this complex can become the root of future neuroses. The essence of the Oedipus complex is not actual matricide and patricide, but rather similarity and complementarity. Taking boys as an example, they are of the same sex as their fathers, so they are similar; similarity leads to identification, and boys look up to their fathers as role models and adopt their psychological traits and qualities as part of their own. Boys are of the opposite sex as their mothers, which allows them to complement each other, rely on each other, and this is what love is. Therefore, boys form the most fundamental interpersonal relationship with their parents, which can be summarized as love for the mother and imitation of the father. Love for the mother and imitation of the father often mutually reinforce each other. When the father loves the mother, boys imitate the father, and they will love the mother even more. When the mother loves the father, boys must become more like the father in order to win the mother's affection. Freud believed that "children often take their mothers or fathers as their sexual objects, and fathers love their daughters more than their sons, while mothers love their sons more than their daughters. Children respond accordingly, sons wanting to occupy the father's position, and daughters wanting to occupy the mother's position. The pleasure derived from these parent-child relationships and the relationships between children also carry a sense of both tenderness and hostility." If you are experiencing this situation, it may be because the Oedipus complex has not been resolved. You can read some relevant books to understand this complex, or you can consult a professional psychoanalytic counselor who can help you change your feelings towards your mother and transfer this emotional attachment to other females. This is my analysis and suggestion, hope it helps you! Best wishes!

output: Hello, you just broke up yesterday and now you're feeling very sad. This is a normal reaction. However, you have to know that this state won't last forever. I have encountered many people who have gone through a breakup, and in the initial stages, they might feel just like you, sad and even contemplating suicide, thinking that they will never love again, and exhibiting all kinds of extreme reactions. They will be grateful for their perseverance at that time. I believe you will also be the same. Don't rush, give yourself some time. Allow yourself to feel sad. When you feel uncomfortable, cry, talk about it, write it down, or even shout it out, but do not give up on yourself in a moment of impulsiveness. You miss your grandmother a lot, but have you ever thought that if there really is heaven after death, would your grandmother want you to join her there? Can expressing love through sexual intimacy be a way to fulfill sexual needs?

Feeling satisfied with sexual needs, there is an element of love in sex, just like satisfying the needs of eating and drinking. From this perspective, it is a form of care. However, if satisfying sexual needs and expressing love through sex can also create a sense of confusion.
output: Hello, I'm glad to discuss the topic of sex and love with you. I believe that as someone who has thought about this topic, you must understand the importance of sex in romantic relationships. This is a great progress. So, I would like to share my understanding with you. "Sexual needs are inherent basic needs for everyone." In Maslow's hierarchy of needs theory, physiological needs serve as the foundation of the pyramid, and sexual needs are an important component of these physiological needs. Therefore, sexual needs are actually mutual states of satisfaction. In intimate relationships, sexual love is about meeting each other's inner needs, rather than one-sided satisfaction. Of course, everyone's needs may vary, with some having more needs and some having relatively fewer. Therefore, it is important for both parties to adjust and satisfy each other's needs to find a balance. Thus, mutual fulfillment of sexual needs does involve elements of care. "Subjective experience takes priority in sexual love, with appropriate attention to the partner's feelings." In your question, you mentioned feeling "confused" about expressing love through sex. What is the cause of this confusion? Is it because expressing love through sex makes you feel ashamed? Regardless of the reason, sex should be considered a right and a way to obtain inner pleasure. As we discussed earlier, sexual needs are basic needs for everyone, so sexual love should be viewed as a basic right for everyone. Therefore, caring in sexual love or satisfying sexual needs should not be done solely to please the other person, but rather as an opportunity for oneself to be the subject in sexual love and to boldly enjoy it. If we view sex as a way to satisfy and please the other person, we are actually suppressing and depriving ourselves of our sexual rights, making ourselves passive participants in sexual relationships. In the long run, this can lead to feelings of shame and discomfort. Such an attitude is extremely harmful to intimate relationships. On the surface, it may seem like we are satisfying the other person's sexual needs, but this suppression and compromise of our own feelings will gradually build up inside us and eventually cause problems in the relationship. "Become aware of the underlying intention behind the deliberate satisfaction." From what we discussed above, it seems that there is a cognitive perspective of "deliberate satisfaction" behind this type of behavior. How did this perspective develop? It may be related to the beliefs you acquired from your upbringing, but from a broader perspective, our society's past concept of "male superiority and female inferiority" seems to deliberately diminish women's feelings and rights in sex, thus making it easy for women to develop subconscious beliefs of "I should satisfy my partner more in sex". This subconscious belief can turn women into mere accessories in sexual relationships without their realizing it. This belief actually also harms men's positive experiences in sexual life, leading to a situation of "both parties suffer losses." I hope the above response is helpful to you.

output: Hello there! Hugs to you! @First of all, have you carefully observed your own description and feelings? "I thought that if I achieved success, my family would be happy." "I feel disappointed, as no one is truly happy for me." ○ You need to realize that your so-called success is for yourself. Since childhood, we have been taught that parents are the ones who wholeheartedly love us, who worry about our pain and rejoice in our success. From childhood to adulthood, teachers, parents, and society have instilled in us the belief that good deeds are rewarded and bad deeds are punished. However, we gradually come to realize that parents' love for us is not entirely pure; after all, they are also individual beings who love themselves. The one who should feel happy for your success should be yourself. Perhaps you should understand that what you have accomplished is not to gain rewards, but to fulfill a personal life goal. ○ As for not receiving a positive response, when you focus on your own feelings, you won't care whether others' feedback is good or bad, and you will still be happy! It is good if you can bring joy to others, you can see it as a gift you give to the people around you, but it should not be used as a judgment of whether you have done well or not. We are not other people, we cannot understand their feelings. Maybe they are currently going through something troubling, and that's why they cannot be happy. Or maybe there are other reasons. Try your best not to assume that it is because they dislike you, as many misunderstandings arise from this. ○ Dear friend, never say, "No one is truly happy for me." That's such a worrying and absolute statement. You need to accept yourself and believe that people are not that fragile; even when you don't receive the kind of love you need, you still have the ability to love yourself. @Everyone expresses love in different ways, and I don't know how you found out about your parents' separation without divorce. The protagonist, in order not to lose his parents' love, keeps making wrong choices, thinking that if he becomes wealthy, his mother won't leave his destitute father. A freshman girl often has a desire to date, but doesn't know where to start.

Freshman girls, I used to get nervous and shy when talking to boys in high school. In college, every time I take a walk on campus, I see couples everywhere, and my roommates are also still single, talking about getting into relationships. I've also made friends with some guys, but whenever I talk to them, my mind goes blank. I really want to be in a relationship, but no one is pursuing me, and there isn't anyone I particularly like either. I also feel like my views on love are too simplistic. Today, I quietly like one guy, and then after a while, I start liking another guy. Sometimes, even after just a short interaction, not knowing much about the other person, I might just chat with them for a bit and develop feelings for them.
output: Hello! First of all, I would like to thank you for asking such a great question! I think many single girls have the same concerns as you. Actually, I am in the same boat as you and have been waiting for my own love story! I'm not afraid to admit that I'm already 27 years old and still searching! And I'm perpetually single, haha! I don't have any dating experience to teach you, but I would like to share my feelings with you! In fact, I used to be just like you, eager to be in a relationship but never had any guys chasing after me. I didn't have anyone I particularly liked, felt like anyone would do but also didn't want to settle. Although my standards for choosing friends were not high, there were always certain factors holding me back from taking the first step! Often, even before a relationship started, I already had an idea of how it would end. This reveals the contradiction in psychology known as avoidant conflict, where the same thing or person has both what you desire and what you fear. This contradiction is like two evenly matched little people in your heart playing tug-of-war, neither willing to give in, just stalling. Because I study psychology myself, I took some questionnaires and read some books to explore myself. Later, I found the reasons behind this state: (1) I haven't developed a mature view of love and have a limited understanding of intimate relationships. (2) A lack of security within myself and a fear of stepping out of my comfort zone. (3) Always predicting outcomes, fearing hurt and unable to handle losing. (4) Lack of self-confidence. Because I am an ordinary looking girl with average height, I have always felt insecure about my appearance. The above is my analysis of myself, and once I knew the reasons, I started making changes! The first and third reasons are relatively easy to solve and can be changed gradually through reading. The difficult ones are 2 and 4. Developing security and self-confidence don't happen overnight, so when faced with these reasons, I set a three-year goal for myself. In these three years, I started focusing on my inner self, reading many books on psychology, such as "Intimate Relationships" trilogy, "Marriage Psychology," "Why Love Hurts," "The Heidi Chronicles," and others. Through reading, you will understand different types of intimate relationships and the problems that arise in them. You will gradually form your own view of love and find the right way to love for yourself. Apart from reading, I also observe the interaction patterns of couples in real life. I used to think that in a relationship, two people should always present their best sides to each other, but later I slowly discovered that two people in love actually give each other their true selves. Love is not as perfect as imagined, love is about acceptance, understanding, and being there for each other! Realizing this, I found that I am not as insecure anymore. In fact, I am quite cute, at least some guys have complimented my eyes! Thinking about this, I am not so insecure anymore! When a person overcomes their insecurities and builds self-confidence, they will find a sense of security! I used to think that security should be given by the man, but now I understand that in any relationship, only when both individuals have a complete sense of self, will there be a sense of security! Although I haven't entered a romantic relationship yet, I have already stepped out of my comfort zone, and I now have some great male friends around me that I can freely communicate with! And, there are people who have started liking me! I think that is the change brought by self-confidence! So, my advice to you is to also try self-exploration, find the reasons, face them, and I believe that deep down, every girl has a beautiful and confident angel, believe in yourself, make changes, step out of your comfort zone, and you will definitely meet your destined partner! That's my sharing and advice, I hope it helps you! Keep it up, young girl!

Female college senior, attributes success to external factors and failure to internal factors, how to change?

As mentioned above, when I achieve good results, I tend to attribute it to luck, the simplicity of the questions, or the lack of competition. However, when I fail, I tend to believe it is because of my own lack of ability. I am currently feeling very unhappy and have low self-esteem. How can I change this?
output:
Hello, I think you are a person who is very self-aware and seeks personal growth and self-improvement. Your question resonates with my state of mind during my junior and senior high school years, and at that time, I firmly believed that this kind of thinking was correct. I remember one time when I did well on a test, the teacher asked me to share my experience on stage. I said, "This time was just luck, maybe I'll do poorly next time." The teacher was very angry after hearing this. In fact, you are much better off than I was at that time because I never doubted that my belief was wrong and never had the idea of wanting to change. Since you mentioned internal and external attributions, let me talk to you about Weiner's attribution theory: Weiner's theory consists of three dimensions and four factors. The three dimensions are: locus of control (internal attribution + external attribution), controllability (controllable + uncontrollable), and stability (stable + unstable). The four factors are: 
- Ability - stable internal attribution
- Effort - unstable internal attribution (controllable)
- Task difficulty - stable external attribution (uncontrollable)
- Luck - unstable external attribution (uncontrollable)
When there is success, attributing it to internal factors generates a sense of pride and increases motivation, while attributing it to external factors creates a sense of luck and reduces the feeling of success. Attributing failure to internal factors leads to guilt, while attributing it to external factors leads to anger. Attributing success to stable factors generates a sense of pride, while attributing it to unstable factors creates a sense of luck. Attributing failure to stable factors leads to despair, while attributing it to unstable factors leads to anger. Attributing success to controllable factors motivates further effort, while attributing it to uncontrollable factors does not generate much motivation. Attributing failure to controllable factors leads to continued effort, while attributing it to uncontrollable factors leads to despair. I think a good attribution style can enhance self-efficacy and increase motivation, creating a positive psychological state for future learning and life. Of course, this does not mean that success should be attributed to internal factors and failure to external factors. I believe it is more important to focus on the controllable components, as individuals have different attitudes towards ability, which can be divided into a growth mindset and a fixed mindset. Having a fixed mindset is more conducive to personal development. Analyzing the psychology behind attributing success to external factors and failure to internal factors: 
1. Early education and environmental influence with immature educational concepts, promoting modesty and suppressing pride and self-confidence, have a significant impact on current attribution styles. Moreover, your current attribution style may be reinforced and supported by people around you.
2. It is essentially due to self-doubt and the belief that one is not good enough. Although you did not specify the specific internal and external factors, I believe you see both internal and external factors as stable, unchangeable, and uncontrollable.
3. Maintaining self-worth and self-esteem. When success is attributed to internal factors, the underlying psychological belief may be that because it is an internal factor, I should succeed next time as well, otherwise others will mock me and I will perceive myself as lacking ability. Therefore, I believe that my success is accidental, so even if I fail next time, it will not affect my sense of self-worth. When failure is attributed to internal factors, the underlying psychology may be that because my ability itself is not good enough, that's why I failed. If it were due to lack of effort, it would be a moral judgment, while lack of intelligence is not. Alternatively, it could be because I didn't put in enough effort that I failed, and if I make an effort, I will surely succeed, rather than believing it's because I lack ability. The specific reason may vary from person to person and may require further exploration on your part. As for how to change, firstly, you can learn about various attribution theories, as well as self-efficacy and the growth mindset, through the internet or professional books. Then, have a clear understanding of your current state. Secondly, accept yourself in this state instead of blaming or excluding yourself. Then, reflect on the benefits you have gained from your current attribution style, which are the underlying psychological motives that lead you to continue using this kind of attribution. Finally, believe that you can make a change, and believe in your own courage to withstand the discomfort or pain that change may bring. In other words, you can reattribute past experiences and consciously attribute future events. Of course, it will be uncomfortable and you may struggle at first, but don't doubt yourself. What matters is not how many times you fall, but how many times you get back up. What matters is not where you are, but the direction you are heading in.

My sister has a conflict with our family and she came to me to talk about it. How can I help her?

I have a sister who is only 26 years old. Maybe she went back to our hometown to work. Our parents think she is getting old and they are extremely worried. They always bring up the topic of why she doesn't have a boyfriend or why she hasn't found a partner yet. My sister feels a lot of pressure every day and doesn't even want to go home on weekends. She currently has a car, a house, and a stable income in Leshan. She has her own hobbies and friends she can confide in. Maybe she occasionally feels lonely, but she never sees herself as pitiful. However, people around her always look at her with a pitiful gaze and constantly backbite about her in front of her parents. Her relationship with our parents has become confrontational right after they meet, and she also rejects meeting them. She even feels that life is too exhausting. She wants to tell our parents that she is fine and they don't need to worry, but every time it ends up in an argument. My sister asked me how she should communicate with our parents, but I haven't experienced these things yet so I don't know what to do. How can I comfort her?
output: There are significant differences in mindset and priorities between the older generation and our younger generation. The older generation's starting point is to hope that their children can have a stable and happy life with a family. In their mindset, getting married and having children early is the key to a stable and happy life. Your sister, as a young person, has her own career and life, her own aspirations, and her own views on marriage, which naturally differ from those of the older generation. It is common for the two generations to experience differences and conflicts, and it is difficult to reconcile them immediately. Therefore, both sides should start from their own perspectives. If they approach the conversation with the intention of persuading or refuting the other person, or trying to change their perspective, it will inevitably lead to arguments, conflicts, and ultimately, no one can convince the other. However, from both sides' standpoint, they both want their children to have a better life. It's just that the definition of "better" is different for the older generation and the younger generation. Therefore, both sides should not have an antagonistic identity and state, but should seek mutual understanding, accommodate differences, find consensus in the midst of disagreements, and adapt to each other's personality and psychological state for coordination. Firstly, let go of the intention to refute and persuade the other person's thoughts because this kind of argument leads to no results and it is difficult to have a positive outcome. As children, on the basis of understanding the good intentions of the older generation, it would be worthwhile to take a step back and show good manners and language that harmonize with the older generation's intentions. In simple terms, the older generation is like children; sometimes they also need to be "pacified." Because, at this time, the older generation is not trying to immediately make the child take action or get married and have children, it is just a habitual behavior to nag a few words when they see their child, expressing their worries and concerns. At the same time, they may feel a bit embarrassed due to idle gossip, so they unconsciously shift the conflict and hope to save face. As children, we can understand the behavior of our parents. At this time, there is no need to aggressively refute or argue face-to-face. Instead, you should learn to make appropriate concessions and show vulnerability in front of your parents, expressing an attitude of accepting their opinions, and also expressing that you accept their concern. This kind of empathy can give parents a sense of comfort. Then, you can shift the topic appropriately, and maybe they will forget to continue nagging. For example, you can respond, "I understand that Mom, you care about me and hope I can marry a good man, right? So, I am also carefully selecting, hoping to find a good man to marry and not make you worry too much. What dishes are we having tonight? Do you need my help in cooking?" In interpersonal communication, including communication between relatives, some skills need to be taken into account. When there is a conflict between the two sides, both parties' emotions are in a stress state, making it difficult to think calmly and rationally. If a tough attitude and language are adopted, it is not conducive to resolving conflicts. At this time, only by calming emotions first and then solving the problem can be achieved. Try to consider each other's thoughts from their perspective, find common ground that both sides can agree on, in order to persuade with care, take care of the other person's emotions, and appropriately make concessions. This can resolve conflicts and make the contradiction cease to be a contradiction. In addition to using communication skills, it would also be helpful to show more initiative in caring for parents, actively communicating, and actively showing parents the happy and fulfilling aspects of your life. This way, parents can understand you better and not be affected by idle gossip, thinking that their child is not doing well and worrying unnecessarily. Ultimately, parents worry because they care about their children, which leads to various thoughts and interference in their lives. I believe your sister is an understanding person who can understand her parents' intentions and thoughts and can communicate and get along well with them. Best wishes!

After about a month of getting to know each other, both parties may still only have surface-level understanding. From your description, it seems that you don't know what topics to talk to him about, and can only discuss the topics that he deems important. Being in a relationship means discussing each other's views on life, values, and worldviews, and talking about each other's ideals and beliefs. People tend to associate with those who share similar views and values. Only when your perspectives align can you become like-minded individuals! Only then can you become true friends and potential life partners in the future! After a month of being together, you are still in the stage of getting to know each other, and it can't be said whether you are boyfriend and girlfriend yet, as the relationship hasn't reached that level of commitment. Then decide whether to continue developing your friendship into a romantic relationship.

Why do some people feel the urge to harm animals when they see them?

As soon as I see the ducklings, chicks, and kittens, I want to squeeze them to death and abuse them to the point of death.
output: Hug the host. I have also had such behaviors and confusion before. I would like to share my thoughts and hopefully provide you with some inspiration. When I was in elementary school, I raised two small turtles. I had thoughts of killing one of them and even applied force to pinch its shell, but I was afraid of the bloody scene so I controlled the intensity. At that time, I felt so cruel and perverted. I think these thoughts of wanting to harm small animals must also have been troubling for you, right? My situation at the time was that I was an only child, my father was fully devoted to work, and my mother had a strong desire for control and had fluctuating emotions. I felt that the atmosphere at home was very oppressive and my mind seemed to be filled with negative emotions. But I had nowhere to vent or confide, so I took it out on the small turtles that were unable to resist and were weaker than me. I don't know what has happened in your life, but you can consider if you have encountered a similar situation: accumulating a lot of negative emotions in your heart, but not being allowed to express or see them, and lacking outlets for release, so you would only take it out on small animals who are even weaker than you. This is the reason I saw from my own behavior at that time, and I hope it can give you some inspiration and help you understand your own thoughts. My small suggestion is: thoughts do not equal actions. I may want to do it, but I can choose not to do it. I suggest that the host can focus more on "what has happened to make me have such thoughts," pay attention to the emotional changes and physical reactions caused by the facts. We have all sorts of thoughts every day, so we don't need to be overly anxious about them. Secondly, find a suitable outlet for the accumulated emotions. You can try writing a diary, confiding in someone, painting, practicing yoga, listening to music, meditation, etc. There are many methods that can help us release emotions and calm our restless hearts. You can make decisions based on your preferences and actual situation.

How to balance between raising a successful child and letting things take their course? How to control a child's education?

Is it more appropriate to expect one's child to achieve great success or to let things take their natural course?
output: Hello, this is my feedback: (1) Firstly, every parent hopes for their child to achieve great success. However, we need to distinguish whether we want our children to become better individuals, fulfill our own desires, or to become receptacles of knowledge and machines for learning. What does it mean for a child to "become a dragon"? This is something that parents need to ponder over. (2) Secondly, learning to go with the flow does not mean letting things take their course blindly. We should respect our children's desires for growth but not indulge their unreasonable ideas. We can communicate with them frequently, but we should not neglect them. Apart from providing resources, love and companionship are even more important. (3) Lastly, there is no progress without rules. As early as the 19th century, Freud proposed that parents play different roles in the family. The mother needs to embody warmth, while the father needs to establish rules. Therefore, it is necessary for parents to have a reasonable division of labor and provide love and guidelines. #The world and I love you, take care~.

25-year-old man, feeling very uncomfortable after learning that his partner was sexually harassed in high school.

Just three months into our relationship, she shared her deepest secret with me. At the time, she seemed quite indifferent, as if she had already come to terms with it herself. She told me that she had been involved with the same person multiple times without resisting, which made me very uncomfortable. The problem is that this matter has become a burden for me, and I haven't been able to let go of it. I don't want this issue to affect our relationship, so how should I accept it?
output: Hello. I feel very sorry for her experience, and also very uncomfortable. The fact that she can tell you her deepest secrets and expose her unknown humiliation shows that she already sees you as the most trustworthy and reliable person. But on the other hand, this burden originally belonged to her alone, and after telling you, it becomes a story and emotion that needs to be shared with you. Although it is incorrect to say that this is just a story, as the emotional impact it causes far exceeds what words can convey, I truly hope that the harm it brings will only remain at the story level. It's difficult to determine whether she has already adjusted, but it can be certain that she is also finding balance in some way, otherwise she would be suffering to the point of being unable to move forward. Lin Yihan's "The Little Reunion" is based on personal experiences, using a novel format to tell the story of herself and classmates being repeatedly seduced by a teacher, with understated words carrying an irreparable pain. Finally, she suffered from severe depression, choosing to end a life that could no longer continue. She said: Life is like clothes, so easily stripped away. She said: I'm not disappointed in you, it's this world, or life, fate, call it what you will, it's good and bad. Now I read novels, and if I come across a good ending that rewards good and punishes evil, I will cry. I prefer everyone to recognize that some pain in the world cannot be reconciled; I hate it when people say that only through suffering can one become a better person, I desperately wish for everyone to acknowledge that some pain is destructive; I hate the sentimental tradition of a happy ending, positive thinking is so vulgar! But you know what I hate even more? I would rather be a vulgar person, I would rather be ignorant, than to see the backside of the world. If there was a choice, no one wants to go to the backside of the world, or maybe if they had the ability, everyone would want to erase those unbearable stains, and then live in the light forever. Your partner's experience is a normal issue for you, but for her, it is an enormous scar that cannot be shown to anyone. As Lin Yihan said, we must recognize that some pain in the world cannot be reconciled, and acknowledge that some pain is destructive. But I hope her trust and reliance on you will allow her to be reborn, and her rebirth will allow both of you to heal and bid farewell to the past. If you are the right person for each other, you will choose to cherish her even more. Best wishes.

A 28-year-old woman developed feelings for her uncle and had an affair. How can she express herself after 2 years?

He is 14 years older than me. We met two years ago, and when I first met him, he liked me a lot. However, at that time, I was still considering and maybe he thought I rejected him, but I just thought it wasn't the right time. After two years, I still can't forget him and think he is the best. But suddenly he told me that he has already found someone else who is in a long-distance relationship with him. I'm really unhappy about this. I want to ask, does this mean I have no chance at all? I just haven't mustered the courage to say these words. He should understand now that maybe I still haven't forgotten him. Is it necessary for me to tell him that I really like him? Can he consider me?
output: # I met him two years ago. When I met him, he really liked me, but at that time I was still considering and maybe he felt rejected by me, but I just felt that it was not suitable for the time being. # There was a chance for you to be together, but you felt it was not suitable so you rejected him. # Maybe I still can't forget him # He has something that attracts you, and after two years of experience, you may also appreciate him, so you feel that he is currently your best choice. That's probably why you can't forget about him slowly. Am I understanding this correctly?# But he suddenly told me that he already has a partner who is in a long-distance relationship # It's definitely bad news for you, but you still have a chance. # Is it necessary for me to tell him that I really like him and ask him to consider me? # This is your genuine need. I think you still have a chance and options. Option one: You can continue to maintain a friendship and not rush into a romantic relationship. You can do anything you want for him. If you truly like him, he will gradually feel your affection. He does have a girlfriend now, but it doesn't prevent you from expressing your care and liking for him. However, you shouldn't rush to define the relationship. This involves ethical issues. The cost: for you, you need to accept the fact that he already has a girlfriend. Your ongoing efforts may not necessarily result in him choosing you in the end. It will test your psychological endurance. Of course, you can choose to give up at any time during this process. So, you will spend more time struggling with yourself, overcoming negative emotions, and the constraints of moral beliefs. Also, many of his actions may not meet your expectations. Option two: You can continue to stay in contact with him until he breaks up with his current girlfriend. Then, you can express your admiration for him. The cost: this option is also agonizing for yourself, and the psychological test is not lower than the first option. Slightly better, there is almost no ethical test. The higher risk is that it will be difficult to define the relationship with him, and the chance of losing him is higher. He may marry the other person. Of course, there are other options that would require further communication and more information with you.

output: Hello, dear questioner. It's heartbreaking to hear about your experiences. Sending you a virtual hug! Regarding your current problem: You are always being asked by your parents to do things that you don't want to do, and even when you do them well, there is no praise or recognition. Plus, your family only sees your flaws and never acknowledges your efforts, constantly criticizing you to the point where it becomes unbearable. I have a few suggestions for you: Try to communicate your thoughts with your family. It seems like your family has high expectations and wants you to excel. They may believe that criticizing and being strict with you will make you better. However, they may not realize that everyone has their limits and too much obedience without expressing your own needs can prevent them from knowing how much you can handle. Thus, the pressure keeps building up. Find a time when both you and your family are emotionally stable, and explain your needs, what you want to do, and your own plans. Speaking honestly is a way to release your inner emotions. If communication is impossible, there's no harm in being a little rebellious. You seem to be someone who is very obedient and dedicated in your family's eyes, which has also led to them neglecting your needs. If communication is not possible, don't always prioritize accommodating your family's feelings. Do what you truly want, love, and find useful for yourself. Don't worry about disappointing your family; they may be a little upset at first. But rather than seeing their child overwhelmed and falling into despair, they would prefer to see a happy and healthy baby. If you're feeling unhappy, go out and explore the world. I've also been someone who has been excessively demanded by my family. Although I eventually clarified things with my family and gained their understanding, there was a time when things got really bad, and I broke down and cried all night, throwing books everywhere and ending up with swollen eyes the next day. It was my classmates who brought me back from running away from home and took me shopping and out to eat. At first, my mood was really low, but seeing everyone happy and my friends patiently listening to me vent, I started to feel better. We all have moments when it's difficult to escape our emotions, so it's better to not dwell on them for now and go explore the world, enjoy good food and drinks, and then think about ways to solve the problem. No matter what, don't lose hope in yourself. The world and we all love you. Keep striving to be happy, my little mushroom who hopes for a gentle world and gives yourself the time to grow freely.

Since the beginning of school, I have been feeling homesick every day and wanting to go back home to live. I cry every night and feel unhappy in the morning. The only time I feel better is when I exercise, but as soon as it's over, I feel even worse. I become emotionally unstable over trivial matters and tend to avoid social interactions. Should I choose to live off-campus or should I adapt?
output: First of all, I understand your current situation, and it's completely normal to feel this way when you first start boarding school! Sending virtual hugs ️️ [Missing home] [Crying every night] There is a big difference between being a day student and living on campus. After a long day of studying, it's comforting to have family waiting at home. When you first start living on campus, it's common to feel insecure and have difficulty adjusting to the sleeping arrangements. I assume your sister just started high school? It's a new class with new classmates, and you haven't built a social network yet, so feeling lonely and helpless is completely normal. Don't suppress these emotions. Just like how you've found exercise as a way to release stress, try exploring other activities as well! See if there's anything you enjoy doing at school, and distract yourself with those activities. It might help improve the situation. [Mood instability due to small things] "Small things" are just triggers, but the real problem is your struggle to adapt to the environment, which makes you highly sensitive. As a result, those small things become outlets for your emotions. This emotional state has always been there; it just happened to surface. It's beneficial as long as you don't harm yourself or your friends, so don't burden yourself too much. Moreover, since you've recognized that your emotions are spiraling out of control, let's find a way that you enjoy to release those emotions even better. [Social withdrawal] Actually, the quickest way to adapt to communal living is to establish your own social network within the community. I'm not saying you have to make a lot of effort to fit in, but just find one or two friends you somewhat like and slowly spend time with them. Communal living is also a mandatory course in our lives, as you will have dorm life in college too. So if possible, I hope you can try to open up and gradually integrate yourself without rushing it. If it's really difficult to adjust, please communicate with your parents and teachers as soon as possible. Learning is already hard enough, and being happy is more important!️ I hope you can adapt to the new environment quickly and make friends with people whose personalities match yours. Rooting for you (ง•̀_•́)ง (If this has been helpful to you, please encourage me by clicking "Helpful"!)

My husband and I argue over trivial things every now and then (our arguments are not related to our sexual relationship, but because my husband often messes around with me), and sometimes it escalates to physical violence. Every time it gets serious, my husband threatens divorce, and I feel very insecure. 3. My husband's family is from a remote rural area, and they are very traditional. My father-in-law is very serious, and I don't like living with them. However, my husband has limited abilities and can't afford to buy a house for now, so I can't see a future.
output: Give you a hug. These days are so torturous, but believe me, there must be more solutions than problems when it comes to marriage stability. Love, sex, money, shared values, and nurturing the soul are all important aspects of an adult's marriage. Without the romantic colors of love, a marriage becomes more realistic and secular, which is the ugliest but most realistic part. Even the marriage of a prince and princess involves mundane matters like eating, sleeping, and making money. If legendary love stories like Liang Shanbo and Zhu Yingtai, Romeo and Juliet were to survive, they would also face the worldly reality. So first of all, do not assume that other people's marriages are always happy. My marriage is the most tragic, with flaws and shortcomings on both sides. It's just that some people's flaws are more visible than others. Sex is the premise of marriage, and a sexless marriage will only work if there's a consensus in a utopian style. Considering your sexless five-year marriage, based on your current way of having sex, it is definitely challenging to maintain your marriage. I haven't seen anything else besides love, money, and sex that can provide a foundation for your marriage. So, you need to go back to the core and see what pillars support your marriage. What kind of support can you and your husband provide for a stable marriage? If the lack of sexual desire is due to psychological problems or organic causes, you need to seek treatment. I once had a client who suffered from impotence for two years and could not have sex with his partner. In the process of counseling, we discovered that his impotence was caused by an abusive past relationship. After three hours of therapy to address the emotional trauma, the client's psychological impotence disappeared, and now he's about to become a father. So, what I want to say is, you need to seek help from a therapist or hypnotherapist to address your fear of starting sex. Find out what is blocking you. Is it a fear of men, a feeling that sex is dirty, or trauma from being abused? You need to find out the specific reasons and seek help from a therapist you trust to help you overcome your fear of sex. Because many times, resolving sexual issues can also improve many aspects of a marriage. If your fear of sex is not resolved, any man you try to be with may not be able to begin a sexual relationship. Your sexual life is currently resolved by avoiding sex and just rubbing together; this can lead to problems like premature ejaculation and impotence for your husband in the long run. A large part of your disputes and arguments actually stem from the unsatisfactory sexual relationship. Both you and your husband may need to seek help from professionals. If you resolve your sexual issues, it is highly possible that your current problems of arguing and the husband frequently threatening divorce will be resolved. Deep down, you don't want to divorce him and you fear his threats of divorce during arguments. So instead of waiting for him to change, it's better to take the initiative to address the core issues. Solve the sexual problems and many answers to your marriage will fall into place. Your fears of sex, divorce, and an uncertain future will disappear one by one. I wish you happiness.

Feeling easily trampled upon by others makes me very sad, how can I improve my self-esteem?

Recently, I've been constantly reminded of my first job. At that time, I lived and ate together with the boss's wife. She was a Buddhist and a vegetarian, and often advised me to become a vegetarian and believe in Buddhism. I didn't dare to refuse her. We used the same skincare products, shampoo, and shower gel, all placed on the left and right sides of the washbasin. Due to financial difficulties, I would only use a little each time, so a bottle could last me a long time. Many times, she would intentionally or unintentionally suspect me of stealing her things, asking why her things were being used up so quickly while mine lasted so long. I didn't dare to offend her too much, so even though I denied it, she seemed to take it as an admission that I had indeed stolen from her. In reality, she had forgotten that she never hesitated to use her things and often invited her friends and mother to come and stay, and they all used her things. How could her things not be used up quickly? Every time I think about this past experience, I feel that I have such low self-esteem and feel so stifled. Since then, I have been studying psychology and thinking about how to improve my self-esteem and self-love, so that I won't easily let others trample on my self-esteem. That feeling of being easily trampled upon by others makes me very sad.
output: Hug to the original poster. It really doesn't feel good to be suspected and wrongly accused. You didn't dare refuse the boss lady's request; she suspected and falsely accused you of stealing things, and you denied it, but it made her assume her suspicion. You felt unjust and unhappy inside, but you didn't, or rather, you didn't dare express it clearly to her. This happened in your first job when you just entered society, you were relatively young, and didn't know how to handle this kind of social relationship, didn't dare offend others, and didn't dare resist authority. This behavior is normal and also shows that you are sensitive and have a strong self-preservation instinct. Now you can reflect and be aware of the negative impact of this incident and your own behavior, and want to make changes and improvements, which is rare. This process is painful and difficult, but it is also a necessary step for you to change and improve yourself. The enhancement of self-esteem first requires recognizing your inner needs, improving self-confidence, having a firm will in your beliefs and pursuits; you need to have a correct understanding of yourself, see your strengths and advantages, and not neglect your weaknesses. Set goals for your own efforts in life, and then use your strengths and advantages one by one to achieve them, gain successful results, this process and the experience of success can strengthen your confidence and enhance your self-esteem. In addition to focusing on improving self-esteem, there is a need to pay attention to the issue of boundaries. You feel frustrated by the boss lady's behavior, not only because she falsely accused you, but also because she invaded your boundaries, making you feel uncomfortable, even disgusted and afraid. Whether it's family, friends, colleagues, or bosses, it is necessary to establish certain boundaries, maintain a certain social distance with others, maintain one's independence, not interfere with each other's lives and emotions, not overly intrude into others' lives or be intruded by others. If someone invades excessively, they should consider how to distance themselves in order to get out of this easily violated environment. This can also protect your self-esteem. The past is like a thorn stuck in your heart, always feeling uncomfortable, even painful. However, no matter how uncomfortable or regretful you are, the matter is already in the past. Excessive retrospection or getting trapped in it will only intensify your pain and regret, and cannot change the past facts. What you need to do is to quickly ignore the negative impact of this past event on you, focus on the present and the future, and make plans and take action for your own growth. Keep it up!

At 13 years old, I was diagnosed with borderline personality disorder, and I have always been alone.

Please, help me, I can't take it anymore. Who am I, really? Don't... don't! Go away! I hate this world!! Stay away! Stay away! I'm begging you! Give up on me!! Phew, I feel better now. It feels so much better to say it out loud. It's been weighing on my mind. Sometimes, I really want to scream, "I want to kill myself, why won't you save me?!" I've always been alone, talking to myself, eating alone, sleeping alone, playing on the computer alone, taking walks alone, wanting to jump off a building alone... Why haven't you come to save me? Am I not worth saving? Or did I do something wrong... Mother, why did you leave me all alone? Why did you fly away like a bird, never to return? I really miss you. Maybe if I wake up from this sleep, you'll come back. Maybe life is just a dream and you woke up before me. I really don't know what to do. I don't want to live, I don't want to do anything, I'm not interested in anything. Maybe I have depression? Well, that's okay. I can finally get some sleep alone. Goodnight, mother.
output: Seeing words as if we are face to face, I hope these words can bring you a little warmth. Child - I hope this term does not offend you - I am glad to see you on this platform, which means you still have hope in life, hoping that someone can lend you a hand. And today is my first day here, this is my first answer. I happen to be 26 years old, twice your age. This is probably our fate - so you see, you are not alone, there is a stranger who saw you at a glance, chose you, you are not alone. Sometimes in life, there are too many things that we cannot understand. It doesn't mean that you are without fault, you are not necessarily loved. I can't just tell you through words that your mother loves you, but she may have her reasons. But I can tell you, "The world is so big, there will always be someone who loves you." If you are in pain, do something else, don't immerse yourself in pain. Read a book, the world in the book is vast and boundless, it can warm you, or maybe make you more sad, but even the most tragic stories have a bit of warmth, the worst life can have a touch of light. Listen to music, it embodies the emotions of many people, whether sad or happy, you can always find a song that resonates with you. Go study - yes, go study, whether it is school subjects or things you love, if you can immerse yourself in learning, you will be completely focused and not think about other problems; it will also allow you to improve and slowly overcome the current difficulties. The road of life is still long, do not give up easily, and do not give up on life. This world is beautiful - I promise. I hope I can say good morning to you tomorrow.
