I was the victim of phone fraud this afternoon and I feel really upset. What should I do?

Today is June 25, 2020. It's Dragon Boat Festival. At 15:00 in the afternoon, I fell victim to a telephone scam and lost 1600 RMB. This might not be a significant amount for most people, and even when I reported the case to the police, they said to me, "Why are you crying? It's not a large sum of money." But I am still a student, with no other source of income other than my parents. My family is not well-off, and I can't even be considered comfortably off. That money was my scholarship and financial aid for this semester, which I worked hard to obtain. I always hesitated to spend it. I deeply regret falling for the scam so easily. Looking back, there were many red flags, but I still fell for it. Was I so naive and stupid? After reporting the case, I didn't want my family to worry, so during our dinner gathering, I pretended to be as usual and enjoyed the Dragon Boat Festival. However, after it ended, I was alone in my room, thinking about the scam today, and I felt really sad and upset. I couldn't control my tears. I really hate the scammers. I am truly heartbroken now. Normally, I am always optimistic and cheerful, but since that scam phone call this afternoon, I haven't been able to find happiness, even when watching my favorite anime. What should I do?
output: My friend, a psychology student, are you feeling more stable now? I don't know if my response is too late or too late, but I wanted to offer you a virtual pat on the back. Because when I was in my third year of college, I also experienced a telecommunications fraud, and at the time, the amount of money I was swindled out of was 3000 yuan. I wasn't able to recover it even after reporting it to the police, and I know the feeling of regret and self-blame. I really want to offer you some comfort. Because I am also an ordinary student, I understand the value of this money even more. As a student, 1600 yuan is indeed not as small as 16 yuan, and it has the added significance of coming from your scholarship. From a psychological perspective, it is normal for unpleasant things to happen and for people to experience negative emotions. It is normal for you to feel sad because it has happened to you. There is no need to force yourself to immediately feel happy. It's okay to give yourself some more time to feel down. This is your moment of sadness, and you can experience it fully. Then give yourself a hug and say, "Hmm, this thing happened, and it's normal for me to feel sad. If it were someone else, they would feel sad too." You mentioned that you need to hold it together in front of your parents, eat well, and speak well. From these behaviors, it seems that I can see your small worries about your parents. Are you afraid of being blamed by them? If you feel afraid of being blamed, then don't tell them, it's okay. After weighing the options, deciding to face hardships alone is also a sign of maturity. If the financial loss from this incident is still within your manageable range, you have the right to choose to bear it yourself. Many adults also do the same. Oh, and about being deceived, no matter how many cases there are, it's not the same as experiencing it personally. Many people are knowledgeable about fraud cases, but it's always difficult to avoid falling for scams. The reason for this is that empathy is a difficult thing. Before being scammed, we cannot truly understand the professionalism and rigor of the scammers' words, nor can we truly experience the change in our state of mind when fraud occurs. Fraud groups usually work as a team, creating a tense atmosphere and challenging us in various ways. Our individual strength is easily conquered by fraud groups. However, after this experience, your "immune system" against fraud will be greatly improved. Congratulations, you have completed an experience of being scammed. I believe that after this small scam, your alertness will be higher. I think that if similar scams happen to you in the future, you will be more calm and composed.

We have been married for 10 years, and my wife never initiates intimacy. It's always me who takes the lead, but most of the time, it feels like she is not interested and not responsive. I want to have a heart-to-heart conversation with her, but even when I pour my heart out and express my feelings, she doesn't share her own thoughts and feelings with me! I love her very much!
output: Hello! This description looks like a riddle, and the answers given by the respondents are mostly guesswork, so that's the problem. The troubles you are facing are clearly caused by communication problems. We often say that the key to communication lies in listening, not speaking, because if we "don't understand", we cannot have valuable conversations. "We have been married for 10 years, and my wife never takes the initiative in intimate relationships. It's always me initiating, but the process often feels uninteresting and unresponsive." This problem may be caused by biological factors or psychological factors. In uncertain situations, let's assume it's caused by psychological factors. Intimacy is an important factor that affects the harmony of intimate relationships, so if there is disharmony in this aspect, the first consideration should be the level of intimacy between the two people. "I want to talk to her, but even when I open my heart and share my innermost thoughts with her, she doesn't do the same with me! I love her so much!" The factors that affect the level of intimacy between two people include individual psychological tendencies and the ability to fulfill each other's needs. Maslow divided human needs into five layers: physiological needs, safety needs, social needs, esteem needs, and self-actualization needs. In theory, if one person can fulfill the other person's corresponding needs, the level of intimacy in this relationship will be high. In most marriages, people's requirements for their partners include physiological needs, safety needs, esteem needs, and social needs. Here, "social needs" specifically refers to whether communication is smooth. Generally speaking, this situation does not happen overnight. Usually, there is a gradual process. One important reason why two people go from sharing everything to having nothing to say is that one or both parties cannot accept each other's emotions. Emotions are often illogical, and any attempt to judge the reasonableness of emotions with values is meaningless. This is why people often say that "reasoning does not work at home", at least not on certain issues and at certain times. So, please recall what happened in these ten years. How did the situation of you being active and her passive come about? Did you become too active, forcing her to be passive, or was she always passive from the beginning, causing you to be active? Love can be an individual matter, but marriage is definitely a matter between two people. Don't "guess blindly" when any problems arise in marriage. Make sure to seek confirmation from the other person and do not be confrontational. Understanding the other person is not difficult, just have less judgment. I wish you a happy life!

It's common for major and minor tasks to become a mess when there are too many goals. What should be done in this case?

There are multiple targets, and the importance of each one is often unclear and chaotic. How to handle each task corresponds to a method, but it is easy to get confused and forget.
output: OP, hello~~~ First, let me give you a virtual hug. From your description, I understand that you are unclear about managing tasks of different sizes, which leads to difficulty in completing them effectively. 【A little advice】By using the Eisenhower Matrix, you can effectively manage your tasks. If you categorize your tasks into four quadrants based on their urgency and importance, it will help you gain a deeper understanding of time and manage it effectively. The first quadrant includes urgent and important tasks. These tasks are time-sensitive and have significant impact. They cannot be avoided or postponed and need to be addressed as a priority. Examples include negotiating major projects or important meeting work. The second quadrant is different from the first. The events in this quadrant may not be urgent, but they have significant impact. They are of great importance for personal or business existence, development, and the establishment and maintenance of the surrounding environment. The third quadrant mainly consists of trivial matters. They are not time-sensitive nor important. Such events are purely time-wasting and life-squandering. Activities like daydreaming, browsing the internet, chatting, and aimlessly wandering around are typical for those who have nothing substantial to do. The fourth quadrant includes events that are urgent but not important. These tasks may seem urgent, but in reality, they are not important. Many people have a misconception and believe that urgent matters are always important. In fact, events like meaningless phone calls, conforming to others' expectations, or playing mahjong with three players are not important. However, since they are urgent, they often end up occupying people's precious time.

output: Hello! Discovered that your husband has cheated, and expected the other person to confess and apologize, begging for forgiveness, and make amends for his mistakes through practical actions. When one person in an intimate relationship cheats, the person who has been betrayed inevitably experiences some degree of pain. To determine whether you see your partner as a loved one or a tool, a small indicator is your initial reaction when you first found out about your husband's infidelity - did you feel sadness or anger? If anger was your primary and strongest feeling, it is likely that your husband has always been seen as a tool in your relationship. He can perceive that his emotional needs are not being met, which is why he sought fulfillment outside the relationship, causing your intense anger and frustration. In emotional counseling, it is often said that infidelity seems like a third-party problem, but upon careful observation, it is actually a problem within the relationship itself that leads to the involvement of a third-party external force (assuming your husband is not a playboy). When you have treated your partner as a tool for a long time, there is no true emotional connection between you. Your partner can feel it, and when his emotional needs are not met, he will search for channels outside the relationship to satisfy them. Therefore, it is even more important for the person in the relationship to first sit down and calmly reflect and examine. Where were the problems in your relationship? What communication issues did you have? Did you give him enough attention in the relationship? Did you emotionally blackmail him too much? What is your own emotional pattern like? If your partner were to return to the family, would you accept him without criticism? Do you understand your husband's emotional needs? Take the time to think carefully, use this experience to reflect on your intimate relationship, and both parties need to adjust and grow in order to rebuild a "new" intimate relationship. output: Dear OP, hello there. From your description, I can feel your helplessness and feelings of despair. Firstly, why do parents resist or even ignore our illness? In the older generation's mindset, when emotions such as depression, bipolar disorder, and anxiety are diagnosed as psychological illnesses, they tend to associate it with insanity (what we call "crazy"). This is a cognitive error and prejudice. Parents temporarily cannot accept the fact that you have been diagnosed with bipolar disorder, they cannot accept that their daughter is different from others. This can be seen from their response every time: "How could you be depressed?" This shows it. Parents' love for their children is profound. Because your parents do not believe that you suddenly developed bipolar disorder for no reason, you want to not only understand the cause of your illness for yourself, but also to make your parents understand it in the future so that they can cooperate with your treatment. Let your parents realize that bipolar disorder is just like a cold or fever, it is just an illness that can be cured as long as you cooperate and receive proper treatment, although the recovery process may be longer. However, this kind of need cannot be discovered, understood, accepted, or acknowledged by the OP's conscious self. Asperger's syndrome is a neurodevelopmental disorder characterized by social difficulties, restricted interests, and repetitive behaviors. Asperger's syndrome and autism spectrum disorder belong to the autism spectrum disorders, but ASD does not have significant speech and intellectual impairments, and may even have abilities in certain areas that are higher than average, hence also being called "high-functioning autism." The prevalence of Asperger's syndrome is about 3.6‰-7.1‰, with a much higher incidence in males than females, and there is a tendency for it to cluster in families. Asperger's syndrome is a lifelong disease, but symptoms often improve gradually with development. Adults with this condition can recognize their strengths and weaknesses and improve their social skills. Currently, there are no effective measures for preventing Asperger's syndrome. Asperger's syndrome usually cannot be noticed until after the age of 3. The clinical symptoms of this disease vary greatly among patients. Clinical manifestations in children with Asperger's syndrome include: extreme difficulty in communicating with others. This does not mean that children with Asperger's syndrome are avoiding social interaction, but they lack the instinct and skills to express their thoughts, feelings, and pay attention to the feelings of others. Easily bothered by loud noises, lights, strong smells, or crowded patterns. They like routine and have difficulty making changes. They have difficulty recognizing verbal or non-verbal information and understanding social norms. For example, they may stare at others without making eye contact, or they may not understand the concept of personal space. They speak lacking in tone, intonation, and emphasis, and their speech may be straightforward and difficult to understand. They may have poor coordination, abnormal facial expressions, body postures, gestures, or be clumsy, and may have difficulties in writing or other motor skills such as riding a bicycle. They have only one or a few interests, or are strongly obsessed with certain things. For example, they may have unusual preferences for snake or star names, or they may be able to draw very detailed pictures. (The above information is from the Internet and is for the OP's reference only) The presentation of symptoms is only one basis for auxiliary analysis and diagnosis. In the analysis and diagnosis of psychological problems and diseases, it is also necessary to consider the impact of symptoms on normal daily life and the level of inner conflict and pain. From the information provided by the OP, it can be seen that there is a certain degree of repression in their heart, and social impairment is not very evident. They have the ability to lead an independent and autonomous life and have normal social skills, but they lack a sense of security to some extent, and after being stimulated by certain things, they may exhibit a certain degree of regressive behavior. At the same time, the OP mentioned that they often bump into table corners after not practicing dancing, which on one hand may be due to the OP's nervousness and anxiety, and on the other hand, it suggests possible damage to the OP's imagination and nerve-related symptoms. Emotional changes affect the circulation of Qi and blood in the body, thus affecting nerve reflexes. Is the unconscious desire for others to feel happy, people-pleasing?

Why do we hope that everyone around us can feel happy, and why do we care so much about other people's emotions? It can be exhausting, but we can't control it.
output: Hello cutie! First of all, let's determine whether you have a people-pleasing personality. The main characteristics of this trait are: the motivation behind their behavior is a lack of self-worth and fear of not being loved, even to the point of being afraid of being abandoned. This becomes an unhealthy, compulsive, and painful pattern of behavior. It seems like you're saying that you find it exhausting to focus on other people's emotions, which could indicate a people-pleasing personality. #Why do I want to make others happy? Bringing joy to others is a valuable part of life. Our elders have also taught us this, and taking care of and loving others is one of the highest forms of spiritual practice. Making others happy is an effective way to convey our own worth, gain a sense of value, and experience happiness. But are you truly experiencing this sense of value and happiness from it? It seems not. So where is the problem? It lies in our motivation. We pay attention to others' emotions not out of a desire for "I am happy and I also want them to be happy," but out of a desire for "I am not happy, I feel invaluable, and I hope to receive a feeling of love and acceptance by making them happy." In other words, we treat love and acceptance as a transaction. I must pay a price that causes me pain in order to receive it. And when we don't get the expected response, our inner balance is disrupted. This behavior pattern is an unhealthy, compulsive, and painful one. The formation of a people-pleasing personality is due to childhood trauma, specifically the lack of unconditional love from our original family. But I'm not asking you to blame your parents! That would only make us more miserable. Instead, let's explore the reasons behind this behavior and then find the right solutions to heal ourselves slowly, to become the person we want to be rather than the person we're forced to be. This is our ultimate goal. #Only when we make ourselves happy, when we have inner strength, can we pass on happiness to others. Everyone has their own life issues to face. Our main issue at the moment is the self-healing of our people-pleasing personality. It's a long but meaningful journey. Once you embark on this path, you will gradually discover that your pain is slowly dissipating, and you will learn to love yourself more and more. Here are a few suggestions: 1) Practice mindfulness: Mindfulness is being aware of your present state without biases or a closed mindset. Because our thoughts are often clouded by past "traumas" and the fear of being rejected, criticized, or even denied if we don't please others, through mindfulness, we can establish a connection with our bodies and minds, and bravely face difficult experiences, including the feeling when the emotions of needing to please others overwhelm us. 2) Remember that our thoughts are just thoughts, not facts: Through a period of mindfulness practice, we focus on the present moment. When pleaser thoughts arise in our minds, instead of immediately acting on them based on instinct, we gently greet them as an adult would greet a love-deprived child, saying, "Oh, you're here! Hello!" Rather than engaging with these thoughts, because behind them is the love-deprived version of yourself! If we resist these thoughts, we are essentially rejecting our past selves. But what is wrong with the love-deprived child? They only want unconditional love. 3) You have the power to give unconditional love to this love-deprived child within you: Regardless of our age, when we realize that we are responsible for our own lives and that we want to make ourselves happy, we actually have the ability to take care of this love-deprived child. When there aren't so many ups and downs within you, set aside a "Children's Day" for yourself. On this day, do what the child inside you wanted to do at that time, spend time with them, talk to them, and assure them that you will meet their needs and give them unconditional love. Because this unconditional love already exists within us, we just accidentally lost it when we were young. When you can give yourself happiness, you will find it easy and joyful to bring happiness to others. However, whether others truly receive this happiness is up to them! It is their responsibility, not ours. Lastly, I hope that in the future, you can truly be happy and truly find joy in the process of bringing happiness to others!

Expose her true face? How should I treat my incredible mother?

I have an extraordinary good mother, what makes her extraordinary? The following points: 1. I was raised by my father since I was young, even after my two younger sisters were born, my father's love for me did not diminish (I should be grateful, otherwise I would truly have an uncaring father and unloving mother). I am growing up now, but I suffer from insomnia every day, and my extraordinary good mother is always involved. So, after being awakened by my extraordinary good mother in the early hours of the morning, I sit in front of the computer and type (yesterday I finally managed to fall asleep before 12 o'clock). 3. She loves to pretend. In the eyes of others, she is an extraordinary good mother, and I am an ungrateful child. No one knows the truth, including my father, and I dare not speak up, even if I do, no one will believe me. People surrounded by maternal love, I believe, will not believe my words, but I have been pushed into depression and insomnia from being a happy and healthy person, and my grades have also been affected. This is my extraordinary good mother! Can someone tell me how to expose her true face?
output: Hello. Allow me to first talk about my impression of you: *I don't know your gender or exact age, but I assume you are underage.* Your relationship with your father is much better than with your mother, but you also feel that your father seems to be gradually distancing himself from you, probably due to some influence from your mother. *You usually have poor sleep quality, and your mother often wakes you up when you're already asleep, but you haven't mentioned why or provided specific details.* You find the image of your mother that she presents to others to be fake and pretentious, and it seems like others see you as an ungrateful child who doesn't understand maternal love. But you dare not tell anyone about all this, including your father, because you think no one would believe you. *Now, you feel that the person you used to be was healthy and happy, but now you feel overall terrible, with declining academic performance and a depressed state of mind, reaching the severity of depression (I'm not sure if a professional doctor has diagnosed you or if it's your own belief).* You attribute all these negative changes to your mother. *You seem to want to expose your mother's true nature to others. But I'm not sure if you have any other plans, such as trying to adjust your own state without changing the current situation or finding a way to distance yourself from your mother, etc. Now, allow me to share my thoughts: *I feel sorry for what you're going through. If what you say is true and your mother has caused you a lot of pain, I'm glad you can come here to vent. I believe you're not a lying child. *However, I'm also willing to continue the conversation with you in order to better help you, especially to learn more about you and your mother, to understand what other things besides disturbing your sleep she has done that bother, embarrass, and distress you. If it's not convenient, you can seek help from your homeroom teacher, the school's counseling teacher, or any other person you trust. I believe they will help you. *If unfortunately, they don't believe you or refuse to help you, at least there are people here willing to listen to your experience and help you get out of this predicament. Stay well.

Will mental illnesses send signals to the body? For example, will pimples and rashes appear on the body?

Recently, I watched a psychological interview where the interviewee had white spots all over their body, which was very distressing. However, I didn't finish watching it, as the teacher mentioned that it caused some mental health disorders.
output: Hello there! After experiencing certain psychological issues, some physical symptoms may occur. In psychology, this phenomenon is called somatization, which refers to a situation where a person has emotional or psychological problems but does not manifest them as psychological symptoms, instead, they are converted into various physical symptoms. For example, a patient with anxiety disorder may often experience insomnia, headaches, and other problems. Alternatively, some people may experience stomachaches when they are particularly stressed. It is important to note the causal and correlational relationships between somatization symptoms and psychological problems. Causality means understanding whether certain somatization symptoms are caused by psychological problems or if the psychological problems are caused by certain physical factors. Correlation refers to the fact that psychological problems and somatization symptoms do not always occur simultaneously. Specific situations require specific analysis.

Always repeating these conflicts, every time I encounter them, my first reaction is to think about divorce.

Trying to conceive, my husband can't quit smoking and occasionally drinks alcohol... I'm very distressed about this and have communicated with him, made arrangements, but ultimately all failed! Over the past few months, his old problem has resurfaced. He wants to play mahjong every week and plays it on his phone when he comes home from work every day. I told him I wanted a life where we are both busy with work during the day and can spend time together at night chatting, cooking, and exercising. He occasionally does it, but still can't resist playing mahjong on his phone regularly. I've had heartfelt conversations with him about these two issues, gentle communication, sad confessions, arguments, negotiations... but they only have temporary effects! Now he has started to avoid communication. He drinks, smokes continuously, and stays up late playing mahjong... He no longer wants to hear what I have to say, no matter how calm or what tone I use, he just turns around and walks away without saying a word! Last year, I had a miscarriage because the gestational sac didn't develop properly, so I really want a healthy child. But I always feel like I'm the only one making an effort. He has also tried, but it's intermittent. He can't control himself. We have been married for three years, and it has been a three-year adjustment. Now, I'm really tired and conflicted. I want a divorce, but I also have many concerns!
output: Hello! Hearing about your current life situation, I understand the pain you are going through. Facing problems in your marriage and repeatedly trying with disappointing results has left you feeling conflicted and doubting the commitment to your marriage. Let's talk together and see if there are any areas where we can improve your current situation, okay? You are currently trying to conceive and, due to a previous miscarriage, you hope to have a healthy baby. You are concerned about anything that could harm the baby, such as your husband's smoking and drinking. You have asked him to quit smoking and drinking, but he hasn't done so, which disappoints you. Maybe he is trying, but not meeting your expectations in quitting smoking and drinking. Your request is understandable as it is for the well-being of your baby. I believe your husband understands this fact and knows that it is not good for the baby. Quitting smoking and drinking is not easy, perhaps you need to try to understand his perspective, talk to him, and understand the underlying reasons for his continued smoking and drinking habits. No matter the reason, try to show him some understanding, as it may help him improve. He has resumed his old habits of smoking, playing mahjong, and not spending time with you, which is not what you want. You have communicated with him many times, but in the end, he avoids the conversation and refuses to communicate. This makes you feel unaccepted and helpless, as if you are the only one making an effort while he doesn't seem to care. You want him to spend more time with you and have the kind of life you desire, but he can't seem to do it. Have you considered his needs and desires while only expressing your own? Both partners in a marriage should strive to satisfy each other's needs and rely on each other. If you can't see his needs or meet them, he will surely be dissatisfied, even though men may not express it as directly as women. So, when you make demands, you should also consider his thoughts, pay attention to his needs, and respect him, providing a certain response and satisfaction. Love flows in both directions, he will feel your love and express his love to you. His refusal to communicate makes you feel that he is not putting effort into your family, which causes your dissatisfaction. Regarding his behavior, you think that he can't control himself. Why does he refuse to communicate? This depends on how you communicated in the past. If he ultimately refuses to communicate, it means that your communication approach is ineffective. Therefore, improving your communication pattern is vital. Building effective communication: First, you need to listen. You need to listen to his perspective and feelings towards the issue. Ask if he has considered the harm smoking and drinking can cause to the baby, and what worries or concerns he has. Listen attentively and take this opportunity to fully understand him. Secondly, offer understanding. Put yourself in his shoes and empathize with his emotions. Agree with his feelings and provide reassurance. Thirdly, directly express your requirements to him. Tell him that you hope he can work together with you to raise a healthy baby, spend more time with you, and create the kind of home you desire. Fourthly, acknowledge his efforts and provide feedback. Thank him for his contributions and let him see the positive impact he has had on your life. This will make him feel supported and motivated to continue his efforts. Feeling helpless and resentful has led you to doubt your marriage. After three years of trying to make it work, your marriage still makes you sad and exhausted. So you now consider divorce but have concerns. The truth about marriage is that harmony can bring sweetness and happiness, while pain can make you want to leave. Divorce is not a wise choice for pain because the pain is not the root of the problem. Just like in your marriage, the pain you feel is not the issue, but rather the conflicting approaches and actions when dealing with your husband and resolving problems, which causes your pain. We all say that marriage requires effort, and this effort has no time limit. Whatever problems arise, they must be bravely faced and resolved together so that the marriage can move towards greater happiness. I am sure that once you and your husband can resolve this issue and work together to welcome a healthy baby, the intimacy between you and your spouse will greatly increase. I wish you a happy life and take good care of yourself. The world and I love you, and this is a secret base for your questions anytime.

The pain of life, feeling like everything is concentrated on me?

Difficulty in handling interpersonal relationships, pain from the original family, childhood misfortune, feeling like everything revolves around me. I want to die but I am afraid to die. Will dying bring relief?
output: Hello, the many things in life seem to be cyclical. When you feel good, everything seems to go smoothly, and this smoothness makes you feel even better. Then you perform better, forming a positive cycle. Conversely, there is also a negative cycle, where everything feels bad and nothing goes smoothly, leading to a downward spiral. It's like the ancient poem says, "When the roof is leaking, it always coincides with a night of rain." You said that it feels like everything is concentrated on you, but perhaps you are just trapped in this negative cycle. If you can break this cycle and enter a positive one, everything will gradually improve. Actually, the pain you mentioned is all interconnected. It's because your original family was painful that you had an unfortunate childhood. This unfortunate childhood didn't allow you to learn healthy patterns of interpersonal relationships, making it easy to encounter problems in that area. Not all the problems revolve around you; it's just that one problem leads to another, triggering a series of issues. Although the impact of the painful original family is significant, it is not something that cannot be overcome entirely. Through our efforts, we can try our best to overcome the trauma from our original family, break free from the negative cycle, and create a different life for ourselves. However, this process is not simple or quick. It may require long-term effort. If possible, I suggest seeking a consultation with a counselor. With the counselor's guidance, you can reexamine your growth journey and achieve psychological growth and transformation. If you currently don't have the means, you can also read more books related to psychology, such as "Transcending the Original Family" and "Having a Life Where You Have the Final Say." These books contain many theories and methods that can help us in our self-growth. You should know that as long as you don't give up and keep making efforts, you can gradually break free from the current terrible state. Give yourself some time, be patient, take it slow, and remember that life won't always be this bad! Sending you a hug, the world and I love you! (^_-).

Phil wants to say, first, you need to stabilize your mindset. The more critical the situation, the less you should panic. Panic and anxiety won't solve the problem and may even make it worse. It's possible that the material you missed is easy for you but difficult for others to understand. But no matter what, the most important thing is to retain your assignments and exams, and then ask the teacher promptly when you return to school, whether it's for the missed parts or the parts you don't understand, and make use of your free time to catch up.

23-year-old female has been suffering from depression for two years and social anxiety. She wants to self-regulate. How can she do it?

A 23-year-old woman has been suffering from depression for two years. After taking medication for half a year, she experienced severe side effects, including uncontrollable hand tremors that hinder her from performing delicate tasks. She decided to stop taking the medication on her own for six months. Currently, she is experiencing severe social anxiety, unwilling to answer phone calls or interact with others. She even refuses to leave her room. Although she doesn't want to be this way, she feels extremely anxious and nervous when interacting with others. She wonders how she can regulate herself.
output: This is what I wrote, my own experience, hoping to help you. Article title: "In-depth Analysis: Why do we isolate ourselves and refuse to see any friends when we are depressed?" In the Warm Home group, some of the depression patients I am more familiar with will find different degrees of interpersonal sensitivity and compulsive tendencies when doing the SCL-90. After the onset of depression, we find ourselves in a dilemma. After discovering the huge gap between our true selves, ideal selves, and our past selves, we cannot accept it when we see our true selves. In fact, our previous self in Horney's "Our Inner Conflicts" is called the idealized self, which is the self that we excessively magnified before and is not real; our current self is also not real, but has been continuously depreciated by us. In a previous article on our public account, "The Power of Self-Suggestion" was mentioned, which said that self-suggestion can change our thinking and then change our behavior. This suggestion can be positive or negative. It is precisely because of this that we first have a discrepancy and then have compulsive thinking. Under the constant depreciation (suggestion) of ourselves, we feel more and more that we are getting worse and worse, more and more unacceptable, and more and more worthless. Conflict with friends 01: We lost completely. After staying in the Warm Home for a long time, I am more familiar with the personality of most group members. Regardless of how their interpersonal relationships were before, they basically have two personality traits: perfectionism and assertiveness. Perfectionism makes us demand perfection in things that we particularly care about (mainly due to different growth experiences) and cannot accept any criticism; assertiveness makes us unable to lose to anyone in things that we particularly care about. The problem arises here. After the onset of depression, when we discover that our true selves are not as perfect as we imagined, and under the constant depreciation of ourselves through compulsive thinking, our current selves become more and more worthless. So our assertiveness comes out again. "They must laugh at us, look down on us." "We're done, we can never hold our heads up in front of them again. I will never be able to be proud in front of them again." This is the first conflict, we are inferior to others, we lost to others, and they will laugh at me. Then we start to see that people who used to be worse off than us are doing better than us, and we feel more and more uncomfortable, and we hate ourselves more and more. We feel that we are worse than everyone, and we are simply the worst person in the world. Self-confidence completely collapses, crushed brutally. Occasionally going out to see friends, but always feel that they are laughing at us, looking down on us, and anything negative they say is about us. So we have various fears, fear of crowds, fear of social interactions, and then we start to isolate ourselves and cut off contact with family, relatives, and friends. Because we cannot accept this fact, so we start to escape. We hope to find a countryside, a place where no one knows us; we hope to find a place to retreat to. 02: I want to ask for help, but I have hurt them before. In a previous article, it was mentioned that during depression, we actually desire to find friends to help us. But it is difficult to speak up. Looking back, I feel that I am ashamed to ask them for help. Because I have hurt too many people when I was in glory. Or, because we refuse to forgive others for their minor mistakes, our relationship becomes strained. When we have depression, our confidence collapses, and our previous self only showed the best side to others. And at this time, we are already in such a miserable state, and I have hurt them before, they will definitely not help me. So, I start to feel guilty, self-blame, isolated and helpless. Under compulsive thinking, constantly repeating, constantly suggesting, feeling that the past cannot be saved, if this friend who we have hurt knows how miserable I am, they will definitely take pleasure in my misfortune. Finally, it turns into another emotion: self-hatred, despair; and then continues to strengthen, and turns into self-attack. 03: Why don't they understand me? When my depression attacks, I have turned to several close friends to confide in. Of course, I didn't tell them that I have depression. I just told them about my current situation and various problems, and I told them over and over again. Friends didn't understand me at the time, and they felt that we were full of negative energy, always complaining, and didn't want to talk to me. At that moment, I started another emotion: anger. "Why did I treat you so well before? When you were in a bad mood, it was me who comforted you. But when I am in a bad mood, you are not there for me." "You should care about me, accompany me. You used to be my best and most trustworthy friends!" ...Then, under compulsive thinking, constant suggestion, I feel more and more that there is no good person in this world, and it finally turns into another emotion: hatred. How to deal with relationships with friends? 01: Thinking that friends will mock oneself may just be projection. Many people think that friends will mock themselves, including myself before. Until one day, I learned to do things solidly, instead of always analyzing the success of something based on my own logic, but discovering the feasibility of doing things based on my own gradual adjustment. I realized that any small thing that I thought was easy before, is actually not easy when doing it, and mistakes will occur. Until one day, I learned to accept that my life is not always smooth sailing; learned to accept that I am not perfect and dare to show my imperfections; learned to accept that I will make mistakes and learn from them; learned to accept that I will fail and gain growth from failures; learned to do things step by step diligently and discover that things are not as easy as they seem... At this time, I finally started to stop judging and evaluating others, and even started to feel compassion for people in adversity and helped them sincerely. So, this is my understanding, only by reconciling with ourselves can we reconcile with the world. What you think of others, depends on your needs and your inner perspective. 02: Accept reality, appreciate and learn humbly from friends who are better than us. Our current selves are not as worthless as we imagine. We are just constantly suggesting and feeling worse in compulsive thinking, under various comparisons. In today's society, many people need to receive praise from others to affirm themselves, so when you see them showing off, it is not genuine, and it also reflects their own possible insecurities. At this time, they are not real either. Everything good you see about them is just superficial. Because we are looking at them while depreciating ourselves, so we appear to be much worse than them. Moreover, those who were worse than us before are not really worse than us, we just cannot see what we care about in them. For example, we did not care about emotional intelligence before, thinking that it is being naive and easy to be bullied. But the truth is that they know how to give, they are loyal, they are more diligent than us, so they are appreciated by their superiors. And we are difficult to control, unconsciously not putting our superiors in our eyes, so our superiors don't like us... So, we must admit our shortcomings and learn from others when necessary. Only in this way can we progress and constantly improve ourselves. Finally, those successful people around us, you have to admit that they are indeed better than us. They have higher emotional intelligence, stronger abilities, and have put in a lot of effort privately. Only when they were putting in effort, we couldn't see it, we only focused on their success. So, when it is necessary to admit defeat, we must admit defeat, don't envy, just appreciate. The envy of successful people around us is a normal emotion, not only for us with depression, but also for many normal people. It is a very normal emotion for human beings. So, you don't need to blame yourself because of envy. Envy breeds dark thinking in our hearts, and then changes our behavior, deliberately causing trouble, belittling others, and ultimately destroying relationships. Only by appreciating and learning to see the strengths of others can we learn from them and make progress. 03: Learn to understand and forgive. In fact, the world of depression patients is difficult for those who have not experienced depression to understand, including psychologists and counselors. What about our friends? We must know that during depression, all of our negative emotions and negative thinking cannot be resolved through just one conversation. It requires repeatedly discussing the same problems. And in their view, these are issues that are easily dealt with. So they may not have the patience, and in a different perspective, we wouldn't have the patience either. A few days ago, a friend left a message on our public account, saying: "I feel like my friends don't want to talk to me anymore, and I feel like I can't keep up with their thinking." I replied: "Actually, friends don't dislike talking to you, but when we have depression, we repeatedly talk about the same problems. Others may not have the patience anymore. From another perspective, you might lose patience with yourself too; it's not that you can't keep up with their thinking, but when we have depression, all our attention is on ourselves and we don't really listen to what they say, so it's normal that you can't keep up with their thinking. Everything will be fine when your depression is cured." This world will inevitably have imperfections, and indeed there are people who have truly hurt us. But a few people do not represent everyone. And those who hurt us may also have mental problems, or maybe we have hurt their interests in the past? Furthermore, everyone makes mistakes, including ourselves. So depression is an opportunity for us to learn to understand and forgive. 04: Make every effort to make up for past mistakes, and avoid making them again. Take the initiative to apologize. Apologizing is not giving up, but admitting past mistakes. This way, we can correct ourselves; at the same time, it helps us maintain our friendships. Perhaps our true friends have already forgiven us. Regardless, relationships are based on fate and need to be cherished. We should do our best to make up for what we can. Do what we should do and don't force others. When we apologize, some friends may still not be able to forgive us. At this moment, don't force it, just do what we can. As long as we have done what we should do, whether to forgive or not is up to others. At least, we don't need to blame ourselves anymore because the past is already in the past, regrets are futile, only lessons can be learned. A family member of a recovered patient once said, "Work hard as much as possible, and accept the outcome that comes." Yes, let's do what we should do, so that we won't feel guilty or regretful, and whether others choose to forgive or not is their business. We should just do our best, avoid making the same mistakes again. In the future, when we meet new friends on the path of life, we should learn to treat them with a sincere heart, without ulterior motives. What does it mean to have no ulterior motives and not use others? It means not caring about any return. Recall that before depression, whenever we made a new friend, didn't we always think about what benefits they could bring us? At this time, we need to adjust our thinking and not care about any returns. Because treating a person sincerely and unconditionally can be felt. The so-called "a long journey tests the horse's strength, a long time reveals a person's heart." Only with sincerity can we exchange sincerity. Relationships require hard work, and in the end, you will also receive genuine friendship. After recovering from depression, I have gained a few sincere friends. No matter what problems I encounter, they will support and help me. I really cherish these friends, and at the same time, I will do my best to support them unconditionally. I know that I have shortcomings, so I also accept their shortcomings and focus on their strengths, so I have learned to be tolerant. I know that I also have difficulties, so when they encounter difficulties, I sincerely encourage them. I know that I will also have good times, so when they are successful, I sincerely congratulate them instead of being jealous. Actually, how you treat friends can be felt by them. So, we appreciate and cherish each other. Because of them, I often feel happy; because of them, I feel empowered; because of them, I am no longer afraid in adversity; because I know they are there. So, I sincerely thank those friends who unconditionally support me. Thank you, because of you, my heart is often filled with gratitude. Friends who unconditionally support you are really rare, so we should also treat others with sincerity. This kind of friendship is more resilient than the friendship you obtain with ulterior motives. It made me reflect on what I really want after experiencing depression. Happiness is not having people cheering for you when you succeed, but having friends accompany you when you are at a low point in life.

Feeling useless and unable to solve problems, how to change one's fate?

I feel like I can't solve problems, I am overly dependent, and I'm very weak. I had a friend who told me the reason she doesn't like showing her drawings to others is because when she was younger, one time her classmates took her drawings and showed the whole class, saying they were ugly. I don't know how to help her, and I don't know how to comfort others when they cry. They always say it's nothing, but there was one time when my math teacher ignored me and I cried alone in a dark place. Then a group of boys surrounded me and laughed, saying I looked scary like a ghost. I felt so alone and misunderstood. That teacher, for me, was during a phase where I was giving up on myself, and he was the only one who didn't give up on me, along with another boy who unconditionally accepted me. I don't really like talking to them, and others think they have character issues, but because they accept me unconditionally and always respond to me, I feel like I can't live without them. As a post-2000s, I've actually enjoyed posting updates on social media since I was young. I used to think that social media could record life, interact with friends, and even vent about unhappy things. Overall, I felt that it was something meaningful. Even now, I still enjoy posting updates. However, some of my friends have told me that I share too much online, especially personal thoughts, and they think it's embarrassing. There are also friends who say that instead of building an online persona on social media, I should focus on living a good life. I now feel conflicted about posting updates because sometimes it can affect others and honestly, it doesn't seem to have much meaning. So, I'm currently in a dilemma. Sometimes, I feel like what I say might make others dislike me, but I also believe that it's the real me, and I wonder why I should care about what others think. However, I don't want others to think I'm a weird person, so I'm hesitant to express myself. After every update I post, I end up feeling conflicted and torn, especially when it's something unconventional or not in line with the social norm. I don't want to always care about what others think, but I also find it boring to constantly share irrelevant updates. How should I approach this situation?
output: Hug you~ The problem you are facing is: you love posting moments on your social media feed, but after being criticized by your friends, you start to feel conflicted. On one hand, you still enjoy sharing your life and thoughts through posting, but on the other hand, you start questioning the necessity of sharing these moments. In my opinion, the real dilemma you are facing is whether to be true to yourself or to care about what others think and hide a part of yourself. "Moments" on social media are originally a platform for sharing and documenting your life and thoughts. You can treat it as a record or as a means of sharing. I don't understand why your "friends" would judge such a simple act of posting moments as "building a persona." If I were to ponder whether or not each moment is worth sharing before posting, wouldn't that be creating a persona? In your case, you simply want to document your life and share what you want to share, so how can it be considered creating a persona? You mentioned being conflicted and trapped by the opinions of others, perhaps because their words have made you overthink. Sometimes, overthinking hinders our progress. Instead, it's better to simplify things and think about why we started posting moments in the first place and whether what we are doing now contradicts our initial intentions. If it doesn't, then bravely continue doing it. How we correctly listen to others' opinions is a lifelong lesson that requires constant reflection and learning. Others' evaluations may not necessarily reflect objective facts since their opinions are influenced by their subjective consciousness. Therefore, we need to think independently and develop our own sense of right and wrong. You are a kind, lovely, and life-loving person, so don't let the thoughts of a few individuals discourage your passion for life. Although I personally differ from you in terms of posting moments, I don't believe that my way is right and your way is wrong, nor do I have any intention of controlling or changing you. On the other hand, it seems like your "friend" aggressively wants to change the way you live, and I hope you seriously consider this.

First, you need to relax psychologically and not force yourself to let go quickly or immediately. Give yourself the mental suggestion that "not being able to let go" is not necessarily a bad or serious thing. It can sometimes have positive effects, such as being more cautious and reflective in facing new relationships. For example, cultivating hobbies to divert your attention, talking to friends to get different perspectives, seeking opportunities to interact with the opposite sex to expand your social circle, or even seeking help is also an option. I want to study and read more books, but I can't finish reading them. What should I do if I can't calm down?

Although I am a beginner, I still have an eager heart for learning sometimes. I hope to study well. Whenever I want to learn, my mind becomes chaotic and I can't focus. What should I do?
output:
Let me tell you two stories. The first story is one that I heard from Teacher Huang Zhangjin. He said that during the Sino-Vietnamese border war in the 1980s, many soldiers who had stayed in the frontline bunkers for a long time could recite the instructions for using medicated oil by heart. The instructions on the bottle were printed in incredibly small letters, with nearly 2000 words packed onto it. Some soldiers also memorized the instructions for skin ointment, which only had about 400 words, and they could recite it backwards. It was truly impressive.

The second story happened in 2008 when I took a train from Changchun to Wuhan. I was on a green train, which took 39 hours to reach the destination. It was my first time on such a long train journey, and I was alone and introverted. There were no beautiful women around to strike up a conversation with, and even if there were, I wouldn't have dared. Back then, mobile phones didn't have as many functions, and internet access wasn't as easy as it is now. Therefore, those 39 hours were truly arduous. At first, I could still enjoy the scenery and sleep a bit, but as time went on, I became increasingly bored. I had brought only one book with me, "Research Methods in Psychology." Just by looking at the title, you know it's a dry book. When I couldn't bear it any longer, I finally took out the book and started reading, surprisingly finding it less boring and even engaging. By the time I got off the train, I had finished several chapters. In the past, the basic contradiction in our mental life was between the growing demand for mental stimulation and the scarcity of activities to satisfy it. Now things are different – a smartphone can solve this contradiction, offering countless ways to pass the time. So, I had a revelation – if I want to read more books and learn more, I need to create an environment that is boring enough to make me crave reading and studying as a way to kill time. Though it may sound extreme, the results are remarkable. So, how can you achieve this? It's actually very simple. Phase 1: Bring the book you want to read, but leave your computer and phone behind. Go to the library or any other suitable place for studying. Limit your water intake to avoid going to the restroom, and set a small goal for yourself: "I, XXX, will sit here for three hours." During these three hours, you don't have to study at all – that's not a problem. But remember, you absolutely cannot do anything else, just sit there and endure it. Soon enough, your instinctual resistance to boredom will make you start studying. Phase 2: For this phase, you don't need to go to the library or leave your computer and phone behind. Anytime you want to start studying or working, apply the principle of "for the next period of time, I will only do this one thing, even if I don't do it, I will sit here without doing anything else" – don't strive for perfection, just remember, don't do anything else. Based on experience, after a while of feeling bored, daydreaming, and being distracted, you will return to focusing on your current study material. We often think that we need to calm our minds before we can read, but that's not the case. This method will force you to start reading with an extremely restless mind, and eventually, your mind will calm down. Interested friends can give it a try.

I don't know what to do, but I have grown accustomed to this person over the past few months.
output: Hello, OP: The internet has indeed brought us a lot of conveniences and changes in our lives, including dating. However, the internet is virtual, and we cannot fully trust each other without actually meeting. So, I think your concerns are very necessary in this regard. Let's talk about your relationship: you have known each other online for more than two months and have had enjoyable conversations. He keeps you updated on his work, what he eats, etc. There is mutual attraction and you have both expressed liking each other. He always wants to video chat with you, even during his few minutes of lunch break. But whenever you talk about gender relations and being together in the future, you feel fear and afraid of being deceived. So, OP, have you ever been deceived or hurt by someone in relationships or other aspects before? Because chatting normally with each other but feeling fear when it comes to gender relations and defining the relationship might be triggered by recalling some unpleasant experiences and creating an instinctive reaction. If it is indeed because of past experiences, OP should face this issue head-on. Take some proper psychological tests and analysis to overcome the fear in your mind so that you can better face life. Of course, if you are simply afraid of the internet's unreliability, afraid that the other person is not sincere or has ulterior motives, there is no need to be overly scared either. Because we are currently in a society governed by the rule of law, as long as you learn to protect yourself and have your own judgement, there shouldn't be any major problems. For example, when you first meet the other person, you can bring your friends or best friends along and choose relatively safe public places. Avoid being alone or engaging in intimate activities when meeting for the first time because there is a difference between the internet and reality. You need to further understand the other person in real life to avoid being deceived. If the other person truly likes you, they will surely understand. As for going on trips after defining the relationship, I think the condition is that you have lived together in real life for a period of time before making that decision. Otherwise, if you go out together without truly knowing each other, you won't have anyone around to ask for help in case of an unexpected situation. I hope these suggestions can be helpful to OP, and I also hope that OP can find happiness. You are a good girl who deserves a beautiful love.

output: I understand that you want to quickly resolve your state or problem, but I think it needs to be divided into two judgments. 🤩 It requires someone to take responsibility for the visitor. 🤩 For me, sometimes if the client is in a state of depression or even a more serious state with suicidal tendencies, then we cannot judge: - Whose consultation is ineffective? - Whose consultation is effective? - Who is responsible for this emotional loss of control? - Who is responsible for this crisis? These two cannot be separated: one person to solve emotions, one person to solve problems. Problems and emotions are like twin sisters. We also need to see what uncontrollable emotions are brought about by the problem for this visitor. How to solve this problem and emotion requires us to work diligently on both fronts. 🤩 Work with the visitor, not just their problems and phenomena. Our goal in working with visitors is to accompany them in facing themselves, facing the outside world, and facing problems that may arise at any time, rather than just solving the problems and emotions they are currently facing. I don't know if I should expose him now, and I don't know how to deal with him.
output: Hello, dear! Whether you catch your child cheating on assignments or exams "on the spot" or "discover it secretly behind their back" will determine how you approach and educate them about not cheating and make them aware of the seriousness of cheating. If it's the former, you can directly guide and educate your child not to cheat, helping them realize the gravity of cheating. If it's the latter, avoid direct confrontations or conflicts with your child. During their 8th-grade year, children are usually going through an adolescent rebellious phase, so generating emotional conflicts may not be conducive to resolving the issue of cheating or forming their personality during this period. First, try to understand why your child is cheating instead of criticizing them outright. If it is due to high expectations, many parents tend to have high expectations for their children, and in such cases, children may seek shortcuts in their studies. At times like these, parents can appropriately lower their expectations to avoid imposing excessive psychological pressure on their children's studies. Comparing children's academic performance is a good thing as it enhances competitive awareness among classmates and helps foster a desire to study. However, this should be based on a "formal" competitive system. Inform your child that the purpose of learning is not solely to achieve a specific result but that learning is an endless process. Encourage them to face problems rather than ignore them. Learning is a gradual process, building upon one step at a time. Positively guide your child about the seriousness of cheating, encouraging them to actively tackle the problem instead of attempting to deceive others by putting up a false display of "perfect scores." Solution: Regularly supervise your child's study progress If you notice signs of your child ignoring problems, you can allocate regular time frames to supervise their study progress. It could be checking their daily progress every evening or conducting weekly assessments, etc. Divide the semester into segments and conduct periodic assessments for subjects in which your child has cheated. Positively guide your child about the seriousness of cheating Engage in discussions with your child about the topic of "academic cheating." This topic is important for your child's growth and can be combined with real-life news cases to help guide your child to distinguish between cooperative learning and cheating. During conversations with your child, who is going through the rebellious stage of adolescence, they may appear irritable and impatient. Avoid emotional conflicts, control your own emotions, and calmly discuss these issues with your child. During the adolescent stage, children exhibit distinct characteristics and have their own thoughts and opinions. They do not want to be constrained by other people's thoughts, including their parents' advice, even if it is for their own good. It is difficult for them to listen carefully to their inner thoughts. Allow rebellious children to make mistakes, as this is a crucial period for them to form their own convictions. It is natural for them to make small mistakes. Do not overly restrict their freedom unless the problem is very serious or beyond your ability as parents, as long as it does not involve illegal activities. Let them face and solve some problems on their own instead of telling them what they "cannot do" or "should not do." Adolescents often realize the correctness of their own convictions through making mistakes.

According to the perspective of psychology, a person's fundamental personality is largely stable. In your description, the different aspects of yourself before and after junior high school actually indicate that your fundamental personality has not changed. It is your innocence that led to the distress of being afraid of being disliked. How should we understand this kind of innocent personality? Actually, we can say that you have a kind and pure perspective, expecting others to behave in a kind and pure way towards you. However, due to the complex reasons of personality and environment, others did not respond to you in the same friendly manner, which eventually led to the frustration and development of your inferiority complex, and the thought of wanting to die as a way to escape. Your fundamental nature is innocent, but because you care about others' opinions, you put on two different masks for the purpose of gaining positive evaluations from others. Therefore, overall, what you need to improve at this stage is not living for others and suppressing your own true needs to meet others' expectations. Actually, at this stage, you need to adjust your mindset and experience positive and optimistic emotions, in order to face the present and future difficulties. You also need to restore self-identity, be confident in yourself, in order to feel your own thoughts and needs, and put yourself first, thus completely breaking free from negative evaluations from others. Now, let's talk about the issue that is troubling you, whether or not your past behavior of wearing masks is right or wrong. Actually, this question makes you feel like you can't find the real you. First of all, according to psychology, people will wear different masks in different situations and environments in order to meet the needs of the environment and social interactions. So, wearing masks to face others is actually a normal and acceptable behavior, and not just for you, many people in reality also use masks. Therefore, you don't need to deny yourself because of this and deepen your sense of inferiority. Before, you used a careless personality which was disliked by others, and then you learned to be quiet. You need to have a clear understanding that none of this is your fault. The careless and quiet personality traits you exhibited were actually efforts made to have friendly interactions with others. However, for students of the same age as you, their minds are not yet mature enough to understand these efforts made for friendship. They only see the surface phenomena. So, you don't need to spend energy blaming anyone; this kind of blaming is not meaningful. What you need to do is to appreciate yourself and affirm your past behaviors. If you like someone, you can try to develop the relationship; if you don't, give the other person some indications and reject them tactfully. It's better to have a short-term pain than a long-term one. Avoiding is actually a vague response that can lead to misunderstandings. Don't drag it out for too long. The longer it takes, the harder it may be for the other person to move on, and it may also become more difficult for you to speak up. It wastes both the other person's time and your own, and the future relationship may become more awkward. Lastly, if someone likes you, it means that you have qualities that attract others and deserve their admiration. From this perspective, being liked by someone is actually a good thing. Every time my mother says something, I feel like jumping off a building. I truly hate my mother, I hate that she gave birth to me. I'm so tired. I feel like a clown. Every day, I try my best to appear normal, work hard, and treat the people around me well, hoping to gradually become better. But it's so difficult. Every day, I cry, tears flow uncontrollably. It's so hard. I'm sorry.
output: Hugs to you for being in such a difficult period. Thank you for being willing to come to this platform to confide in us and allowing us the chance to offer you support. It sounds like you are currently in a very lonely and confused state. There is no one around who can understand the hardships you are going through and the emotions you are experiencing. Your family is unable to respond to you and provide you with warmth and support. Additionally, you are facing significant pressure at work and in your personal life. In this situation, it is possible for us to experience sustained feelings of sadness, lack of focus, and disrupted sleep and appetite, which can also affect our work. From your description, it seems that recent major changes have occurred and there have been some changes in your life, such as starting work. When we encounter major changes in life and find it difficult to adjust, feeling lost and lacking support can lead us to a low point. In this stage, I hope we don't be too hard on ourselves. We could try to tell ourselves that we are currently in a difficult period, but there will be a day when the difficulties will pass and our wounds will slowly heal. We can try to replace negative thoughts such as "nothing will ever get better" and "I will always be in pain" with positive self-suggestions like "difficulties will pass" and "I will be able to overcome this pain". We can write them down or say them to ourselves before getting up and before going to bed, giving ourselves these affirmations. This can help us regain confidence and a sense of control. How can we better alleviate our emotions and break free from a negative cycle? It may require us to change the way we perceive negative events and how we respond to them. Perhaps we are now afraid of our mother's phone calls and have internalized her negative emotions and family issues as our own sources of stress and negative feelings. When we fully accept and internalize them, we may easily feel overwhelmed and drained. By setting an invisible boundary and telling ourselves that our mother is a separate individual, we cannot transform ourselves into her and solve all her problems. Accepting the existence of boundaries and recognizing that everyone has their own limitations and worries can allow us to stop burdening ourselves with our mother's troubles. This may help us gradually learn not to see our mother's phone calls and voice as sources of pressure or to transfer this pain, and even learn to say no. Of course, I understand that everyone has their own concerns, and perhaps your conscience doesn't allow you to ignore your mother's calls, or you have put a lot of pressure on yourself to meet others' needs. However, just as it is mentioned in the safety instructions when we board an airplane - we need to put on our own oxygen masks first before helping others. Similarly, we need to learn to take care of our own physical and mental well-being first so that we can respond to those around us with full energy. Before that, we can adopt some ways to show others our boundaries and communicate our more important needs that require attention. Learning to prioritize ourselves and care for ourselves is a topic we need to gradually learn. I hope this is helpful to you. If you have any questions, feel free to interact with me.

I originally wanted to see him again, but when I see him, I don't know what to do, and it feels indescribable. I hope he's doing well and that I don't leave a lasting negative impact on him. Seeing his profile picture, which is from when we were together, brings up an indescribable feeling. I feel like if I want to do something, it's better to do it soon, or else it will feel like a scar that's harder to heal. What should I do?
output: OP, here's a comforting hug for you. You and your partner broke up, but what was the reason for it, and is there hope for reconciliation? I feel like neither of you have truly moved on from each other, and it seems like there are unresolved regrets and unfinished business that have become deep emotional wounds. Your idea is correct - complete all the things pertaining to this relationship, without leaving any regrets or scars that will continue to hurt when mentioned. Only by completing these things can you truly say goodbye to this relationship. I noticed that you have mentioned a phenomenon of avoiding contact. Now that you're aware of this, try to understand yourself first, accept yourself, and why such a phenomenon has occurred and formed. Then, try to communicate with him and explain to him. Make an effort for him to understand you. If he truly loves and cares for you, he will find a way to truly understand you and most importantly, he will cherish you. He won't think about leaving you because of this characteristic or anything of that sort, if he truly loves you. Regardless of whether you are preparing to reconcile or let go, it is important to address this unfinished business. This is a technique from "Gestalt Therapy" called "unfinished business." It emphasizes fully learning, understanding, and experiencing the present moment. Every event in life, big or small, especially when it comes to love relationships, can only be truly absorbed and experienced when we complete every step and say goodbye to the past, moving towards the next stage. However, sometimes, when things are suddenly interrupted, the unfinished business continues to persist, and sometimes it may take a lifetime to make up for it. For example, if a loved one leaves without saying goodbye or if we constantly fail to obtain something we like. In contrast, there is the completeness of an event. In one's life, we are constantly pursuing complete experiences. Once the "unfinished business" is formed, the usual methods of correction are catharsis and compensation. Unfinished business often persists until individuals are brave enough to face and deal with these unexpressed emotions. Only by increasing awareness of one's current state, recognizing and clearing repressed emotions and needs, can one integrate the fragmented parts of their personality and achieve a complete self. 1. Improve self-awareness. Pay attention to your interactions with others in life and work, enhance self-awareness of your emotions, thoughts, bodily sensations, beliefs, and behavioral manifestations, in order to avoid self-defeat and achieve personal growth. 2. Learn to face and accept your past, find constructive ways to solve problems, practice positive attributions, and reduce the negative impact of "unfinished business." 3. Continuously improve oneself through lifelong learning. Should you try to reconcile or let go as soon as possible? The following four questions can help you clarify your thoughts and make the best choice for yourself. Question 1: Are the issues that led to the breakup not crossing any boundaries and can be resolved? Question 2: Do you want to return to this relationship because you genuinely like them? Question 3: Are you truly willing to invest time and effort in rebuilding the relationship? Question 4: Is your partner just as willing as you to make an effort to fix this relationship?

There will be many bends on the track of life, going on stage is the best proof of strength, so if you get passed on a bend, it doesn't mean you change course or quit. But when they make amends, my heart softens and I think they're not so bad after all, taking further steps to be friendly with them. I feel disappointed in myself, lacking resilience and determination. I shine when others give me a little attention. Sigh, what have I experienced in my childhood? How come I am so afraid of being isolated?
output: Hello, considering what you have been through, it is understandable that you are feeling this way. You are someone who reflects and is aware, and I believe you will find your own answers in the future and not be so entangled. It is normal to feel upset when being bullied and afraid of being isolated. Everyone experiences this. We live in a society where we interact with various types of people, so differences and harmony are inevitable. It is also impossible for us to sever contact with people around us, as there are material or existential needs aside from our psychological ones. It seems like you hope to express anger, dissatisfaction, and your own feelings and emotions when you are treated unfairly. But it seems like you are able to endure. In that case, you should consider why you endure and what you are afraid of. What will happen if you express yourself? You are conflicted about reconciling with those who have hurt you and even seek to please them. You do feel the other person's kindness when they are good to you, so it is normal to treat them well in return. It shows that you are very tolerant. However, you also need to consider whether the boundaries in your relationships are unclear and whether you find it difficult to establish your own boundaries or don't know where they are. Suggestions: 1. Examine the patterns between yourself and your parents, whether you have experienced the feeling of being ignored, treated harshly, or not being liked, and whether this has been internalized into your psyche and generalized to your relationships with others as an adult, making it difficult for you to express your true feelings, especially unpleasant ones. 2. Try to establish your boundaries with people around you or those you feel safe with, express your dissatisfaction, because only when you express it will others know and care. They will be more careful next time. If someone knows you are upset but still insists on doing it, then stay away from such people, because they don't care about your feelings, only their own pleasure. 3. You can also discuss with your parents or find a friend to confide in about your emotions. Releasing emotions is necessary to deal with the problem and handle relationships well. Establish boundaries, express dissatisfaction, and respect your own feelings.
