output: Hello, I happened to come across your question while listening to "Like Someone Like Me..." on my headphones that day. I can understand your frustration. Who is truly content with mediocrity? It's just a way to console ourselves in the face of harsh reality. I hope my answer can help you: 1. We can distinguish right from wrong, and we are not truly content with mediocrity. We just cannot resist temptation. (a) Others have achieved something while you have nothing, and you feel defeated in comparison. Your current feeling of "despondency" is a punishment to yourself. Maybe you have lost interest in studying, life has lost its flavor, and work is just getting by. If you continue like this, you will become more and more numb. There is a voice in your heart fighting against this, unwilling to silently live like this. That's why you are filled with a sense of crisis. You don't want to be the same as everyone else, you are unwilling. But there are still three big mountains in front of you: work, study, and life. You know you can't be like the old man in the fable, causing earth-shattering changes. Therefore, you are in pain. (b) You feel very inferior. This kind of inferiority makes you suffer, leading to self-deprecation and even self-abandonment. Many times, people belittle themselves because they have never received objective affirmation. People who have long had a sense of inferiority rarely receive recognition. Usually, only insecure people cannot objectively evaluate themselves. Facing various challenges, you repeatedly fail, and we can feel your frustration. Because the current you did not live up to the image of your dreams. The reason you are unhappy is probably related to the way you were raised in your family environment. Maybe you have grown up in an oppressive educational model since childhood, and no matter how hard you try, your family and teachers have not given you enough love. As a result, you have developed an "emotional void" as an adult, and you desperately try to fill it without success. 2. Your subconscious is struggling, you are just getting by during the day, but at night, it's hard to avoid feeling lonely. It's as if there are two people tearing apart your soul and making you unhappy. I can understand your pain. I'm also almost 30 years old and have not achieved much. Facing the pressure of getting married from various relatives, and the sighs of my parents, I always feel helpless and sad. Every time night falls and I'm alone at home, I start to doubt myself, wondering if my life is destined to be so lonely and helpless? Later, I gradually let go of the burden in my heart, because I know that the more I suffer, the more my actions will contradict my desires. It is like giving you a piece of paper with a small black dot on it, and you keep staring at that black dot, forgetting that you have countless blank spaces to explore. So, to change your destiny, the first thing you need to do is to reacquaint yourself with who you truly are, learn to appreciate yourself, and make peace with yourself. I advise you to give yourself some time. Try to examine yourself and understand your strengths and weaknesses. Evaluate yourself objectively. Only when you learn to appreciate yourself, will you become confident. Second, life is not something you rent. Even if you are dissatisfied with your work, you should work diligently and achieve a sense of accomplishment step by step. It's already difficult to survive in this world, and if you continue to feel sorry for yourself, your life will become even more challenging. I suggest you actively adjust your mindset and give yourself some time. Seriously write down your strengths, and tell yourself that you deserve to be loved and treated well. Don't think you are not worthy of happiness, you deserve all the happiness in the world. Don't bring the frustrations of work and study back home. Learn to balance work and relaxation every day. After work, you can go out with a few friends for a relaxing spa, or soak your feet at night to relax. Don't let frustrations linger overnight. Learn to balance work and rest. You need to make an effort to explore and develop your potential to become a charismatic person. I know you have tried many hobbies, but you always get discouraged and give up. You need to understand that everyone has different talents, and finding a hobby that suits you takes time and effort. I hope you don't give up on your hopes so easily. Besides singing and dancing, there are many things you can try. You can learn and appreciate tea ceremonies, try getting involved in art, or try running... and so on. Don't lose your expectations for yourself. All the good things are waiting for you in the not-too-distant future. Lastly, "Someone as outstanding as me should have lived a brilliant life. It's not too late for anything. Thank you for reading, and I hope you will give it a thumbs up. Welcome to follow the author: Ms. Liu, the Panda.

My ex told me after our breakup that he was happy and moved being with me, but he didn't have romantic feelings. In this relationship, I carefully remembered his preferences, occasionally prepared surprises for him, and showed him all the tenderness and thoughtfulness I could offer. When he said that, I felt like a blow. A friend who knew I had just gone through a breakup confessed their feelings to me, but I didn't have any feelings for them, so I explained my thoughts and suggested we remain friends, to which they agreed. However, the next day, I discovered that they had blocked me. It feels like no one truly likes me, and they only see me as someone kind and considerate to be a girlfriend when they feel lonely or empty. They all want to try dating me, even if it means the confession fails. I feel so hurt. Am I not important? Are my feelings not important?
output: Hello, I understand your feelings. When you were with your ex, you always remembered his preferences, surprised him, and were considerate and gentle. But in the end, you were broken up and received the words "no feeling of love." I know this must have made you very upset. When your friend confessed to you, after you confessed that you had no feelings for him, he thought he was being rejected. Perhaps he also felt hurt, so he refused to be friends with you. You think that he also didn't really like you. It seems that the attitudes of these two guys are confirming a subconscious belief of yours: I am not worth being liked, and no one truly likes me. But looking at these two guys from another perspective, you may discover something new: 1. When you were with your ex, you need to think back and see if you respected your own feelings in that relationship. Was your effort something that he needed? Were you giving without expecting anything in return, or did you expect him to reciprocate in order to feel validated? When he didn't give you the response you wanted, you felt disappointed and unwilling. 2. Was your friend truly a sincere friend before confessing to you? After the failed confession, did he have the right to protect his own feelings and not be friends with you anymore? The premise of love is self-love. When you can respect your own thoughts in any relationship and not compromise yourself, you won't need to seek acceptance from others by pleasing them or determine whether you are worthy of love based on their reactions towards you. Furthermore, relationships are maintained through attraction and mutual understanding. When you can prioritize self-love and focus more on yourself, you can improve yourself and make the other person willingly and voluntarily contribute to you. So, you are important, and you deserve to be treated well. Best wishes.

I like a girl, but suddenly, I don't know how to make a decision when looking back on the past.

I recently developed a liking for a girl and it's bothering me. I don't know if she is seeing someone or how she feels about me. At the same time, I have a good relationship with another girl, but it seems like I just can't develop that kind of liking for her. As I was thinking about it, I suddenly recalled two similar experiences I had in high school. Both times, there was a girl who liked me and our relationship was ambiguous, but at the same time, I would develop feelings for another girl. I don't know if it's because of the pressure or because I'm weak, but from my previous experiences, I regretted rejecting the girls who liked me and they suddenly became very attractive to me, yet I couldn't get close to them again... I don't know what choice to make now. Should I give it a try with the girl who likes me? Or should I continue pursuing the girl I currently have a 'feeling' for (even though it seems like she's out of reach)?
output: "What you need is not these two girls, but facing yourself. Confused people tend to create ambiguity because they don't even know what they want. First of all, the fear of rejection is actually the fear of facing your own insecurities and lack of confidence, being afraid of being rejected by others. A man who knows what kind of girl he wants will usually have the courage to ask the other person if they already have a partner. If they don't, he will try to pursue them; if they do, he will immediately let go and find someone else. He is straightforward, even if he is rejected, he knows the answer. But what about you? You are afraid of being rejected, prefer to waste your own and other people's time, and stay in an ambiguous relationship. You are willing to waste time and procrastinate rather than face the truth. You lack the courage to face reality and lack confidence in dealing with rejection. If you find out that the other person has a partner, you feel like you are not good enough, so the other person didn't choose you. If that's the case, you are avoiding facing yourself, afraid of facing your own insecurities. Second, ambiguity is not love. 1. Love is not a cure for your deficiencies. We all enjoy being loved, even if we know we don't like that person, we still want them to like us. Why? We yearn for attention, care, and love from someone. But love is not a tool for healing, using someone else's admiration to heal yourself without loving them back is taking advantage of them. 2. Wasting someone else's time and emotions is equivalent to invading their boundaries because time and emotions belong to someone else, and it's only fair to respect them as you would want yours to be respected. 3. Loving someone is about fulfilling them and wishing them well, not worrying about whether you will fail. If you find out that the other person has a partner and you truly love her, you would congratulate her and be happy for her. Many people have the misconception that jealousy is a manifestation of love. Jealousy is only about possession and wanting to have someone, but that's not love. If you really liked these two girls so much, I think you would have confessed your feelings long ago. Third, what you need is not these two girls, but facing yourself. 1. Facing your insecurities makes you react negatively to the outside world, which leads to your avoidance and procrastination. Solution: Use daily journaling to record the areas where you deserve praise until you develop positive reactions to the outside world. No longer feeling insecure, taking responsibility for your actions, and recognizing your inner worth. 2. Independent satisfaction of your emotional needs. Respect your emotional needs and learn to satisfy them independently. Understand the emotional needs behind all your motives and learn to satisfy them independently, rather than seeking emotions from others through ambiguity. 3. Think about what you really want. Everyone experiences confusion, but ambiguity is definitely not the way out or the solution. Think about whether you want a relationship to fulfill your own needs or if you genuinely love someone. Because love is about giving and gratitude, not about taking and entitlement. When someone's emotions become independent, you really don't need to seek love through taking advantage or being selfish. I remember a famous psychotherapist said: 'Immature love says, "I love you because I need you." Mature love says, "I need you because I love you."' If you truly love someone, you don't need to worry about being rejected because you will fulfill and wish them well. If you truly love yourself, you don't need to fear rejection because even if the outside world rejects you, it doesn't define you. You are who you are, and whether the outside world rejects you or not has nothing to do with your worth. Your existence itself is an achievement. Love yourself, and at the same time, cherish the people who like you. Wishing you well, namaste!"

For example, if your family compliments your sister's beautiful eyelids, remember that beauty is not just external, it also comes from within. If you cannot generate confidence externally, try to cultivate your own temperament and talents. However, it is important to understand that following other people's evaluations and opinions will not help you find your own path. For example, if someone tells us today that all our features are good, but our nose is a little big, you might fixate on that aspect, becoming very agitated internally until one day, you get surgery. This applies not only to appearance but also when people clash with our values and beliefs. If their suggestions or opinions are objective and rational, then we should strive to improve ourselves. However, if we believe we are worthless because of such suggestions from others, this kind of perception needs to change. Best wishes.

How to reject some overly friendly people?

There are a few people in the workplace, mostly women. Whenever they encounter a problem, they would complain about how they cannot handle it and the leaders would easily agree to their requests, sometimes even assigning the tasks to me. They seem very righteous, but in my opinion, these are not big issues and they shouldn't make such a fuss. How should I deal with these kinds of people?
output: Hi OP. Seeing your description, this is indeed a troubling issue. Sending you a virtual hug! I believe you know that having boundaries is necessary in interpersonal relationships. Boundaries can make our relationships more stable and balanced, and they are especially important in the workplace. For example, clear division of responsibilities is a form of boundaries. I won't elaborate on these things that I think you already know, because your concern is "how" to refuse. You want to know how to say no without being disturbed and without offending your leaders and colleagues. Here are some thoughts on how to say no: daring to refuse is difficult for many of us. We always worry that saying no is impolite or cold-hearted. But if we never learn to refuse, we will become more and more boundaryless. We will waste too much time and energy on unnecessary things, and force ourselves to do things we don't want to do or feel we shouldn't do, which will bring feelings of suppression and various negative emotions. So practicing saying no is a required course. In the process of practicing saying no, we also gradually build our courage and become more clear about what we want and what we don't want. We gradually understand and see what we truly think deep in our hearts. We also become more willing to fight for ourselves. Saying no is an important step in helping us become ourselves. When refusing, we should be decisive. We are used to not refusing, so when we start practicing saying no, there is always self-blame and doubt when refusing others. We feel guilty, unsure, and uncertain. Therefore, our refusals are always ambiguous or lack confidence, such as "Let me see if I can do it for you," or "Let me try, but I can't guarantee if I can help." But if we consider these as refusals, we not only make it difficult for ourselves but also hinder others. Because the other person will assume that you have agreed, and if you can't complete it on time due to various reasons, and the other person can't do it themselves in time, not only will you feel guilty, but the other person will also be angry, and it will also delay things and time. Therefore, once we have made up our minds and determined that "I want to refuse this matter, I don't want to do it," a firm refusal is the best choice for both parties: - Accepting our own limitations, "I'm sorry, I really want to help you, but I can't." - Purely not wanting to help: "I'm sorry, I can't help/I can't do it!" You don't always have to find a reason to tell others or convince yourself to have the confidence to refuse. You have the confidence and freedom to say no, so you can refuse without any reason and dare to refuse. This will also earn the respect of others. After a few times, your colleagues and leaders might think to themselves, "Oh, OP has become more capable." They will know that you have boundaries and principles. If your leader is smart, they will definitely see your growth in this aspect and appreciate and value you more. Having boundaries can also provide flexibility. After we learn and dare to refuse, we can have some flexibility based on our feelings and circumstances. Does having flexibility mean not refusing and accepting everything? No, this flexibility is not about sacrificing and not daring to refuse anymore. Now we can refuse with peace of mind. We can choose to help or not. Regardless of our choice, we can be at peace with ourselves. Our inner psychological flexibility will also increase. I hope this is helpful to you. Blessings to you: Smooth sailing in your career! The world and I love you.

My boyfriend has been showing signs of depression recently. He doesn't want to talk and just wants to be alone and do nothing. It has been going on for a while now. What can I do to help him? Should I try to cheer him up or just let him be and stay quiet?
output: Hello, there is a movie called "Husband with Depression" that I recommend you to watch. The production team specially invited a psychiatric expert as a consultant to ensure that there are no medical inaccuracies in the film. This movie realistically portrays the life of an individual and a couple dealing with depression, for example: #The wife learns a lot of knowledge to understand what depression is, its symptoms, and how to treat the patient. #The wife accompanies her husband to quit his job and experiences the daily agony of crowded subway commutes, saying, "I finally realize how hard it is for you to go to work every day. Thank you for all these years." Upon hearing this, the husband feels understood and bursts into tears on the subway. #After quitting his job, the husband attempts suicide in the bathroom due to feeling neglected and impatient by the wife who is busy with her comic drawings. Thankfully, the wife saves him, and they both cry and embrace each other. I feel that my parents are Graland. What should I do?

I'm 26 years old, and since I was young, my parents have always been obsessed with money and constantly instilled in me the idea that spending money is sinful. According to the Engel coefficient, our family is considered well-off, but our quality of life is even worse than that of an average family who can afford basic needs. I always feel that my parents love money more than they love me, and because of this, I have harbored a lot of hatred towards them. When I was young, I didn't have much pocket money. It wasn't until middle school that my parents started giving me a little bit. In high school, I only received 400 yuan as monthly allowance, and in my first and second year of university, I only had 500 yuan per month. Elementary and middle school education was free, and in high school, I had a scholarship, so education didn't cost much. When I graduated from university, my parents stopped providing for me. I had to earn and spend money by myself. Previously, I spent 16,000 yuan on a preparatory course for postgraduate studies, which was my own money. In addition to that, I had to pay the mortgage. As a result, my savings were depleted. I had no choice but to ask my parents for money, but the way they looked at me was as if I were asking for their flesh and blood. It made me feel really uncomfortable. Am I not their daughter? I didn't ask for much, just 800 yuan. I just don't understand why it's so difficult for me, while people my age around me seem to ask their parents for money as easily as drinking water.
output: The author's experience is really similar to mine. I am already in my 30s, but the influence from my parents still exists. However, unlike the author, I was the one assimilated, while the author had different opinions and I truly admire that. I have a younger brother and my mom often praises me to others, saying that XX (me) doesn't spend money recklessly like XX (my brother) who spends money all the time. When I was young, parents were everything, so whatever they said was right. I always had this thought that spending money recklessly was wrong and asking parents for money was wrong too. In high school, when I lost some money, I managed to survive with 10 yuan for 7 days, and I didn't feel miserable at all. In fact, I was proud of myself for saving money for the family. I didn't realize this issue until I started dating my partner. I don't not love her, I do love her. I have always had part-time jobs and I give all my salary to her. However, I can't stand going out to eat together. She is a very bourgeois girl and always chooses expensive places to eat. Actually, with our salaries, we can afford it, but I feel extremely uncomfortable and even get angry. But I know deep down that she is right, I have no reason to get angry at her. I was also confused about where my anger was coming from. Later, after some introspection, I realized that I was brainwashed since childhood, brainwashed by my parents. When we go out to eat, at a subconscious level, I would think my partner did something wrong. But at a conscious level, I know there's no issue. For a long time, when we go out, she would eat something nice and I would choose the cheapest option for myself. I love her, but if I hadn't studied psychology, I might have ended up like your parents. I think what hurt the most for the author is feeling that their parents don't love them. No matter who experiences this, it is a very painful thing. And it is indeed the case, if they are not willing to spend money on you, how can they claim to love you? When I was in college, I read the Analects of Confucius and there was a story about Confucius borrowing an umbrella. When it rained and Confucius and his disciples passed by Zixia's house, someone suggested borrowing an umbrella from Zixia. But as soon as Confucius heard it, he said, "No, Zixia is quite stingy. If I borrow it, he won't give it to me, and others will think he disrespects his teacher. If he does give it to me, he will definitely be heartbroken." Nobody is perfect, everyone's situation is different, and the standard for measuring love should also be diverse. Besides money, did your parents make you feel loved in other ways? Did they give you money when you needed it despite being stingy? If they did, then maybe you can forgive or accept your stingy parents. But if they didn't, why should we accept parents who don't love us?

My boyfriend is currently twenty-five years old. He used to work on a construction site, earning a decent income but suffering from the hardships and having a poor mental well-being. Therefore, he wants to switch jobs. However, starting a new job means a significant income gap compared to his previous job, and he is afraid to take this step. How can I help him?
output: The only thing you need to do to help him is to encourage him to meet new people. If he is the one asking questions, there can be many opportunities for further discussion. But since you are the one being asked, and not directly involved, you don't need to do too much. In my opinion, the two of you have probably discussed everything you could on a rational level, but he hasn't made a firm decision yet, indicating that he is not emotionally prepared. Why should he meet new people? And what kind of people should he meet? These two questions cannot be explained logically. Since he is not emotionally prepared, you need to start from an emotional perspective and use the life he aspires to as a way to motivate his determination. So, it's not just about finding anyone to introduce him to a different lifestyle; it's about finding people who lead the kind of life he aspires to and have similar experiences. Actually, when deciding if a job is what you want, you can look at someone around you who has a similar background and see if the life they are currently living is what you want. Now what you need to do is encourage him to have these kind of people around him. Because knowing these people personally will enhance the sense of connection to this kind of life, and it will be easier for him to believe that he can also achieve it, thus taking the first step to improve his current life. Of course, meeting these people doesn't mean he can proceed without any concerns, so you may still need to discuss some rational aspects. For example, how much salary difference can he accept after changing jobs? How long can he tolerate this gap? Which cities should he consider working in to reduce the gap? There are many questions that you need to discuss again. For now, what you need to do is encourage him to broaden his horizons and see more possibilities in life. Meeting new people is one of the most direct ways, and he can participate in online activities to meet more people. When he faces the job change with a positive attitude, you can also discuss other topics such as building personal competitive advantages, but that involves other content.

Our behaviors are influenced by various factors, including our own personalities, ways of thinking, and the environment we are in. Moreover, the same person may have different behavioral responses to different things, or even to the same thing at different times. These are all normal things. Whether we sympathize or take pleasure in others' suffering depends on rational and moral considerations. As for our emotional response, it varies from person to person. We say we should sympathize with others and be kind, which is more about rational thinking and moral perspective. Let's take a specific example. For instance, if someone accidentally bumps into you while you're walking down the street, you may still feel angry. Or you may feel the pain from being bumped. Whether it is anger or pain, it is a fact that cannot be changed and is your genuine reaction. Another important question is, can you guarantee that you will always sympathize with others when they are in pain? I don't think anyone can. Let's take an extreme example. If someone suddenly punches you for no reason, and then they fall and hurt themselves, would you sympathize with their pain? Or would you be more likely to think they're silly or feel happy? Another extreme example, if a murderer escapes from prison and is caught shortly after, and during the escape, he is kicked hard by a police officer. Would you sympathize with the pain caused by the kick? I think everyone is ordinary and no one can unconditionally understand everyone. Of course, I want to emphasize that none of this is to encourage people to take pleasure in others' misfortune. It is to say that taking pleasure in others' misfortune may be a normal reaction. Because I think you may not understand why some people have such reactions. And I want to tell you that even if someone has a tendency to take pleasure in others' misfortune, it does not mean they will always do so whenever they see someone in pain. However, every person's chosen lifestyle will inevitably bear the resulting consequences. Note, I am referring to consequences, not punishments. When we want to view things truthfully, we must let go of judgment and focus only on the facts and individuals involved. We only need to understand the patterns and directions of things, while right or wrong, good or bad, are based on judgment standards deeply rooted in each person's heart, which are connected to their own personal feelings, societal expectations, upbringing, and education, among other factors. Therefore, there is no need to demand strict standards, as they are not uniform. However, humanity also shares common emotions, one of which is to not harm others. I think you should find out the reasons behind these accumulated conflicts, why you feel such a strong sense of insecurity towards women and intimate relationships, and why there is this mixture of shame and anger. output: I am glad to answer your questions. Seeing your question, I think this is a question that many young people, especially those who have some understanding of psychology, consider when choosing a partner. [In fact, the majority of people have experienced trauma from their origin family.] The origin family does have a significant impact on the psychological growth and many qualities that are formed under this influence (such as sense of responsibility, ambition, and sense of security in marriage) directly affect the happiness of future marriages and families. If you haven't established a deep emotional connection yet, it is indeed possible to make judgments and identify based on this aspect, in order to make a better choice for yourself. Of course, if you already have a strong emotional foundation, it is recommended to grow together with the guidance of a psychologist, gradually improving the potential impact that the origin family may have on your future family. It is important to know that the majority of us come with some kind of trauma. For different reasons such as cultural level, cognitive ability, and social emphasis on family education, our childhoods have left us with some traumatic experiences. But these "not-so-good" experiences allow us to constantly discover and improve ourselves. In fact, life should be like this. [The relationship patterns in the origin family are a shadow of future relationship patterns.] As for how to judge through the origin family, the relationship pattern is very important. In psychology, it is said that "the relationship pattern in the origin family largely determines future relationship patterns." Therefore, you can infer your future relationship based on observing their interactions with opposite-sex members of their origin family. For example, if their mother is extremely doting and they have a strong dependence on their mother, then you will also be responsible for taking care of them in the future. Similarly, if they have a long-standing tense relationship with their father, they may not handle relationships with same-sex authority figures such as bosses well in the workplace, leading to more obstacles in their work. Of course, these relationship patterns in the origin family are just a microcosm, and if they are aware of the impact of these patterns and make efforts to modify and improve them, there will be significant differences. [The quality of parents' relationship affects their trust in marital emotions.] If they have lived in a family where parents constantly argue, have a troubled relationship, or even experience infidelity, then witnessing these marital conditions from childhood could lead to a lack of trust in marital emotions, resulting in a decreased sense of responsibility in the family and other aspects. In contrast, if they have grown up in a harmonious family where their parents have a good relationship, it will increase their sense of security in marital emotions, giving them more confidence and strength to maintain a happy family and having a stronger ambition in their work. Therefore, paying attention to the quality of their parents' relationship will help you understand their inner values ​​and attitudes towards marital emotions. [Parents' parenting styles affect their approach to future children's education.] If we have not deliberately studied or improved our knowledge of parenting, then after becoming parents, we will most likely continue to use the parenting styles of our origin family, such as the father often scolding them. In the future, they are likely to adopt a similar approach with their children, which perpetuates a repeating problem. Of course, if you can learn and improve together, it will also improve to a certain extent. In summary, when choosing a partner, it is good to consider the situation of their origin family as a reference, but it is best not to make a final decision based solely on this aspect because the influence of the origin family is not absolute. As long as you both make efforts, you can create your own happiness.

Now, if the child is taken to a hair salon, where there are also chairs and white coats, if the child feels fear in the hair salon, that would be an example of stimulus generalization. The resistance to compliments may not be about the compliments themselves, but rather, it might trigger memories of past frustrating experiences. This is a defense mechanism with rationalized denial, defending against narcissistic satisfaction when appreciated by denying others' appreciation. The reason for defending against narcissistic satisfaction is to protect oneself from experiencing the pain of narcissistic frustration. Most people are used to speaking negative and hurtful words to themselves and feel that they are constantly living behind a mask. In order to break free from the curse of "I'm not good enough" in their minds, some people study hard but still can't escape its grip. The most important thing is to know oneself, to see one's own strengths and advantages, as well as to recognize one's shortcomings and flaws. Build on strengths, improve weaknesses, build confidence, and happily accept others' compliments. Sincere compliments are a good medicine that can help people progress and grow. With self-awareness, one can clearly identify and disregard insincere compliments while accepting genuine ones. Second, pretend to be confident. The strategy of "pretending to be confident" can help you at least have the opportunity to get many jobs and opportunities, instead of shutting them out from the beginning. Once you have a certain opportunity, the "imposter syndrome" will strive to complete it, and in fact, the results are usually much better than they expected. Sometimes pretending turns into reality. Third, try to believe. Start by learning to believe, believing that others' compliments are true, and believing that you deserve them. The next time someone compliments you, at least respond with "thank you." Over time, you will become more accustomed to compliments and then say, "I am beautiful," "I work hard, and I deserve these achievements." Believe in yourself, you deserve better, you deserve to have it.

Long-distance relationship, haven't seen each other for over two months. The passion is fading, we don't chat as much anymore, feeling low and unmotivated. output: Hello, OP. In a long-distance relationship, even though your boyfriend contacts you every day, you no longer have common topics to discuss. The excitement of the honeymoon phase has faded, and you are only left with low moods. You are unsure if it is caused by this person or this relationship. From your description, I see a contradiction: on one hand, you say you enjoy having your own space, having many interests, and being able to fulfill yourself without the need for constant intimacy and clinginess in a relationship. On the other hand, you feel disappointed because you haven't seen each other for two months in this long-distance relationship and there are no topics to talk about. Behind every contradiction, there is always some truth. It's possible that you have an avoidant attachment style, which means you don't inherently crave love, understanding, and acceptance, and you don't want highly intense emotional relationships. But deep down, you actually need these things more than anyone else. You need your self-worth to be recognized, someone to share the meaning of life with, and someone to understand and accept you. You say you enjoy missing someone from a distance because it allows you to project your imagination onto the other person, making you constantly feel loved and safe. In reality, you really need attention and understanding, but maybe you didn't receive much of it when you were young. So you use the approach of hiding in your own world to protect your heart which was hurt and disappointed in the past. Any emotional relationship will transition from passion to calmness. However, after the excitement fades, some relationships evolve into true love - caring for each other, nurturing each other, and supporting each other. Such relationships may seem calm, but they are stable and gentle. Your contradiction may come from your experiences of growth. What you need to explore yourself is what you truly need - is it what you described? Is the most authentic need really as you said? Once you find that authentic need, you can possibly find a relationship that fulfills your needs. Otherwise, you will find that even though you are in a relationship that seems to fulfill your described needs, you are not happy deep down. I hope you can love yourself and find someone who loves you the right way.

output: You just started high school and feel that the school is not good and not suitable for you because you feel that the teachers are not implementing effective management and are just slacking off every day, so you feel despair, right? ****** You are dissatisfied with the teachers not implementing effective management, so you hope that the school can have a good school atmosphere and the teachers can play a real role in management. You actually do not want to be influenced by this kind of environment, afraid of slacking off every day and not being able to get into college. This makes you feel disgusted with the current school and want to escape and leave. I see your inner pain and struggle, fighting against the efforts and the environment. The root of this pain lies in the fact that you both want to pursue a better learning environment and the possibility of future development. However, you feel powerless to fight against the environment and have to have conflicts within yourself, which affects your behavior and emotions. Sickness intensifies your disgust and avoidance towards the school, but you cannot get understanding, care, and acceptance from your family, feeling very disappointed and helpless, and wanting to express your struggle and helplessness through self-harm and suicide. You are dissatisfied with the school environment and think that it is not good, but you unconsciously give up your own pursuit and become a member of slacking off, confirming your negative impression and evaluation of the school. ****** The environment does indeed have a great impact on us. A good environment can help us progress more smoothly and achieve our goals. A bad environment can easily become an obstacle and make things less smooth. However, the development of anything is a result of both internal and external factors. In addition to having a good environment, what is more important is whether our internal motivation and strength are strong enough to support us moving forward. Only the internal driving force can help us overcome resistance and continue to strive. Many successful people are able to overcome adverse environments, hone and break through from them, find opportunities, and ultimately overcome the obstacles of a harsh environment, growing into more powerful individuals. So when you complain about the school not being good and you are not satisfied with the environment around you, you should first ask yourself if you really want to study well and go to a good college. Do you place your hopes of realizing your dreams on yourself or on the external world? There is a theory called "locus of control" that explains the attributions of success or failure that individuals often make. Internal locus of control attributes success to their own internal control power, so they tend to believe in their own abilities and are willing to take responsibility and actively seek solutions to problems, striving for their goals. External locus of control attributes success to external factors and relies on external forces to drive things forward, with the success or failure of things determined by external factors, finding excuses for failures and giving up their own power and efforts. This tendency of attributional explanatory style can influence our perception of the external world and ourselves, and therefore affect our actions and confidence. ****** I am not quite clear about the situation in your school. Apart from the poor management of schedule, how are other aspects? For example, the faculty strength, teaching quality, classmates' learning situation, etc., are there really no advantages to be found? Can you see their good side? How can they influence you? You should also ask yourself these questions: How is your current learning situation? What talents and strengths do you have? What can you learn from and gain in this school? Have you set clear goals for yourself? Have you ever believed in your own abilities? Is it the school that makes you slack off, or did you give up on yourself early on? Can you find a way to overcome difficulties and study well? For example, find teachers willing to help you and classmates willing to study together. If you transfer schools, can you guarantee that other schools will fully meet your requirements and that you will be able to motivate yourself to study well? Environmental factors should not be an excuse for avoiding difficulties, and changing the environment cannot completely solve the problem, because the root of the problem lies within yourself - you have both aspirations and desires, but also find excuses to avoid and give up. Even if the environment changes, you still cannot control the environment and fulfill your potential. If the pursuit of future dreams cannot rely on your own power to grasp and achieve, it can only be wishful thinking. Reality shows that many times, the environment is difficult to change. So, do you want to succumb to the environment, be defeated by the environment, or do you want to make an effort to adapt to the environment, change your thinking, adjust your cognition and behavior, and strive to overcome it and break free from this environment? This is a process of training and growth. Disgust, complaints, self-harm, and suicide are not effective forms of positive resistance, but rather a form of escape and giving up. Learn to accept the environment, adapt to the environment, find strength within yourself, and grow in a harsh environment, regain control over your own life, and that is the true form of resistance, allowing you to come closer to your dreams. Think carefully about your dreams and your life, find the source of your own strength, and face the challenges of the environment with confidence. Keep going.

I like a comfortable life, reading books, drinking tea, and avoiding difficult and challenging things. I always want to procrastinate and find it difficult to change. I also can't stand it when people around me behave this way, why is that?
output: Hello, OP, I would like to analyze this issue seriously with you. You mentioned that you enjoy comfort and avoid difficulties, but deep down inside, you seem to not accept comfort and want to change. This creates an internal conflict. If there is no internal conflict, you can simply enjoy this comfortable life without any problem. But you have noticed that not only for yourself, you also project this requirement onto others: to step out of the comfort zone! This tension of confrontation is causing you distress. Why? What should you do? I want to explain the reason from Jung's theory of "individuation." Simply put, "individuation" means becoming a complete, unique self, possessing a sense of sacredness while still maintaining human attributes. In the process of pursuing individuation, we will go through seven different stages, namely protection, differentiation, consolidation, integration, guidance, and transcendence. Each stage can also be subdivided into these seven different levels of functionality. The spiral development of human life takes place in these seven stages and levels. I don't know your age, but I think you must be a person with some life experience because you have a desire for personal growth. Based on your description, my initial judgment is that you are in the protection period. On the one hand, you need this comfortable life to nurture and protect you, but on the other hand, you lack strength in action. During the protection period, our energy is not sufficient, and our sense of self is relatively weak. What we need is to accumulate and replenish our energy, and draw nourishment from the external world. So reading books, drinking tea, and other seemingly useless pastimes are good ways for you to recharge yourself. However, you want to experience more possibilities because you know that you cannot always stay in the protection period. Your life needs to develop, your self needs to be perfected, and that is what we call the drive of "individuation" pushing and inspiring you. You have a vague awareness of this unconscious energy but cannot explain the reasons clearly, which creates a conflicting tension. You are anxious but currently powerless. In this regard, Daoism says to follow the way of nature, let everything take its natural course. The Diamond Sutra also says, "All conditioned things are impermanent - work out your own salvation with diligence." This tells us that we should not only focus on "how to do" but also maintain an attitude of doing "without doing" and being calm in our hearts. Therefore, when we currently lack the ability to step out of the comfort zone and cope with difficulties, we don't need to force ourselves to do so. When you have recharged yourself and have sufficient inner strength, you will naturally have the energy to explore and change. What we need to do is to go along with this development and nurture ourselves in the present moment. The same goes for dealing with other people. Everyone is at different stages of life's development. Some people are deeply influenced by childhood trauma and stay in the protection period for a long time, while others have had a relatively smooth life experience, with broad interests and fast stage development, leading to great achievements. So if we look at it from this perspective, we can be more tolerant and understanding of each person's behavior, without making subjective value judgments or projections. I hope my analysis above can help you. Best wishes!

Why do some counselors always have better results than others?

Professor Bruce E. Wampold, in his book "The Great Psychotherapy Debate," states, "There is a significant difference in the effectiveness of therapists: some therapists consistently achieve better outcomes than others, whether in clinical experiments or practical cases." What causes this difference? What are the characteristics of psychologists who consistently achieve positive counseling outcomes? How do they enhance the effectiveness of counseling?
output: The most important factor in determining the effectiveness of counseling is the counseling relationship, which is heavily influenced by the counselor's personality. If a counselor has a gentle, understanding, and patient personality with strong empathetic skills, they have innate advantages and talents in counseling. Even if they may not be highly skilled in counseling techniques, they can easily navigate the counseling relationship. Over time, the counseling effectiveness will gradually manifest. On the other hand, if a counselor has an impatient and controlling personality, and tends to give advice and directives in a dominant manner, the counseling effectiveness will be poorer. Even if they have excellent counseling skills, their ability to improve the effectiveness of counseling will be limited. Many people who study psychological counseling today have a misconception that they focus too much on techniques, striving to learn techniques everywhere, but neglect the cultivation of their own personality, which is detrimental to their work. In addition to the counselor's effectiveness in counseling, the counseling setup also plays a significant role. If a counselor adheres to principles, remains calm, follows proper counseling procedures, sets counseling goals, and establishes good rapport with clients, the counseling effectiveness will be very evident. Conversely, if the counselor's counseling setup is disorganized, such as frequently changing appointment times or being consistently late, the counseling effectiveness will be particularly poor. As a result, clients may become unsatisfied and ultimately leave. This situation tests the counselor's fundamental skills and their ability to manage the counseling setup. Counselors need to accumulate experience through long-term practice, reflect on their mistakes, and continuously improve themselves. Ultimately, they should strive to reach their optimal state in terms of personality, skills, and all other aspects. Counseling abilities grow and develop through continuous accumulation, and the more experience one has, the better their abilities will be. Combined with the counselor's continuous learning, the effectiveness of counseling can be consistently ensured.

How to overcome the feeling of inferiority caused by one's family background?

After studying psychology, I realized that the influence of the family of origin on the individual is truly significant. This feeling of inferiority seems to be ingrained in my bones. How can I overcome the feelings of inferiority caused by my family of origin?
output: Hello, OP! First, let me give you a big hug. When I saw your question, it really resonated with me. Our upbringing can bring us feelings of inferiority from various aspects, such as poverty, negative family relationships or parent-child relationships, physical defects, and so on. Because of these factors, we feel inferior to others, and thus develop a sense of inferiority. As for overcoming inferiority, I have some suggestions for you. First and foremost, we need to face ourselves and accept who we are. This understanding of ourselves needs to be objective. Only by facing ourselves can we understand our strengths and weaknesses. Nobody is perfect, and accepting our imperfect selves allows us to rationally leverage our strengths and mitigate our weaknesses. In this world, no one is perfect, and it is precisely our imperfections that make us closer to perfection. Distance yourself from sources of harm: Since we are unable to confront external sources of harm, why not choose to distance ourselves from them? I had a strained relationship with my parents since childhood, and when I went to university, I chose a city where they were not present. Because we rarely saw each other, their words and actions no longer had a significant impact on me. Of course, distancing ourselves does not mean being disrespectful to our parents; it means establishing boundaries and understanding our differences, without forcing others to accept or be influenced by us. Consequently, my feelings of inferiority in terms of family relationships have also significantly diminished. Maintain distance from sources of harm. Over time, you will forget about them until they no longer affect you. Live in harmony with your feelings of inferiority: It is undeniable that feelings of inferiority bring negative emotions and impact our studies and daily lives. However, appropriate feelings of inferiority can also motivate us to progress and give us the drive to move forward. Face your feelings of inferiority, don't suppress or resist them. Instead, choose methods you enjoy and consider reasonable to release them. When you are unable to control your emotions, slow down and engage in activities you enjoy. After a few hours, you will find that your feelings of inferiority have disappeared, and you will feel more relaxed. Engage in a dialogue with the "other": When your feelings of inferiority arise, write them on the left side of a paper, and then, in the role of an imaginary observer, write their perspective on the right side. For example: Left: "Why am I so inadequate and incapable?" Right: "Don't underestimate yourself. You are good at writing and drawing, and you treat others kindly... You have many strengths; you just haven't realized them yet." This method will gradually help us establish a more accurate cognitive thinking process. In this world, many people are plagued by feelings of inferiority caused by their upbringing. Some fortunate ones overcome the feelings, while others may struggle with them their whole lives. It might be impossible to completely overcome them, but we can become better every day.

After studying psychology, can one understand and manipulate anyone?

Can you understand most people after studying "General Psychology" and "Social Psychology"?
output: Hello! First of all, according to the common understanding of "拿下" (which means "take down" in English), it refers to control, conquest, or surpassing. Secondly, assuming that we understand "大部分人" (which means "most people" in English) as referring to more than 50%, there are currently about 20,000 certified consultants in the domestic statistics, and a population of 1.4 billion in China. So let's assume that the "大部分人" you are referring to is either over 10,000 people in the industry or over 700 million people in society. Furthermore, since you put the book titles in quotation marks, I assume you are referring to the books "普通心理学" (General Psychology) and "社会心理学" (Social Psychology) as separate works, not vertical specialized research in these two fields. ● If "普通心理学" refers to a book, it studies the general principles and mechanisms of psychological processes and behaviors in normal adults. It is a basic introductory discipline that includes the theoretical principles and methods of psychology, psychological processes, psychological states, and personality traits. At the same time, it encompasses the research achievements of various branches of psychology and serves as general knowledge and theoretical foundation for these branches. ● If "社会心理学" refers to a book, it is a branch discipline based on "普通心理学", focusing on the psychological and behavioral processes and changes of individuals and groups in social interactions. In summary, the content includes the individual's influence on society, society's influence on individuals, and the mutual influence between social groups. Other branches at the same level include but are not limited to educational psychology, management psychology, consumer psychology, and criminal psychology. Although we all have the wish to simplify things and hope that limited knowledge can serve a large number of people, "拿下" at least 10,000 people is definitely not something that can be achieved simply by finishing reading these two books, let alone "拿下" over 700 million people. Even if you have read 2,000 books and mastered knowledge in multiple fields horizontally and vertically, it does not directly connect with "拿下别人" (to take others down). Knowledge acquisition is not like memorizing jokes to become a topic of conversation, and possessing a small amount of knowledge is not capital, let alone qualification. If our desire is to conquer others and be respected by them, the first mandatory lesson is personal charm, followed by professional cultivation. Both of these require comprehensive qualities, which means having the ability to attract and influence others through personal character and temperament, as well as constantly overcoming challenges and achieving a high level of expertise in the field we are studying. I told her at her doorstep that I fainted from low blood sugar during running, my head felt empty, like I was dying. Impatiently, she sent me back home without expressing any concern. Holding back tears, I returned to my room, and since then, I haven't talked to her about anything. Similar incidents happened before. Suddenly having a high fever, I told her I wasn't feeling well, she said I was pretending and ignored me. Soon after, I started vomiting, and my dad took me to the hospital. When I was young, I fantasized about my mom being Zixia from "A Chinese Odyssey," which meant she could transform. When she treated me well, she was Zixia, but when she didn't, she became Hongxia.
output: Hello, encountering challenges and feeling lost in life is something that everyone goes through. Don't worry, you're not alone. Everyone is going through their own journey. As a child, one often wishes for a caring and loving mother. A mother's embrace brings warmth and companionship, as well as a connection of love. However, when a mother hurts, it cuts off this connection harshly. This is the true source of pain. Should one continue to be entangled in the unchangeable past, or should one grow and reclaim their own power and decision-making ability from this experience? First and foremost, it is important to understand that we cannot choose our mother in this lifetime. If we think about it, she is also a pitiful person. As much as she is indifferent towards you, she is equally neglectful towards herself. This indifference stems from never having been valued or cared for in childhood, growing up in a family that is just as cold. She treats you with the same indifference as she treats others because she simply doesn't know what it means to care or express emotions. Letting someone who is completely incapable of caring show you affection would only lead to disappointment. Accepting this lesson from your mother's life, even though her own unfinished growth and breakthroughs affected you, it is still a part of your destiny. You have to decide if you want to be like your mother or break free from these constraints and have control over your own life. When children are deprived of their parents' love and care, they face a survival test. However, now that we have grown up, we are fully capable of providing ourselves with the love and care we need. It's just that the unfulfilled needs and the wounds from childhood don't disappear as we age, and at some point in life, we have to face our inner vulnerability. Accept this vulnerability, acknowledge the loss, and allow yourself to experience various emotional states. For example, if you don't want to forgive your mother right now, then don't. If you don't want to see her, then don't. It's not avoiding the situation, but rather temporarily allowing yourself to feel that way, while also clearing the accumulated negative emotions from your body. Engage in physical activities, do things you enjoy, and allow yourself to express your emotions when needed. Writing down your grievances towards your mother or expressing them verbally can help release your inner feelings. Through continuous self-clearing, your inner peace will grow, and you will be able to accept the states of others. They are all experiencing their own destinies, and the question is whether to let others influence your entire life or to live according to your own desires – the choice is yours. Through this process of clearing, you will continuously gain the power to make choices. I wish you to be true to yourself and return to your inner strength. In this return, you can provide yourself with all the care and love you desire. Whether others care for or hurt you, you will still love yourself. Best wishes.

20-year-old male, my mother extremely dislikes me using skincare products.

When I was very young (around seven or eight years old), whenever I applied face cream or hand cream, she would have a strong reaction. As I grew older, using skincare products became even worse... I received intense disdain from my own mother on this matter... We often end up arguing about these issues. I even wonder if she had some kind of experience that caused such a reaction. I don't think it's wrong for boys to care for their skin; on the contrary, I think it's worth promoting and I take it very seriously myself. I don't want to sneak around as if I'm doing something shameful. Maybe it's not me who has a psychological problem; maybe she should see a mental health specialist. What should I do?
output: Hello, give you a warm hug. According to your description, your mother is very opposed to you, as a boy, using skincare products. However, at the same time, Phil wants to remind you that both your thoughts and your mother's thoughts are fine. So your sentence "Is it not me who has a psychological problem, should she go see a psychologist?" actually puts the other person in a state of having a problem that needs to be corrected, just like your mother. In this state, holding on to one's own views will only exacerbate the contradiction and make it difficult to resolve the issue. As for the issue of men using skincare products, traditional beliefs have deeply influenced society. Many people still believe that only girls use makeup and skincare products, and that it's unnecessary and even effeminate for a "tough guy." However, with the deepening of gender equality awareness, just as some people emphasize feminism, there are also people who emphasize men's rights and avoiding biases. One of these rights is that men also have the right to use makeup and skincare products because taking care of oneself is not gender-specific. Therefore, Phil believes that your perspective is valid. Let's talk about your mother's perspective. Your mother's strong aversion to this matter may be due to a combination of reasons. Firstly, when you were young, you used to apply face cream and hand cream to yourself, which may have seemed "outrageous" to your mother. Moreover, not just boys, but most girls of your age would likely be scolded for such behaviors, labeled as "makeup is bad" or "at such a young age, all you care about is dressing up," or even told that "you have good skin, you don't need skincare" or "these products are dangerous, they are medicines, you can't touch them," and so on. This form of education where parents are in control can subtly influence children, making them unable to engage in behaviors that may seem strange to their parents or society, even though those behaviors may not be wrong and may simply be unacceptable to the majority. Secondly, she may have been influenced by the thoughts of the time she grew up in. As the saying goes, there is a generation gap every three years. Sometimes, communication with middle or high school students or even younger children can be quite frustrating, let alone our parents who grew up in a different era. They may not have encountered or even dared to think about many things. So misunderstandings are normal. Maybe skincare products were very precious to your mother's generation, and she may have also been influenced by the idea that men cannot engage in "feminine" behaviors. Or maybe she can't understand why her child would do such a thing and wonders if there is something going on in your mind. The specific reasons can only be guessed. -- Resolution strategy -- Expressing your thoughts and opinions is not only beneficial for yourself but also helpful in changing your mother's perspective. There are many things in modern society that require our parents to understand and accept. As children, it is our duty to take on the role of "teacher." Or, to be a little selfish, if our parents can accept these things, we can also avoid a lot of trouble. So don't avoid the topic just because it always leads to unpleasantness. Instead, guide and express your views correctly, just as you said, it is not wrong for boys to take care of their skin. When communicating with your mother, try to remember the reasons for each disagreement. Is it because you simply don't want to bring up the topic, or both sides believe they are right and try to convince each other, or one party's words are too extreme and lead to arguments, or there are incompatible beliefs that are hard to accept? If it happens only once or twice, it may be a coincidence or mishandling, but if it happens frequently, it is more likely that one or both individuals have a problem. So when communicating with your mother, also pay attention to whether you have any problems or instances of excessive behavior. Try to empathize and understand your mother's perspective, rather than just standing in your own shoes. Soft tactics may not be necessary, it's a way to ease the situation, just as you said, there may be something happening to your mother or it may simply be that there is no way to communicate and compromise. In that case, you can use this tactic – using products secretly. Out of sight, out of mind. Naturally, your mother won't look for trouble, but this is a strategy that tends to avoid the problem and ultimately isn't ideal. So Phil doesn't really recommend it. I hope my answer can help you (･ω･)ﾉ.

output: 1. If diagnosed with depression, you can ask the doctor to provide you with a sick leave, so that you can rest at home for a period of time. Some people can adapt to certain jobs, while others are naturally unable to adapt to a particular job, and sometimes perseverance alone cannot lead to improvement. 3. Only by receiving treatment and recovering can you have a better future. Otherwise, constantly doing a job that worsens your mental and physical condition may provide temporary financial security, but in the long run, it's not worth it. Because compared to a few months or even a year's worth of wages, after recovery, you still have decades of opportunities to earn money, so there's no need to rush. 4. For individuals, necessary stress helps enhance abilities, but excessive stress can only crush a person. So while you are gradually getting better, think about what kind of work won't subject you to excessive stress. However, also remind yourself not to avoid necessary stress. Then write down your thoughts and feelings on this matter when searching for a new job or when returning to work, and discuss them with your superiors. For example: excessive stress - frequent business trips; necessary stress - lower salary, lack of peers in the work environment. Only by recognizing the difference between "excessive stress" and "necessary stress" can you avoid getting ill and avoid becoming the kind of person your parents call "sensitive."

But then I became eager to learn, ambitious, humble, and hardworking, and I managed to make a lot of money again, which I believed would last for a long time. And then I started to relax slowly. This cycle of bankruptcy has happened four times. The reasons for bankruptcy are different each time, but overall they are the same as the reasons mentioned above. Luckily, I am young and intelligent, and I have managed to get back on my feet each time I went bankrupt. However, it's strange that the suffering after each bankruptcy, as well as the hardships I endured when I had no money, sometimes forced me to meet more useful people and try new things in life. But I am still afraid of stumbling in the future. Where did I go wrong? Do you have any life advice for me?
output: The easier things come to us, the less likely we are to cherish them. When I was young, my family conditions were poor, and I had to stretch every cent as much as possible. I endured a lot of hardships and received many disapproving glances. Later on, I had some opportunities and earned quite a bit of money. I entered circles that I never dared to dream of before and indulged in what is considered high-end consumption. However, it seems that I have fallen into a cycle where, once I earn enough to meet my expectations, I go back to living the same way, and once the money is gone, I figure out ways to earn it again. It's just like getting drunk when there's wine available today without thinking about tomorrow. There is no clear goal or ambition, and most of the time, we just settle for what is in front of us. Living in a state of constant indulgence is one kind of life, while trying new things is also a part of life. Each time we stumble and fall, we will surely gain different experiences. We just need to understand the meaning of our own lives and leave ourselves a way out, as Lady Luck won't always favor us. Therefore, we can start by improving our parents' living environment and saving up some retirement money for them. We can also invest in several properties for ourselves, even though property is not meant to be speculated on, it at least serves as an asset and provides us with some security. Additionally, we can explore different lifestyles, meet exceptional people, observe their lives, and see if we are interested in trying something new. Moreover, we should pay attention to our health, as health is something that no amount of money can buy, and excessive indulgence can be detrimental to our well-being. The world loves you, and so do I.

What should a person with depression do if they develop feelings for someone?

I am a patient with moderate depression and currently taking medication. I feel very lonely, so I chat with strangers on a social media platform. Lately, I have found myself eager to meet up with nearby strangers. I like to dress up and look glamorous when meeting them, chatting, and smiling, as if I were a normal person. The first person was because I wanted to jump into the lake, but he came to pick me up on his electric scooter. We walked in the playground and then he took me back to my dorm. The second person was because he said he was willing to accompany me to the hospital, which touched me. Then we had a meal together. The third person was because I was bored, and he happened to be on vacation. We met, walked, and chatted. I admired his experience. I don't feel like seeing any of the people I have met again. Until the fourth person, I understood his sadness and academic pressure, and I resonated with him. He tried to do something for me, and I started crying loudly because I was scared. He comforted me and hugged me like comforting a child. In fact, we were both well-dressed, and nothing happened. I realized that I have developed feelings for him, so I deleted everyone else and left only him. However, I stubbornly declined his second invitation. What's wrong with me? Am I better now? But I am still that sad, terrible, wanting-to-disappear me. How should I face myself and this strange feeling?
output: Hi, it's nice to see you here. Major depressive disorder is really unpleasant, I understand. But what I see is an image of someone who, despite feeling uncomfortable and having more darkness in their life than the average person, is still actively seeking redemption. Honestly, it moves me. Your process of meeting strangers through social media is a process of self-redemption. Because you believe that you can be okay, really okay. [To someone who doesn't know your past, you believe in showing a very normal side, even superior to others (because the ability of depression patients to perceive and respect life is beyond average)]. So you are enthusiastic about meeting strangers, believing that there will definitely be a meaningful connection. Indeed, you have achieved that. But on the other hand, you know that this ability cannot be sustained. Depressive disorders cannot maintain a stable emotional state; the random words and actions that occasionally appear in this world will trigger our existing traumatic experiences. It's easy to light the fuse. And more often than not, it's because the explosive inside needs to be released properly. Because we're not okay yet, we can't always control it. And once separated, we don't want to see each other anymore. Knowing that the purpose of meeting has been fulfilled, knowing that we are not ready to invest ourselves in such a relationship (regardless of what it may be), we naturally won't meet again, won't seek to continue. Because for our inner feelings, this is enough, we don't have the desire to make something happen or become something in reality! These moments are like when a person sunbathes when they have nothing else to do. They can enjoy the sun, but that's it. The sky cannot always have the sun hanging high, and we are not prepared to be seen when the moon comes out. When the day comes, [when we can take day and night interchangeably, when joy and sadness coexist without feeling uneasy], at that time, we will feel love for ourselves, like ourselves, and hope that this beautiful self can be seen by more people, and believe that this self deserves to be loved by more people. That's when we can truly say we're doing well! Lastly, I want to say that [depression can definitely get better, you have to believe in that]. It's just that this process includes so much that the average person cannot perceive, and as a result, you will ultimately have to understand and accommodate more than others.

Recently, I have been involved in emotional entanglements with a guy. Every time we have sweet moments, I dream sweet dreams at night, and when we fight, I have anxious dreams. output: Hello! @We often find that dreams are colorful and often do not align with reality. Sometimes, dreams can be vivid, like a science fiction movie. Of course, we also have dreams that reflect our daily experiences. Dreams are so mysterious and profound that people have been studying and exploring their meanings since ancient times. @If you try to understand dreams, you will realize that most of our dreams are wrapped in layers. Superficial dreams may have just a few layers, while complex dreams are like layers of an onion. ○Freud believed that dreams stem from our desires. Jung believed that dreams have a compensatory nature and can convey important messages to us. (This situation probably applies to you.) Adler believed that the main function of dreams is problem-solving, providing a positive outcome. Overall, these theories suggest that dreams are related to our subconscious and understanding your dreams is like glimpsing a corner of the iceberg, helping you understand yourself. @Dream processing involves four mechanisms: condensation, displacement, representation, and secondary elaboration. People or objects in your dreams generally have symbolic meanings. For example, dreaming of a house may symbolize your inner self. Dreaming of a person may imply someone you have in mind. Symbolic meanings can vary for different individuals due to cultural differences, mindset differences, or gender differences, resulting in different interpretations of symbols. ○You mentioned that you are currently experiencing relationship troubles. I think that may be why you are feeling fearful or avoidant, perhaps even afraid of seeing that person. So, in your dreams, that person cannot simply appear directly, but instead takes on the identity of someone else. If you observe carefully, you will find that the person you dream about is not unrelated to the person you have in mind. Let me give you an example: I had a falling out with a friend, and our relationship became strained. One day, we both coincidentally encountered each other on our way home. Initially, we both pretended not to see each other and planned to just pass each other by. While exploring your self-identity, the most important thing is to focus on living in the present moment and completing your current tasks. It is okay to maintain a stable state, and it is already good enough to work five days and rest for three days. Secondly, don't set a goal that is too distant as it may have some motivating effects, but the side effects can be significant, such as continuous anxiety. It is recommended to set periodic major directions, such as learning English. For example, "spend 2-4 weeks going through English grammar, practice areas that are weaker" can be a phased direction. Then, move forward in this direction every day. If you make more progress on a certain day, you can give yourself a small reward. If you make less progress on another day, there is no need to be disheartened. There may be many factors affecting the results. Summarize the progress made and the lessons learned every week or two. In this way, one will feel grounded, and the ultimate result will be determined by oneself (often better than expected because we tend to underestimate the power of accumulation over time).

I remember the comforting words she said and the things she did that appealed to me when we were dating. However, it has been five years since we broke up. In the past, I used to sleep better by holding onto my ex, but after the breakup, I started hugging my pillow instead. These past few days, I've been playing the sound of a girl breathing and spraying a perfume on my pillow that smells similar to my ex's shampoo.
