Parents are separated in two different places to help their brother and sister-in-law take care of their grandchildren. What should be done if there are signs of infidelity?

The older brother and sister-in-law have two children. The first child has already started attending kindergarten, and in the beginning, the mother used to go alone to their house to help take care of the child because the father hadn't retired yet. Now that the father has retired and the second child is only two years old, a boy, both parents are taking care of the children at the brother and sister-in-law's house. However, the father has recently suggested taking turns to spend half a month taking care of the children and the other half at home. My mom doesn't really want to do this. A few days ago, while at the seldom-used house with my mom, I noticed extra child pillows, women's socks on the bed, and magazines. My mom also found a piece of fabric for making children's clothes on her bed. Both of us are suspicious. My parents are already 60 years old, and my mother wants companionship in her old age, so she doesn't want to reveal anything. When I was 12 years old, my dad had an affair, so my mom has always been very sad. Their upbringings were very different, with my dad's side being poor and my mom's dad being a director. My mom has feelings of inferiority. I want to protect my mom and help them improve their relationship. Now, the plan is for one person to go and see the children for half a month, which gives my dad an opportunity to have an affair. What should I do to save this family? Can I install cameras? Does anyone have any good suggestions?
output: Hello, after reading your question, I can feel the distress and turmoil this situation involving your family has caused you. It also reminds me of a female friend whose father had a habit of cheating and her mother, upon discovering it, would often be subjected to domestic violence. When the children grew up, they asked their mother why she didn't divorce him, and she always said it was because they were still young. There were five children in the family, who witnessed their mother being beaten from a young age. As they grew up, the mother would constantly complain to the children about their father, saying he was still cheating. Four out of the five children had conflicts with their father and expressed the desire to cut ties with him. Every time they tried to convince their mother to divorce him, she would say she was afraid of being laughed at because of her age. As a result, although the mother seemed to have accepted the situation, the anger still lingered inside her, and she would call the children to complain, causing them to distance themselves from her. At the same time, the children themselves also became trapped in the pain. Seeing their mother's vulnerability, suggesting that she leave him would fall on deaf ears. However, her daily phone calls complaining about him would cause her unbearable headaches, severely impacting her life. The mother became disconnected from society. At the age of 48, she had no skills, never having worked since getting married, so she had fear of change and didn't know what she could do if she divorced. Furthermore, her husband's infidelity was a shameful matter for her, and she believed that her own weakness and incompetence had led to his cheating. Every time she saw him, it was as if she was seeing her own incompetence, which made her very angry and led to arguments. But she was "afraid" to divorce... This example shows that the older generation's aversion to divorce is partly due to the belief that "divorce" is a shameful thing, and if it becomes public, it's like proving their own incompetence. On the other hand, as the children grow up and have children who will "stand up" for them (a saying indicating that enduring will pay off once the children grow up), the children will naturally "punish" the father. This gives them a sense of revenge and balances their emotions. At the same time, as they get older, remarrying involves too many issues, so they are hesitant to divorce, fearing they will have no one to rely on in old age. There is also the fact that they have been detached from reality for too long, with no personal life or interpersonal support outside the family, which fills them with fear of the unknown, etc. [Getting back to the main topic] Based on your description of the current situation in your family, your father has previously cheated and your mother is used to self-denial, and now she suspects your father is cheating again. [Analysis] This suspicion is built on the foundation of previous mistrust in your father, and it is normal to have this mindset when trust has been broken in a relationship. However, humans are also peculiar creatures. There is a psychological phenomenon called "self-fulfilling prophecy," which means that how you perceive something will subconsciously push it towards that direction. For example, after the mother experienced her husband's adultery, she believes that he is someone who enjoys cheating. So although she seems to have forgiven him, seeing him still causes her distress and pain, and she suspects he will cheat again. As a result, she becomes angry and doesn't give him a warm reception when she sees him. Humans need emotional support, and when they don't receive it from their spouse and children, they often seek it outside the family. (I personally don't like this explanation, as it makes it seem like infidelity is someone else's fault. But for the older generation who haven't studied psychology, they are more easily controlled by emotions and primal instincts, which is indeed a fact.) [What can you do?] Your current concern is how to solve the problem without damaging the emotional foundation. First of all, try to ascertain the facts and not blow the problem out of proportion. Don't go around telling everyone in the family about it, as this will cause more harm. On the factual level, you can directly ask about the suspicions of infidelity, but this will only startle the snake in the grass, even if there is something going on, he won't admit it, and it will damage the relationship. As for whether to install surveillance cameras, as long as it doesn't violate any legal issues, it may be worth considering. However, it is important to understand that installing cameras is just to make yourself clear about the situation. Regardless of the outcome, you can tell your mother that your father didn't cheat (since it's her desire), and you don't need to let them know about the cameras. Next: if you find out he didn't cheat, you can put it to rest for now. If you find out he did cheat, you can talk to him about the previous incident of cheating and the harm it caused to the family, and express that you are willing to forgive his previous behavior, but if it happens again, you will choose to stand with your mother, and the family will not forgive him again. (Since he is worried about retirement issues, expressing it in this way can also be a deterrent.) Lastly, encourage your mother to go out more in the evenings, join in some square dancing, and open up her body, as an open body leads to an open mind, gradually avoiding negative thinking. Organize more family gatherings and outings to distract and experience the beauty of life. Every family has their own difficult experiences, so imagine if this happened in my own family, I would probably handle it more decisively, and I think my mother's personality would also have less tolerance. So, with different family situations, think more about your own approach, as you are the one who knows the family situation best. Home is a place where love is cherished, so cherish it. If love can solve the problem, try not to resort to dark methods. I hope this is helpful to you and good luck~.

People often regret and entangle themselves with things in the past, always thinking that if they had another chance, they would do better than before and the outcome would be different. As a result, they can't help but feel regret and self-blame. However, what we don't know is that any choice you made in the past was the best choice you could make based on your limited resources at that time, such as your level of knowledge, maturity, abilities, and state of mind. In that state, you did your best. Even if you could go back in time and start over, you would still make imperfect choices with the same limited resources. The reason you regret the past today is because the present you, in all aspects, is more mature and capable than the past you. 2. Holding onto the past and what is happening right now is because you haven't learned how to forgive and let go. I guess maybe when you were a child, you were also held onto by adults because of a minor mistake. It is because we haven't experienced forgiveness and tolerance that we cannot forgive and let go of ourselves and others. It's just that we often don't realize our own behavior and even can't trust ourselves, and all of this comes from the push of our subconscious. If you want to know how to change, you first need to know why, where the root of these behaviors lies. 3. The past is already gone, it has long disappeared in the river of time, and it no longer exists objectively. However, the unpleasantness of the past still lingers in our hearts, becoming an obstacle, a burden. Therefore, the first thing we need to do is to understand why we are like this, so that we can take targeted actions; secondly, based on what we know, we can heal. Perhaps it is necessary for you to go back to scenes from your childhood that you cannot forget, and heal that child, releasing the suppressed emotions such as grievances, sadness, anger, etc. Only when the emotions are processed can rationality return, forgiveness and tolerance can be discussed, and we can move forward better. If someone has dreams every day, what should they do?

If someone dreams every day, what should be done?
output: Hello, the Jungian psychology understands dreams as a compensation of unconscious deviations from consciousness. Dreams have both compensatory and predictive effects. In most cases, if a person frequently dreams, it means that they may have significant psychological conflicts internally that cannot be expressed at the conscious level or realized in reality. They are compensated for through dreams at the unconscious level. On the other hand, dreams are also a healing process, repairing inner repression and conflicts. Through dreaming, healing occurs. Dreams are alive and the language of the unconscious. If you feel that there are a large number of dreams occurring during a certain period of time, it is worth noticing if there are any untransformed repression and conflicts within. You can seek a psychoanalyst to analyze your dreams. The scenes, characters, and symbols in dreams all represent the manifestation of your inner world and certain aspects or traits of your personality. Through dream analysis, you can understand the unconscious symbols, respect the unconscious itself, and achieve a balanced and developed relationship between consciousness and unconsciousness. Additionally, if there are always rich dreams, it also indicates that you have a very rich inner world and significant inner energy. Dreams are vivid, lively, and can bring creativity. Therefore, people who dream a lot have great creative potential. Dreams also have a predictive effect. Through dream analysis, dreams can be more than just imagination; they can be realized and dreams can come true.

How to resolve the conflict in Oedipus Rex? Would feeling guilty if one surpasses their parents?

After graduating, I have been working in Shanghai. Due to the epidemic this year, my previous company dissolved, so I went back to my hometown to live with my parents. During this period, I have been feeling strange for no reason. For example, I feel awkward when I have to put on makeup and wear a nice dress for job interviews. When I see the way my mom looks at me when I come home, I feel embarrassed and weird. They are used to living frugally, so even when I buy snacks or ice cream, it feels strange. I feel like enjoying life a little is a kind of guilt, and at the same time, I feel that I don't deserve to live a good life or to have a good job. I came across a quote by Teacher Zeng Qifeng before: "Anything related to suppressing one's abilities may be related to the Oedipus complex." I feel like I am suppressing my own abilities, making myself live in hardship, because if I surpass my parents, there seems to be a particularly difficult to eliminate feeling of guilt, or you could say I am betraying them (it's hard to describe this feeling). I would like to ask the teachers for guidance on how to resolve this conflict. Would it be better for me to live alone away from my parents?
output: Hello, you mentioned that once you are in front of your parents, you suppress your desires and abilities because they have had a difficult life. If you surpass them, you will have an indelible guilt. I have also had similar experiences and can understand the awkwardness and discomfort you mentioned. You also mentioned the "Oedipus conflict" theory discussed by Teacher Zeng Qifeng. This theory can explain your feelings to a certain extent, but there can be other explanations as well. Let me share my opinion for your reference. First, feeling awkward or ashamed in front of your parents when you are able to have things or a life better than theirs shows your "sympathy" or "empathy". It is true that our parents have lived a harder life than us, which is related to the era they grew up in. Your awareness of their hardships shows humility and understanding, and this emotion enables you to have more compassion and be more considerate towards them. Second, it is normal to feel a sense of unworthiness in front of our parents when we can enjoy the many good things in life. This is because we were indeed born in a peaceful era, and the foundation that our parents have worked hard for allows us to have a comfortable life. Perhaps when you were young, your parents had strict expectations of you, which made you feel that everything you have must come at a great cost. However, in reality, as long as it is not obtained through theft, it is reasonable for you to use money that you have earned to consume. Lastly, you mentioned if it would be better to live alone away from your parents. In my opinion, it can indeed improve your situation. You can reflect on whether you still have such emotions when you live alone. If not, it means it works. If you cannot leave your parents, when you are at home and realize that you have feelings of awkwardness or guilt, you can simply say "Thank you for your hard work" to them, or cook something delicious for them, or pour them a glass of water. You can give it a try and see if it helps you feel a little better. Best wishes, Sauce.

I want to find a partner, but my mother said that the epidemic is severe now, there are many viruses, so it's better to work for the country. I'm very puzzled. On one hand, I want to follow my heart and have some adventures, but on the other hand, I am also worried that I don't have a secure job and solid experience, and I'm afraid that I won't have enough to eat if something unexpected happens in the future. What should I do... My parents' opinions have some merit, but I don't want to live a monotonous life every day.
output: Hello, questioner. As someone who once listened to their mother and took the civil service exam, but then quit after three years following their own advice, my suggestion to you is simple: do what you love and listen to yourself. Based on your description of the problem, I have outlined the following points for your reference: 1. "Mother says" vs "I say" – What does "Mother says, Mother thinks" mean to you? Parents' opinions have some merit, and we should respect them. From your mother's perspective, she believes she is not wrong. She doesn't want you, as a girl, to work too hard. She wants you to have a stable job and a worry-free life without setbacks. However, that is her expectation, her idea of what is good. What are your expectations? If your expectations are the same as your mother's, then there is no need to struggle. But if you expect a life that is free and not monotonous, that's different. 2. What can I do? What do I want to do? You were able to work at the court for two years, and you also mentioned wanting to be a lawyer. This shows that at least for the profession of a lawyer, you have confidence and ability. So at least you can do jobs related to that. What do you want to do? If you genuinely want to become a lawyer, then you will willingly put in a lot of effort and be willing to endure hardships for what you want to do. In this regard, everyone is the same. Everyone will put in a lot of effort for something they love and will persevere. We need to differentiate between work, occupation, and career. About work, occupation, and career, there is a fantastic interpretation by Professor Li Mengchao that I would like to share with you. "Work is what you are currently doing, it brings you income, perhaps it is the work you have always wanted to do, or maybe just temporary part-time work; occupation is a career direction that includes many jobs, it may be something you want to do for a long time, or at least five to ten years; career is something you want to do in the long run, something you are prepared to devote your life to. You are willing to spend money, labor, and even sacrifice your life for this career. It's a lifelong commitment. When occupation, career, and work are combined, that is certainly happiness. However, not everyone has a combination of the three, some may need to work first before achieving their career." So you can examine yourself and have certain expectations for work, occupation, and career before planning. 3. Iron rice bowl and "no food after unexpected events" Due to the pandemic, those who are not employed by the government may indeed experience more anxiety because their income is not guaranteed. They may even worry about their livelihoods. However, if you were to visit Wuhan this June, you would find that people's lives are still going on. You cannot see the marks of disaster on their faces. Wuhan's hot dry noodles are still delicious, Wuhan people are still vibrant, and Wuhan's crayfish still have a lingering fragrance. Donghu Lake is still beautiful as ever. Life goes on. If there are difficulties, they can be overcome. In my opinion, this is the most beautiful aspect of being human. Iron rice bowls have their benefits, but they also have limitations. Everything has two sides. If you want an iron rice bowl, you have to sacrifice a certain degree of freedom. And if you want freedom, you have to sacrifice a certain degree of security. However, if a person has enough confidence and security within them, they will not be limited by any job. They should have the ability to support themselves in any situation and make their lives increasingly better. So, believe in your ability to do this as well. These are my answers. Good luck!

In order to keep our family intact, especially because our children are only 6 and 3 years old, I have to endure something that no man in the world can tolerate. I am willing to forgive her for this mistake, but I'm worried that by forgiving, I might be indulging her behavior. Additionally, whenever I close my eyes, I can't help but think about their video of sexual activity. I feel that this woman will never be clean again, mentally and physically dirty. I don't know how to face her in daily life even if I decide to forgive her. Whether to divorce or not, she has left a shadow in my heart, and I am in immense pain!
output: 【Take it as a learning opportunity】Dear friend: Hello! After reading your words, I feel that you are a very rational person who understands that the key is not whether to divorce. You know that divorce cannot solve the problem. The key issue is your concern about being betrayed again, how to face her, and how to repair this relationship. Why does a third party appear in a marriage? 1. Someone said it right: if there are no problems in the relationship between husband and wife, a third party cannot intervene. If the husband and wife are united, the third party cannot break them apart. 2. It is a common habit in China to not speak up about problems. Because of face-saving and embarrassment, it is a cultural habit not to actively understand each other's views on this matter or their own behavior. Therefore, like a snowball, the problem grows bigger and bigger. 3. If there is no common goal in life and the family atmosphere is not good, some families may appear normal to outsiders, but inside, they are full of problems. There is a lack of care, unity, trust, or boundaries between the husband and wife. Therefore, if you want to face her and want to have a happy family again, you must have the determination to reconcile. 【First】Release anger. Dealing with this matter with anger is futile. Try releasing it, maybe try hitting a pillow. 【Second】Labeling and trying to forgive. If you keep looking down on her and continue to despise her, it will only make you feel that you didn't have good judgement in the first place and hurt your self-esteem. It may even create more negative atmosphere. No one grows up aspiring to be an "unfaithful woman". There must be reasons behind it. I have found that the person who hurts others suffers twice as much pain as the person being hurt, or even more. Try to separate the person from the actions, deal with this matter properly, and think about why you fell in love with this person in the first place. 【Third】Have a calm face-to-face conversation. Take this opportunity to express your feelings about this matter. Let her understand the impact this has had on you. Understand the reasons behind her infidelity and her satisfaction with this marriage. Through this matter, understand each other's true feelings. You have to understand that having a high income is just one aspect of fulfilling family responsibilities. If a homemaker in a high-income family cheats, it may be because she feels too empty. You have to understand that money cannot replace other types of love. Confidence, intimacy, service, dedication... these cannot be bought with money. Check if you have put her first. The proper order of a healthy family is: spouse, children, parents. Is the relationship between husband and wife equal? Often, different incomes can cause the higher earner to look down on the other, creating an imbalance in status and conflicts. 【Fourth】Rebuilding trust requires time and fulfillment of promises. Try to have her write a commitment letter. Let her understand the importance of this commitment. This will make you feel more at ease and also serve as a wake-up call for her. 【Fifth】Don't demand a perfect marriage. Since no one is perfect, how can a marriage be perfect? Take this incident as an opportunity to learn. Marriage is not the end of happiness, but another beginning of learning in life. Approach marriage with a learning attitude and invite your partner to face the problems together. Don't shoulder the burden of marriage alone. Try to openly express your feelings and let the other person understand you and love you. Give yourself and your partner time, and consider yourself and her as classmates or partners.

I often doubt whether others' love for me is genuine, and I want to push away someone and end a relationship.

In intimate relationships, there is often a push-pull dynamic, especially during periods of conflict and disagreement. The more the other person seeks me, the more I resist. When the other person calms down and withdraws, I may feel the urge to provoke them again, hoping they will continue to seek me or try to reconcile. I feel like there's something wrong with me. Often, after investing myself in the relationship, I constantly think about pushing this person and the relationship away, wanting to go back to square one. I also frequently doubt whether this person truly loves me. I tend to magnify small details and think, "See, he doesn't love me or care about me." I silently keep track of these instances until they accumulate and eventually lead to a complete break. I don't know why I act this way. It's as if I am emotionally unstable and lack the ability to sustain a stable intimate relationship. I also believe that I can't hold onto any relationship.
output: Hello, based on your description, the way you handle intimate relationships resembles the ambivalent attachment style in psychology. Ambivalent attachment is a type of insecure attachment that was discovered in the study of mother-infant relationships. It was proposed by American psychologist Ainsworth in 1978 based on the Strange Situation Test. Babies with this attachment style appear to be very vigilant when their mother is about to leave, and they become extremely distressed and resistant when the mother leaves, often crying loudly during even brief separations. However, when they are with their mother, they are unable to use her as a secure base for exploration. When the mother returns, their attitude toward her is conflicting, as they seek contact with her while also resisting it. They may get angry and push her away when she comes close. It seems difficult for them to return to playing games, as they frequently look towards the mother. (Information sourced from Baidu Baike) The attachment style established between an infant and their mother in early stages of development is often replicated in adult intimate relationships. Therefore, in your description, I see elements of the "the more someone pursues me, the less I agree" pattern and the desire to provoke the other person after they have calmed down or stepped back, to make them continue pursuing or to maintain the posture of retention. Furthermore, you often push away this person and the relationship over minor things, wanting to go back to square one, and frequently doubting whether this person truly loves you, often magnifying small details. These characteristics all appear to resemble the ambivalent attachment pattern. It seems that deep within your heart, there is a hidden belief: a lack of belief in being loved. To prove this belief, you try every possible way to collect "evidence" that this person doesn't love you enough, and unconsciously sabotage the relationship again and again. To improve these beliefs and establish a secure attachment style, it is recommended that you seek psychological counseling if conditions permit.

Maybe it has to do with the fact that I was given away to someone else when I was born. In my foster mother's home, I was stubborn, but when my mother hit me, I became afraid to express my emotions and thoughts. In light of your description, let me share my thoughts: good friends are there to trouble each other. Building interpersonal relationships is based on continuous interaction, and good interpersonal relationships make both parties feel comfortable and recognized. Ultimately, good interpersonal relationships satisfy our need for recognition. I don't know if you feel the same way, but after helping others, whether or not we receive material rewards or just a simple "thank you," or seeing the other person improve under our help, we feel a sense of fulfillment. Good interpersonal relationships contain this feeling and involve mutual giving. On the surface, it may seem like I give you something and you give me something in return, but in this give-and-take process, both parties can feel the care and recognition from each other. It's not a process of mutual cancellation, but a process of strengthening each other's relationship. It's not 1-1=0, but 1+1=2. We are not currency, so we don't need to and can't please everyone. We need to learn to say no appropriately. Some of the troubles in life exist because we do things that we shouldn't be doing and think that by helping others, they will recognize us and our "sense of accomplishment" will increase. However, reality may not be like that. Those things we shouldn't be doing and don't enjoy doing bring us more troubles instead of a "sense of accomplishment." Learning to say no appropriately is the foundation of becoming a confident person.

How to chat with strangers online and not know what to say all the time?

I don't have many friends, and sometimes I feel lonely. I want to chat with someone, but I never know what to say. After saying "hello" a few times, I don't know what else to talk about and it becomes awkward. Asking about age and work feels too personal, and even if they answer, I still don't know what to say next. I feel like I can't fit into these conversations, like an outsider. I say things just to get by, while wondering how others would respond. I'm always worried about saying the wrong things because I don't know what I mean myself. I'm just imitating, maybe I'm suppressing myself? But I really have a strong desire to chat. What am I lacking?
output: OP, hello, every suppressed soul lacks the opportunity to be seen by others and the courage to express themselves truly. From your description, I can feel your strong sense of loneliness and the helplessness of not being understood or known by others. You may not be very skilled in socializing, but you have a strong desire to express yourself and establish connections with others. It seems like you hesitate a lot when chatting with strangers, probably because you feel too lonely. When it comes to starting a conversation, you might need to have different topics for different people. When you know absolutely nothing about the other person, including their gender, you can choose some trivial topics that everyone can talk about. For example, the weather, popular TV shows, and music. Focus on the other person and initiate topics that give them a sense of being cared for and valued. When they ask you questions, answer them sincerely based on your own feelings. If you feel comfortable answering, do so sincerely; if you feel it exceeds your boundaries, politely decline. In the virtual world of the internet, to be understood, seen, and have stable relationships, you may need to chat continuously and steadily with one person, genuinely making friends. With time, as you talk about more topics and get to know each other better, the topics will become more personal and relatable, and the relationship may become more stable. Additionally, you only have the desire to ask questions when you genuinely want to know about the other person. If your goal is to meet a stranger and expect them to understand you and become your confidant with just a few words, the chances are extremely slim. Don't force conversations. When one day the topic can no longer continue, you can wait until the next day or the day after to ask some questions you genuinely want to know. Respect the other person's privacy and interests, and don't interrogate them. Start with simple topics like hobbies and interests. This might give the other person a better impression and a sense of trust. Lastly, be sincere. There are many people making friends online, and their motives can be complex. Learn to identify and stay away from such people. As for those who sincerely answer your questions, be equally sincere in expressing your feelings and who you are because we can sense whether the other person is being perfunctory or genuine. Best wishes.

Is it possible to still have trouble sleeping even after taking sleeping pills due to a fear of sleep?

Severe depression, mild anxiety, been taking medication for 3 years, including sleeping pills which also induce fear of sleep. I have always been resistant to sleep, to the point where even with sleeping pills, I still struggle to fall asleep. I take the maximum dosage of sleeping pills.
output: Hello, I can really understand your pain. Because like you, I have also been consumed by insomnia day after day in the swamp. Including now, I also need to take sleeping pills, also known as tranquilizers, in order to achieve relatively stable sleep. First, why do we need to sleep at night? (1) Work at sunrise and rest at sunset. This is the order that the universe and nature have given to humans. Humans can never escape the laws of nature. Our bodies are not made of iron, and the laws of nature will allow us to choose to pause the activity of our bodies at specific times. Just like plants need photosynthesis during the day, humans also need to be active during the day. And sleep at night to detoxify our bodies. But what embarrasses us is that although the arrival of the night makes our bodies feel exhausted, our thoughts and consciousness often go against our physiological mechanisms. This is the fundamental cause of insomnia. The body is tired, but the mind is difficult to stop, this tug-of-war brings us suffering. I'm sure you are well aware, no matter how big your psychological problems are, your doctor will repeatedly tell you to sleep well at night. That's why you take some medication as an aid. (2) Chronic insomnia creates a negative "butterfly effect". The suffering caused by insomnia is not just the depression and anxiety of not being able to sleep at night. It is a series of long-term physical and psychological torment. 1. When you have insomnia for the first night, it will be difficult for you to get up in the morning, and even if you get up, you feel like you want to sleep. You feel drowsy and have low efficiency in daily life and work, decreased memory and prone to mistakes. You can't help but try to "catch up on sleep" and "sleep back" during the day. 2. When it comes to the second night, you will have insomnia again. Because your brain has been exhausted during the day and has been in a semi-calm state, if you take a nap during the day, your brain will think that you should be awake now. You will feel energetic and want to use your phone. As a result, you toss and turn and can't sleep. 3. When you have been in this state of "day and night reversed" for a week, your biological clock will be completely disrupted. In this situation, the brain that controls your emotions will experience functional disorders due to your long-term insomnia. And your body will be overdrawn due to lack of sleep. It is easy to feel tired all over the body during the day, limbs ache, lack of concentration, and frequent mood swings. Insomnia can cause people to become more depressed and anxious under stress. And friends who originally had depression and anxiety will exacerbate psychological problems due to insomnia. Second, if you already have psychological problems and insomnia is getting worse. Is it still possible to get better? Friends with chronic insomnia always say the word "desperate". But in fact, based on my personal experience of long-term battles with insomnia, I think insomnia can be overcome. Because of work reasons, I used to stay up late frequently. Later, it evolved from not being able to sleep to not being able to sleep at all. I felt tired all day and could only rely on coffee to stay awake. At night, I would lie in bed and try to fall asleep but couldn't. Now, I still need medication to improve the quality of my sleep, but through my efforts and adjustments for a period of time, I can now go to bed around 10 pm and wake up at 6 am every day. I want to tell you through my experience, dear friend, although insomnia is really terrifying. But this is not a bottomless abyss of despair. As long as you have hope and strive to change, you can also develop good habits of going to bed early and waking up early, and have a vibrant life! Third, how should we get out of the predicament of insomnia? I have three suggestions to share with you. Insomnia is scary, and even scarier is the "learned helplessness" psychology that we develop when facing insomnia. Faced with the frustration of insomnia, many people surrender, even if they use sleep aids, it is difficult to get better. The person will become more and more powerless. As a mental health practitioner, I must responsibly tell you that although sleep aids can indeed reduce the activity of your brain to a certain extent and promote the secretion of melatonin, if you excessively rely on medication without making comprehensive adjustments to your body and mind, even the best sleep aids can easily develop resistance in your body and become addictive. Just increasing the dosage of medication to force yourself to fall asleep may eventually lead to the medication becoming ineffective and unnecessary harm to your body. To overcome insomnia, you need internal and external adjustments. Only you can change yourself. I suggest the following, hope you can adopt it: Suggestion 1: Pay attention to the problem of insomnia, adopt the 21-day habit formation method, and conduct sleep training to adjust your biological clock. Many people can't get out of insomnia because they always underestimate it and treat it as a minor problem. Finally, it becomes difficult to recover. So, when you feel that insomnia has become unbearable, you need to make overcoming insomnia your most urgent goal. To succeed, you must plan ahead and meet your needs. I personally made a 21-day chart for myself. And I would check off the goal of going to bed and waking up early in the chart every day. I will share my 21-day sleep adjustment method with you. (1) Step one: In the first week, I would require myself to finish washing up at 10 pm, go to bed at 11 pm, and fall asleep at 12 am. (2) Step two: In the second week, I would require myself to finish washing up at 9:30 pm, go to bed at 10:30 pm, and fall asleep at 11 pm. (3) Step three: In the third week, I would stick to the schedule of the second week and strictly follow it. Here are some important tips to remember: Key point one: Set an alarm on your phone to remind yourself, and when it's time to sleep, turn off your phone. Avoid unnecessary temptations. At the beginning, it is the most difficult because there are many things on your mind at night, and you can't help but think about them. However, when I think of how uncomfortable I will be the next day, I force myself to follow the schedule. Key point two: It is recommended to take sleep aids at 8 pm. Because it takes time for the medication to digest and take effect. Key point three: In this process, there will inevitably be temptations. So before starting the 21-day sleep execution plan, I will inform all my friends that I will not participate in any evening entertainment activities, including playing games, singing, watching movies, etc. And I will ask the people around me to supervise me. After 3 weeks, you will find that your body and brain have completely formed a "conditioned reflex" of going to bed and waking up early, and good habits have been formed. Sleeping on time is no longer a problem. The inertia that human beings possess will keep you persisting in going to bed and waking up early. Suggestion 2: In order to avoid insomnia at night, you must fully engage in activities during the day to consume energy. This ensures that you have excess energy at night. Many people can't sleep at night because they sleep too much during the day. Our bodies naturally seek balance. If you put the things that should be done during the day at night and the things that should be done at night during the day, it will eventually lead to a reversal of day and night, and create a vicious cycle. Therefore, I suggest that you find a way to make your daytime activities more fulfilling and not procrastinate or be lazy. (1) For example, you can try participating in activities that consume a lot of energy during the day, such as running or swimming. Exercise can release the body's energy, and it can also secrete dopamine to bring a sense of pleasure. More importantly, it can help your body better sense the signal of rest at night, and improve sleep. (2) For example, you can change the way you work and study, try to be more efficient during the day. Many people work overtime and stay up late not because they are really busy, but because they procrastinate. If you want to sleep well, then the things that should be done during the day should not be done at night. If there is not much work recently, you can try cleaning the house, organizing items, or taking a walk in the neighborhood garden. Don't lock yourself inside and spend every day lying in bed using your phone. Chinese culture emphasizes balance between yin and yang, and only by practicing it can you overcome insomnia. Suggestion 3: To overcome insomnia, you need to create a conducive sleep environment for yourself and adjust your nutritional status. (1) To sleep well, you must create a good sleep atmosphere. If you still listen to heavy metal and watch episode after episode of TV shows at night, and the lights are bright, then your central nervous system will mistakenly think that it is still daytime. This will make it more difficult for you to fall asleep. I suggest you change your sleep environment. For example, listen to soothing music before bed, buy pillows and bedding that suit your sleep, wear comfortable pajamas, and use the softest lighting in the room before bed. You can even use lavender aromatherapy to relax yourself. A good sleep environment can bring a sense of security to your mood and alleviate your anxiety and depression to some extent. It is helpful to you. (2) Try meditation and breathing relaxation exercises before bed to better enter deep sleep. Many people have a lot on their minds and are unable to let go of the problems they encountered during the day when they lie down. This burdensome and psychological baggage on top of the already heavy burden will make it difficult for you to sleep well. If you want to sleep well, you need to let go of the burden on your mind before bed. Relax completely. Choose a comfortable position, or you can sit cross-legged. Then let your brain relax completely, meditate. Breathe in a rhythmic manner, drive away the troubles of the day completely. Through meditation and breathing exercises, you can calm your mind, and you can sleep soundly. (3) In order to sleep well, you should pay attention to your eating and drinking habits. Many people can't help but have an extra meal at night, eat spicy and stimulating food, and even drink too much coffee or alcohol. This increases the burden on the stomach and intestines. The organs that should rest at night have to accompany you in staying up late because of your desire for food and drinks. Of course, you will not sleep well. It is of no benefit and only harms your physical health. Therefore, do not eat cold and spicy foods before bed, and avoid drinking stimulating teas and coffee. Control your diet, and you will have better sleep. Before bed, you can try drinking mild beverages like milk to help with sleep, and during the day, try not to overindulge in food and drink to avoid burdening your body. These are all my analysis and suggestions. Insomnia is really a painful enemy. Not being able to sleep well deprives us of vitality during the day and makes us increasingly unhappy. The body becomes worse and worse like a deflated balloon. Only by breaking it can we make progress. In the miserable cycle of insomnia, it is better to boldly overcome insomnia. Come on! Thank you for reading, please like and follow!

However, this macro perspective is made up of countless micro moments like a year, a day, an hour. Each day in our lives is experienced one by one. How we spend each day in the span of a few decades, what we can experience is completely different. Although we go to work every Monday to Friday, the work content is similar every day, such as browsing resumes, making phone calls to schedule interviews, interviewing, negotiating salaries, and arranging new employee onboarding... But today, maybe we will come across a particularly suitable resume, have a particularly smooth phone conversation, and directly schedule an interview for the next day. When we hang up the phone, we feel really good and think about buying a big cup of hazelnut latte at noon to relax under the sun. The next day, the candidate stands us up and doesn't come, it's really disappointing. Every day, there will be different experiences. After experiencing disappointment, maybe there will be an even better resume tomorrow! Colleagues, friends, family, children are changing every day, giving us different challenges and emotions every day. A high school classmate who hasn't been in contact for many years may suddenly come to town and invite us for a meal, and on the way, we help a mother pushing a stroller by holding the door for her, receiving her heartfelt thanks... Every little thing can bring us special experiences, good or bad, pleasant, sad, angry, painful, and disappointing... These experiences may enrich our inner selves and make us who we are now, and we can become an even better version of ourselves in the future.

I am currently working in an overseas branch of a trading company. This company has a family-style management model and emphasizes loyalty. At the same time, through a friend's introduction, I interviewed with another company in the same city. The interview went well, but the salary offered was lower than what I'm getting in my current company. Taking other factors into consideration, I politely declined the offer. Later, I found out that the person in charge of the company where I interviewed knows the leader of my current company. They called to inquire about my situation, and now everyone in my current company knows about my job interview with the other company, but they still want others to convince me to stay. Just today, the company I interviewed with called me again, expressing their desire for me to work there. I am now torn about whether I should resign and go there.
output: This is the fourth question I am answering, hoping to be helpful to you. As the saying goes, the workplace is like a battlefield, in the workplace, apart from interests, there is nothing else! This point must be clear, everything is about profit for the company and for you! In order to help you make a good choice, let's analyze the situation you are in and your subconscious mind. 1. Regarding the current situation: you are relatively satisfied with the salary of your current job, but you are not satisfied with the operation mode of the current company and some criticisms of a traditional family business. You have even reached the point of considering leaving the job, although you have not resigned temporarily and are struggling to push the work in your own way. However, the fact that you have already interviewed with another company has happened and you have been recognized. In your subconscious, you also have expectations for the new company, but the salary is not as expected. In addition, because the two company's bosses have connections, your intention to seek another way has also been known by the boss of the current company. The current situation may be a bit awkward and there may be more uncertain risks in the future, so you are struggling to decide whether to stay or leave. 2. About the risks: firstly, the direct reduction of salary is definitely the most basic consideration and will have the most direct impact. In addition, the importance of loyalty in family businesses will directly affect the development of your current work. This is a big taboo in similar family businesses, unless the boss makes a wise decision or you are truly outstanding in your abilities, otherwise there will definitely be hidden dangers in the future, which will eventually have an impact. Finally, the decision to stay or leave, when we work outside, we are all tools, and the goal is to support ourselves and our families through work. The company values certain values that are beneficial to its development. Considering your current situation, there are risks whether you stay or leave, and you can only weigh the pros and cons and make a choice based on maximizing your interests. 3. About the decision: this is a comprehensive consideration and requires an overall analysis, such as money, pressure, career prospects, reputation, interpersonal relationships, and so on. This is a difficult process, and I believe you have been struggling with it. Let's make it simple and use the anticipated results to deduce how to choose. Result 1: stay in the current company. In a family business, they despise employees who do not follow their rules. They only look at the results and whether they bring benefits. If there is any slight mistake, it will be blamed on you, and you will eventually be replaced sooner or later. Result 2: leave! Go to the new company. There are two possibilities. One is that you find the opportunity is good after joining, the company is of high quality, there are no criticisms of a family business, no restrictions, and you can truly achieve results and realize your value. The other possibility is that you find no change after joining, you are still a tool, you have no say, you receive even less money than in the previous company, and you may even be more passive in your work. This is difficult to avoid, and it is not a good idea to go back to the previous company, so you must clarify again in the employment contract to reduce unnecessary risks. In summary, there are two outcomes and two choices. I can only help you analyze but not decide. In life, we face multiple choices, and this time, I hope you make the right choice. It is best to listen to your inner self and remember that the future journey is long. Based on comprehensive risk avoidance, you must consider all aspects and make every effort to protect your own maximum interests.

Do you constantly reflect on every sentence and belittle yourself?

I need to reflect on myself after every sentence I say, and I feel really awful about myself.
output: Hello, hug. I don't know how long this kind of self-evaluation "feeling bad about yourself" has been around. Every time you say something, you have to reflect on yourself. It's so tiring and unrewarding, constantly lingering in your ears. I imagine you must be very upset. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ In your impression, do you remember the first time you evaluated yourself like this, when and what happened? Who were the people around you at the time? How did you feel when you evaluated yourself? What did you do? What did you say? What kind of expression was on your face? Now, looking back, if the current you stood in front of the past you, what would you like to say or do to the past you? If it were me, I would definitely hug the sad me and say, "You've been working hard. I know you've done well!" -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ Psychoanalyst Sigmund Freud proposed the structural theory of the id, ego, and superego. The id (completely unconscious) represents desire, suppressed by consciousness. The ego (mostly conscious) is responsible for dealing with the real world. The superego (partially conscious) is the conscience or internal moral judgment. The superego is the regulator in the personality structure, governed by the principle of perfection, monitoring the ego and internalizing the symbols of the father figure and cultural norms. In other words, the formation of the superego is mainly related to important caregivers in childhood, judging whether a person is "good" or "bad" and what one "should" or "should not" do. From this perspective, "feeling bad about yourself" may be the definition of yourself given by important others in your childhood, which gradually transforms into the judgment of your superego towards yourself. So, who is this important other person? In your memory, do you remember any occasions when something like this happened? What was his facial expression when he said "you're bad"? What did he do? How did you feel? I imagine that, like now, you were very sad and upset at that time. However, it is not your fault. In childhood, in order to survive and grow up, we had to rely on others and let them evaluate us indiscriminately. In fact, you are very brave. In such a sad situation, you have overcome it time after time. Now, you have grown up and can take responsibility for yourself and cheer yourself on. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ Now, please ask yourself the following four questions. Is it true that you feel bad about yourself? Can you be sure it is true? How do you react when you hold this idea? Can you find a reason to let go of that idea? Can you find a reason to hold that idea without any anxiety? What kind of person are you when you don't have that idea? These are four sentences from the book "A Turn of Mind," which has helped many people. I wonder what answers or different experiences you will get after asking yourself. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ In addition, you can ask yourself, you said every time you say something, you reflect on yourself and feel bad about yourself. So, are there any exceptions? Have you ever said something and felt that you are not so bad? When was that? What happened? When you say you feel bad about yourself, if you give a score of 0-10 to bad, with 0 indicating good and 10 indicating very bad, can you define a score for each thing or each sentence? Observe how you act when it's a 0 or 1. Perhaps this can be your direction for improvement next time. -------------------------------------------------- ------------------------------------------ I hope my answer can give you some references and thoughts. The world and I love you.

You have the courage and the ability to think. I'll share my understanding with you, and we can explore it together. Our instincts may tell us that it would be great to follow our hearts, to love multiple people without being tied to one person for life. It seems more in line with human nature. But when we think about it on a deeper level, it may not necessarily be true. Setting aside morals, in real life, infidelity is not uncommon even in monogamous relationships. However, if we have no constraints of marriage, we may go to another extreme. Just imagine. It's okay if only a few people have the idea of loving multiple people, the impact on society may not be significant. But what if everyone is like that? It's unimaginable, right? Society may become chaotic. Looking at it from a psychological perspective: people achieve a dynamic balance between constraint and freedom. If there is only freedom, it may not necessarily be good for the individual. People have reason and can recognize their own existence, as well as phenomena such as aging and death. So people develop a feeling: loneliness. And with loneliness comes fear, fear of losing connection to the outside world, fear of being overwhelmed by the world. Therefore, the greatest need for people is to overcome the feeling of loneliness and reestablish connections with others and the whole world. But indulgence cannot drive away loneliness. The unity achieved through indulgence is temporary. Once the effect of the pleasure wears off, people become clear-headed again and the feeling of loneliness resurfaces. So indulgent people have to repeat this process over and over again. Only love can bring people closer, allowing them to form new unions and truly overcome loneliness and fear, and find meaning in their existence. Moreover, it cannot be all-encompassing love. Sometimes, loving too many people may not deepen the connection with individuals. Because love also implies responsibility. I'm not saying that one should only love one person for their whole life, but there may be many differences between loving one person wholeheartedly and loving multiple people at the same time. Love is a giving, not a taking. In the process of giving to each other, both parties awaken the vitality within each other, and obtain happiness and fulfillment. That's the beauty of love. Perhaps one day, you will willingly choose to love only one person. Erich Fromm said: positive love also requires four essential elements: care, responsibility, respect, and knowledge. output: Recently, I happened to be reading "Flow: The Psychology of Optimal Experience," and the author's mentioned concept of psychic entropy can be used to explain the issues raised by the original poster. Entropy, in a sense, describes the degree of disorder and chaos in things. The higher the level of disorder, the higher the entropy value. Applied to the realm of the mind/thoughts, we call it psychic entropy. The abundance of products provides a plethora of information, and the influx of a large amount of information can increase psychic entropy. Happiness, on the other hand, can only be experienced when the entropy value is sufficiently low. Therefore, if the abundance of internet products only leads to an increase in a person's psychic entropy, it will diminish their sense of happiness. However, if a person has strong integrative abilities, the abundance of information will provide them with more materials, and from this perspective it may help them lower their psychic entropy (incorporating previously disordered/unable to integrate aspects through the addition of new materials). So, to sum up, I feel that internet products and other forms of information are the same - they can be used to your advantage if you can handle them, but if you are controlled/drowned by them, they can harm you.

When faced with oppression from people close to you, constantly shedding tears, how can one overcome it?

Being suppressed by important figures such as the boss, boyfriend, or family can create a sense of worthlessness and inadequacy. It causes a great deal of emotional pain, leading to immense internal suffering and an overwhelming feeling of sadness, as if being torn apart. The desire to leave the company and distance oneself from those who suppress can be strong. Although not opposed to receiving advice, it becomes intolerable when it is unreasonable and leads to arguments and emotional distress. There is a strong desire to slack off at work and increase social interactions since being unappreciated. However, accepting these thoughts and feeling at peace with them is difficult and leads to profound sadness, potential difficulty in coping, and even depression.
output: Hello! Before answering, give me a hug! I see that you often suffer from oppression and criticism from close people, which causes you pain. It shows that deep down, you long for their approval and praise. But why do we need constant validation and praise from others? Dr. Chapman, a famous American psychologist, found in his years of psychological research that in all psychological games, there are three roles: persecutor, savior, and victim, and everyone constantly switches between these three roles. The person in the victim role often appears very aggrieved and pained, but in reality, they receive a lot without giving much in return. Although the other person may seem selfish and indifferent, resembling a persecutor, they actually bear a lot of responsibility and give a lot. You can try to see if you unconsciously put yourself in the position of the weak and the victim in relationships. Common clues include feeling helpless, weak, vulnerable, and pitiful, often feeling lonely and helpless, perceiving others as selfish and indifferent or untrustworthy and capable of harming you, avoiding or relying on others when faced with issues while resisting others' demands and suggestions, often abandoning tasks or having a good start but not following through, often longing to go back to childhood or the past, imagining a carefree and worry-free state... So, by catering to their ideas and making ourselves so unbearable, we are actually using self-harming behaviors to make the other person feel guilty. However, this method may not always be effective and may instead cause us more pain, even leading to depression. It may be helpful to replace ourselves with the perspective of a strong person, objectively view others' evaluations, face our own strengths and weaknesses, and strengthen our inner selves in order to better face ourselves and the real world. When hearing oppression from others: Do not see it as their evaluation of you. Sometimes when expressing opinions about specific events, people may mistakenly associate the event with the person. We need to judge whether what they say is only about that particular event, whether it is due to our failure to take responsibility, or whether it is a difference in concepts and ideas between us. In any case, do not see it as an evaluation of you. Lowering self-evaluation can lead to feelings of depression and low self-esteem, causing painful thoughts. Therefore, when communicating, it is inevitable to continue the communication methods they have experienced before. So we need to determine the underlying perspective of the oppression. High school student. Over the past five years, I haven't been very sure about who I really am. I am good at observing the connection between people's emotions, facial expressions, and experiences. And I always put myself into the shoes of a movie character or someone else. My words, expressions, and even walking style would match those of the person I am imitating. I turn every action of the person I imitate into my own behavioral standard. I have no idea how I should be. And when I can't achieve it, I start to self-doubt and feel worthless. I feel like I can become anyone, except for myself. I can't feel my own existence. This makes me very painful because it's like acting for a lifetime, never being "real". My emotions are also unpredictable, one moment I can laugh heartily, and the next moment I can be silent and quiet like a statue. These are genuine emotions, without any deliberate intention. Others describe me as "sometimes like an old man, sometimes like a little kid." I am confused about myself, I have studied others thoroughly but know nothing about myself.
output: Congratulations, you have the question of who you are, which shows that you have begun the process of separating from others. When we were very young, we were in a symbiotic state with our mothers. Infants would feel that their mother is me and I am my mother, we are one person. They wouldn't have the concept of imitation. You become aware of yourself imitating when you realize that you and the person you are imitating are independent individuals. The existence of "me" is what allows me to imitate others. Your confusion may lie in whether there should be a very clear boundary between me and others, whether I should be very different from others, and whether I need to be unique in order to distinguish myself from others and see my own existence. Indeed, everyone has their own characteristics, but it cannot be denied that we also have some commonalities as humans. Self does not necessarily mean being unique. Even if you make the same choices as others, it is still your choice. Ninety percent of what a person experiences in their lives is learned, and imitation is a very common learning behavior. Your experiences, personality, and environment are all different from his, so it is difficult for you to replicate his path. The person you are imitating must have something that you desire, perhaps his achievements, his relationships with others, or certain qualities he possesses. You desire these things, but you are not sure how he acquired them or what conditions are needed. So you use the methods you are capable of to approach your goal and imitate his every word and action. You can become aware of what you envy in him, and if you were to become that person, what would make you happiest? What conditions are needed to achieve this, and what conditions does he have that I do not? Under the current conditions I have, are there other ways to achieve my goals? Growth is a marathon-like, long-term process, not a fixed standard. In different stages, you will find that the self also changes, and you will not always stay at a certain point in the river of time. Your body will change, your environment will change, your needs will also change. Personality is only a relatively stable thing, and in fact, there are countless subtle differences. I am thirty years old this year, and I am still exploring internally and still searching for the answer to who I am. I believe that even when I am eighty years old, I will still be moving forward on this path until the day my life ends. Although we may not have the same experiences and feelings, we are all on the path of searching for ourselves. I hope this solitary lamp can provide you with some company.

Neither overreact nor be impulsive. If you encounter a serious matter that requires a rational approach, and you overlook this and only focus on your own emotions, it won't work. Thus, rationality and emotions should be used in the appropriate context to truly become a rational person. 2) Whether overly rational or overly emotional, don't blame yourself. Some people may wonder why they are always so rational/emotional. They feel their behavior is abnormal, leading to a self-disgust. However, this is completely unnecessary. If you are a rational person, it doesn't mean you are cold-hearted; to some extent, you are more composed and calm than others. If you are an emotional person, it simply means you are more sensitive, more prone to catching feelings, and it is not a big deal. Therefore, change is possible, but try to accept and understand the problems that exist within your emotions. 3) In the balance between rationality and emotions, what suits you best is the ideal choice. For example, if you are a male but constantly live in an emotional state, easily shedding tears in a sentimental manner, it can easily lead others to form strange opinions or give you strange looks. So, be true to yourself and act according to your own characteristics. Acting against your own nature is the strangest behavior. We gradually learn what we should do, should not do, what we should think, and what we should not think through society and culture. So, when we autonomously generate some "immoral" thoughts, we receive punishment and criticism from the superego to suppress these immoral ideas, causing inner conflict and struggle. As long as we limit fantasies to our minds and do not turn them into actions, we can tell ourselves that there is nothing wrong with them and thereby alleviate the inner conflict. "Why are many friendships built on relationships where they need my help?"

Since the beginning of my junior year in high school, I always thought that life was normal, and my interpersonal relationships and interactions with classmates were also normal. But why is it that since I moved from an eight-person dormitory to a four-person dormitory (which is half more expensive but with better treatment), those roommates who used to be together with me started ignoring me? One friend who used to always be with me felt that I was no longer useful to her and cut off ties with me. Many friends seemed to think that I was useless and cut off ties too. Why is it like this? Why are so many friendships built on the basis of needing my help? Now I find myself on the verge of having to do everything by myself. Is it my fault?
output: Hello, I understand your feelings very well. After reading your description, it reminded me of my relationship with a classmate in junior high school. In the first and second year of junior high, our homes were in the same direction, so we went to school and went home together every day. We were like best friends who could talk about anything, at least that's how I saw it. In the third year of junior high, I moved up to an advanced class, while she stayed in the regular class. Because of the advanced class, the teachers suggested living in the dormitory, so I chose to live there. In order to go to her classroom, I had to pass by my own classroom. But when we met, she wouldn't talk to me anymore. Sometimes I would say hello to her, and she would just give me a brief smile. At first, I couldn't understand why we, who used to be inseparable, had become like this. Did I do something wrong? I was sad and upset about it for many days. Later, I realized that she wasn't someone who valued friendship. We used to be close because we went to and from school together. The deterioration of our relationship wasn't my fault. Even till today, none of my classmates have any contact with her. You mentioned that your friends who used to always be with you think you are useless now, so they cut off contact. Isn't that too absolute? They didn't explicitly say they wanted to end the relationship. It's just that you are in different environments now, and there are no more common topics. Our lives are like a train, people come and go, most of them are short-term passengers. Those who can stay with us for a longer time are few and far between. So for those people who come and go, don't get too caught up in whether they are still on the train or not. In our lifetime, we will meet many friends, but most of them are shallow relationships. To have two or three close friends is already very lucky. Even if you are now alone, those who genuinely want to be friends with you won't distance themselves just because you moved dorms frequently. As for your previous roommate, if you meet, you should still say hello, but whether the friendship is deep or not, let it be up to fate. They say love can't be forced, and the same goes for friendship. The most important thing for you now should be to shift your focus to your studies, become better and better, and believe that you can do it! May we fearlessly move forward together on the road of growth. - Wen Xi.

Is it really difficult to practice empathy? Does true empathy exist in the world?

We often talk about putting ourselves in others' shoes, but I find it difficult to truly do so in reality. Even when I try to see things from others' perspectives, my own thoughts often mix in. To be honest, I find it challenging to understand what others are thinking, let alone trying to understand what they have gone through.
output: Hello, OP. You raised a good question that shows you have been making efforts to try to empathize with others, but you haven't found the right way yet. When we talk about empathy, it's actually about thinking, not feeling. No one can completely detach themselves from their own feelings and pretend to be someone else. However, effective empathy can help us understand others' feelings and perspectives. The purpose of empathy is not to guess others' feelings or prioritize them over our own. Empathy is a step in the information-gathering process before making decisions. By gathering information through various channels, we can understand what others are going through, and their emotions are part of that information. It's like playing chess, where you first need to understand the situation and know what is happening, how each move affects each piece. Only then can you think about how to move your own troops while considering how the opponent will move theirs. We often practice empathy to improve our relationships with others, so after understanding the situation, we still need empathy. Empathy may sound like you are forcing yourself to pretend to be the other person and imagine their emotions, but in reality, human emotions are universal. You just may not be aware of their connections and lack training in making such associations. For example, an elderly person who has lost their partner would be very sad, but as a young person with no experience of romantic relationships, you cannot fully empathize. You can only deduce the situation logically, that this elderly person has lost something important and is likely very sad. Though you can't fully understand their sadness, you can consider that they are feeling much worse than when you lost your beloved bicycle as a child. So, when you speak to the elderly person, you can offer sincere words of comfort, which is within the scope of your ability to empathize. The ability to empathize is positively correlated with our ability to recognize and manage our own emotions. That's why children with little life experience cannot empathize well and people who cannot manage their own emotions also find it difficult to empathize. One useful method is to practice naming our own emotions or describing the events when we experience emotions. This can help us gain deeper insights into our emotions. The application of empathy also depends on our attitude towards others. If you believe that humans are a shared destiny community, then you would be willing to empathize with the stories of people all over the world. But if you think you only care about your parents and family, then perhaps you wouldn't be willing to invest effort into empathizing with others. In short, whether it's empathy or simply putting oneself in another's shoes, it's all about making life better. If you have motivation, you will naturally gradually develop these skills through practice.

The more "yes" we get from others, the more we can assert our own opinions, whether it is selling products or convincing others of something. This principle is very effective. When communicating with others, when we refrain from saying "no," or when we already have this thought in our minds, we are already approaching the other person because we understand their needs very well. Consequently, they will also pay attention to us. However, when the other person says "no," or has a mindset of refusal, the situation changes. Is it acceptable if friends and family members have moral issues?

A long time ago, my mother had an affair, and later she encouraged my father to do the same and asked him not to intervene with her. My father wanted a divorce but ultimately didn't go through with it and told me that he never considered me before making that decision. However, a few months ago, I discovered that both of my parents were having affairs. I was deeply hurt, and since then, I have been constantly doubting myself, reflecting on every detail of my life to see if I'm right or wrong. I haven't stopped overthinking obsessively, and more importantly, questioning my moral beliefs. Despite wanting to respect and accept everyone around me, I'm confused about how I can accept their actions. Recently, I found out that my roommate is cheating on her boyfriend, and she casually mentioned it to me and another friend. At that moment, I thought of my parents, and I don't know how to face my friend or the moral standards I know. In fact, I don't even understand my relationship with the world. I know nothing, I don't know what's right or wrong, and it's immature to always seek to judge. But I choose to treat them as if I know nothing, maybe that's safer. Is this a normal phenomenon? Is the other person's private life irrelevant to my relationship with them? I shouldn't judge, but how should I interact with them?
output: Hello! This is indeed a relatively normal social phenomenon. You think they have moral problems, it is the discomfort caused by the difference in your moral sense and theirs that makes you feel uncomfortable. Of course, you can make your own judgment. However, the meaning of this judgment is not to make others become the same as you, or to make yourself become the same as them, but to let this judgment guide your desired attitude towards life. When the moral values of others conflict with ours, emotions naturally first tell us that we cannot accept or understand them. When we find that we are powerless to change or interfere with these established facts, reason tells us some reasons that we must accept. In this way, the inner balance can be achieved, so as to avoid mental breakdown and madness. Your parents and friends, as the people who are in close proximity to you, no matter how they are divided and detached, you are all like fish in the same pond, and you will inevitably influence each other. Therefore, when they have problems, you will reflect on yourself, as if there is something wrong with you. But their problems are only their problems, and you only need to take care of yourself as much as possible to avoid being affected. What we understand as the appearance of life is only a small piece of the whole life, and its depth is mostly hidden in those inconvenient words. When you see these various forms that differ from the original imagination, it is also when you gradually understand the essence of life. It can be beautiful, but also dirty; it can sometimes bring hope, sometimes disappointment. Ethics is a human civilization, but it is not like gravity, which is truth. There are a thousand Hamlets in a thousand people, and there are a thousand moral standards, and these standards will also change with circumstances. The so-called moral sense has become more of a personal emotion, without a guideline. Therefore, morality cannot objectively punish people, but can only subjectively condemn them. When we find that others' approach to private life is inconsistent with ours and we cannot understand it, it is polite to keep a distance and be the person we want to be within the concept that makes us comfortable.

Why do some people choose to restrain their negative emotions while others choose to retaliate?

Why do some people choose to restrain themselves and shift their focus to continue working, studying, waking up early, being proactive, and staying focused, regardless of conflicts and negative emotions arising from others? Meanwhile, why do some people choose to take extreme measures and harm themselves or others as a form of retaliation, instead of taking a step back and letting things go?
