output: Hello, I hope the following answer can be helpful to you.️ **First, let's summarize the situation you described as follows: ▲ The upbringing process is not filled with verbal and emotional abuse, ▲ since adolescence, you don't want to get married and have children and find it difficult to trust marriage, ▲ facing a satisfactory blind date partner, but afraid and don't know what to do?** Schizoid personality disorder belongs to the healthy end of the spectrum, often not much different from an average person. In terms of cause, the origin of splitting mechanism can be traced back to the paranoid splitting state commonly found in infants early on. Schizoid personality disorder is similar to avoidant attachment (insecure attachment) in children, where the mother is not only rough and unreasoning, emotionally lacking, but also repulsed by physical contact with the child. Neglectful parents who disregard the child's needs may raise a child who is self-satisfied and avoids others. Individuals who have experienced isolation and neglect in their early years, out of helplessness, may avoid closeness with others and deal with external stimuli based on their own imagination. They often have a mother who has a close relationship or crosses boundaries, and a father who is cold, strict, and violent. Schizoid personality disorder includes two aspects of "splitting": the split between self and the external world, and the split between self-experience and instinctual desires. Analytical theory believes that the schizoid experience of splitting generally refers to a sense of alienation, a dissociation from a certain part of themselves or from real life. The main relationship conflicts for splitting individuals include closeness and distance, attachment and fear. In their subjective world, there is deep conflict in attachment. They long for intimacy but fear being engulfed. They want to maintain distance but cannot tolerate loneliness. They do not want to risk losing an object and also do not want to lose themselves. Therefore, they are unable to engage in relationships and cannot tolerate solitude. The famous fable of "Hedgehogs in the Cold Night" by Schopenhauer is a vivid depiction of the dilemma faced by split individuals: when they approach each other to seek warmth, they prick each other; unable to bear the pain, they separate from each other, but have to endure the cold. This conflict manifests in life, starting with a passionate and short-lived relationship, and eventually ending with long-term avoidance. This dynamic phenomenon can be summarized as, "Please come close to me to comfort my loneliness, but please maintain your distance because I don't want to be intruded upon." Your case fully embodies this point – your inner self desires warmth and love, but you are too afraid of getting hurt to get close to intimate relationships. Therefore, it is necessary to focus on personal growth, cultivate a strong inner self, and become someone who bravely faces life, the future, and intimacy. If you feel that the blind date partner meets your expectations and you are satisfied, then pursue the relationship boldly. Marriage and love are your own matters that require your own decision. Parents cannot choose for you. Faced with such parents, what can we do? We cannot choose, as it is not a matter of choice. The protagonist Su Mingyu in the TV series "All Is Well" has suffered since childhood due to being a girl and having a poor family background. She has two older brothers and has never felt warmth at home. The family used all their resources, even selling the house, to support the eldest brother's education at Stanford University in the United States and to find connections for the second brother to get into a good university and find a job. As for herself, because her brother went to college, her room was sold by her mother and she had to sleep in the living room. It can be imagined how painful Su Mingyu's internal struggles were. However, she did not let her upbringing hinder her dreams. She remained diligent and worked hard. In the end, she found a sales job, became a white-collar worker, and even climbed up to senior management. These scenes can serve as classic examples for us to learn from. Compensation for what is lacking is needed. From a psychological compensation mechanism perspective, what was lacking in childhood will be desperately sought for in adulthood. If there is a lack of adequate psychological compensation and growth during the upbringing process, the impact can be long-lasting. As adults, regardless of the circumstances, the first thing we need to do is face ourselves, both internally and externally, including parents, family, siblings, etc. We can only have what we already possess, and that cannot be changed. Accepting and growing ourselves is the first step to living a good life. What should I do if I know that studying can help myself to recover, but I have no motivation to change?

Last year, I read a book about anxiety disorders and watched half of a positive psychology video, which was very helpful for me. During severe times, I even thought about writing a farewell letter. I often felt heavy-hearted when waking up and constantly felt uneasy and worried. After studying and practicing, I did improve significantly, but I haven't fully recovered. I guess I have reached about 60-70% recovery. I know that as long as I persist in learning and taking action, I will eventually fully recover. However, I lack the motivation to do so. Whenever I start feeling a bit better, I tend to let myself go. What should I do to overcome my laziness?
output: Hello, I'm happy to answer your question. In fact, people are born with laziness. After working hard for a while, they will relax and take breaks. The key to changing yourself is to overcome this laziness, as overcoming it is a way to achieve self-realization and success. Knowing the reasons behind laziness is crucial. 1) Lack of determination and easily swayed. If you have a goal and believe in your ability to adhere to it, I think you will see it through and not give up easily. 2) Momentary lack of motivation. You may genuinely want to change yourself, but once you see some results, you relax. Initially, your change is driven by your self-will and strong motivation, so if you persist for some time, you will see results. However, later on, your motivation weakens, and although you know you need to continue, you lack the drive and determination to do so. 3) Attitude affects behavior. Changes in behavior reflect changes in your perception, and your actions reflect your current state of mind. First and foremost, you need to correct your attitude towards learning. 4) Besides personal factors, external environmental factors also contribute to laziness. If you are in a conducive learning environment with support from people around you, you will be more likely to persevere. However, this is a secondary factor, and the main influence comes from within yourself. Solutions: 1) Set a goal. Simply thinking that you should study is just a conscious activity, and consciousness cannot guide behavior. To control behavior, you need to have a goal that embodies your attitude towards the task. This will greatly help you. 2) Motivate yourself. We have consciousness and the ability to change ourselves. When facing difficulties while doing something, we need to adjust our mental state to change the current situation. You can use sticky notes to remind yourself of your goals, ignite your passion, and efficiently complete tasks. 3) If your motivation loss is due to mood, take a break and adjust your emotions. Or try diverting your mind and self-soothing. For example, go for a walk, listen to music, or even cry as a way of release. There are many ways to solve problems, and I hope you can find one that suits you.

I often unintentionally belittle another person while chatting with others in order to highlight my own superiority. Afterwards, when I face this person, I feel sorry and very guilty, fearing that he will find out that I talked about him behind his back. This feeling is really uncomfortable. How can I change this habit?
output: Hello, OP~ In your relationships with others, you use belittling another person to overcome your own inferiority and gain a sense of existence and self-worth. At the same time, you feel guilty because you intentionally make yourself feel guilty, fearing retaliation, backlash, and relationship breakdown. Belittling others does not bring you real sense of superiority and pleasure. Is that right? You expect to gain a sense of superiority by "belittling" and place yourself in a high position in the dimension of narcissism. But in reality, you may have been in a low position in the dimension of narcissism, afraid of being belittled, afraid of being judged, and unable to find your own sense of existence. You also worry about your "attacks" being "retaliated" against. Behind these behaviors and feelings, there may be a lack of inner sense of worth. The lack of sense of worth is likely to come from your upbringing. In the process of establishing a sense of worth, your parents or important caregivers may have demanded harshly from you, or neglected you, or treated you consistently with belittlement, resulting in a lack of sense of worth and leaving you in a state of low self-esteem and vulnerability. How to adjust? First, find other ways to give yourself a sense of worth. There are many ways to establish a sense of worth. Belittling others is one of the ways you use, but it has proven to be ineffective. So, you need to change your approach. Looking inward is probably a good way. Find something that truly gives you a sense of worth, such as persistently learning and acquiring a certain skill, or doing some self-healing work. Pursuing excellence and looking inward may help you overcome your inferiority. The second is to step into real relationships. As Teacher Wu Zhihong said, when a person only lives in the dimension of narcissism, they often experience feelings of superiority and power dynamics. Only by entering real relationships can you experience feelings of equality and fluidity. You must believe that everyone is unique and has self-worth.

I feel really miserable. I calmed down and put effort into having a good relationship, even preparing for marriage. However, due to my partner's lack of security and constant conflicts, he broke up with me. My boyfriend is impatient and emotionally unstable. He doesn't listen to me seriously. I don't have the energy to deal with his problems. My boyfriend becomes controlling and possessive because of his insecurity. He disregards my physical condition and wants me to fulfill his needs like a baby. If I don't meet his demands, he throws tantrums. I don't want to indulge him anymore, but when I stop indulging him, he suggests breaking up. He wants me to let go of everything and fulfill his desires, but I can't give up the work I enjoy for him. For the sake of our relationship, I communicate with him and ask him to schedule time with me in advance so I can manage my work and spend time with him. However, he says he can't accept the idea of scheduling time to be with me, so he suggests breaking up. I didn't say anything when he brought up the breakup, and we haven't been in contact for two days. I really feel awful. If I contact him first, I feel like I'm enabling his bad habits. If I don't contact him, I don't know if this is how it ends, and my mood becomes even more depressed.
output: Subject and the other party are used to being together for a long time and will inevitably develop feelings. However, it does not mean that you should continue to be with him at the expense of yourself. Even if you are deeply attached to him, you should prioritize yourself and protect yourself. Having a emotionally stable partner is a basic requirement. Only then can you have good communication, solve problems, and face the ups and downs of life together. If your partner easily gets angry and impatient, unable to solve problems rationally like an adult, you will feel very tired. A family should be supported by both parties. If you have to be both a father and a mother, do you think you can handle it? The subject describes her boyfriend as hot-tempered, emotionally unstable, impulsive, controlling, and demanding. He is clearly an infantile person who does not realize that the world does not revolve around him and that others have their own lives. If you choose to be with him, be prepared to be a mother in addition to being a partner. You will have to take care of the big and small things in life, and he may still not be satisfied. The relationship between partners should be one of equality, mutual assistance, and support. This kind of relationship is balanced and sustainable, instead of one person giving while the other keeps taking without limits. The subject should reflect on why she is attracted to someone with such strong control tendencies. By spoiling him in this way, is it because there is something missing in her own heart that needs to be filled? Therefore, this time of separation is an opportunity for you to focus on building yourself. You don't need to take care of your boyfriend anymore. He should be capable of taking care of himself. Breaking up is not necessarily a bad thing. It shows that you and your boyfriend have different values and levels of maturity. Perhaps continuing the relationship may not lead to happiness. During this time, take care of yourself, now that you are free from his control, you can have plenty of time to do things you enjoy, reconnect with old friends, and believe in your own ability to bring happiness to yourself.

Cannot accept girlfriend's past?

During our first meeting two years ago, I was my girlfriend's first love. At that time, I really liked her. However, we broke up later because of some small issues. After almost a year, she came back to me and wanted to reconcile. I agreed, but she changed a lot. She started wearing heavy makeup and liked going to bars with her friends. She also had an incredible tolerance for alcohol. I really didn't know what she had been through. Her friends often told me some negative things about her. I asked her about it, but she denied everything. She said that she had been targeted by online rumors, so there were many falsehoods. I believed her and didn't pay much attention to it. Later on, we became intimate and she confessed to me that she was not a virgin. I didn't think it was a big deal because everyone makes mistakes. I could forgive her once or twice. However, as time went on, more and more friends told me about her past. They said she had been taken advantage of by seven different people, including being drugged. Every time I brought it up, she would get angry and threaten to break up with me, accusing me of not trusting her. But as time passed, I couldn't keep it inside anymore and I asked her about all these things. Slowly, everything her friends said turned out to be true. She had been intimate with more than ten different people, many of which were one-night stands. She had been taken advantage of and she even slept with guys she met outside.
output: OP, hello. "Minding" and "unable to accept" are words of different degrees. Determine your true thoughts and feelings, make decisions early, and many things will go through the test of time. It's unknown whether they will get better or worse. From your description, I can feel that you have hesitations and conflicts in the development of your current relationship because of your girlfriend's past experiences. Maybe you need to be honest with yourself first. Do you really love her, as a person herself at present? If she didn't have those experiences, would you accept her? Can you accept everything about her now, not just her as a person, but also her changes and experiences? How do you plan to handle your relationship? If you only consider your own feelings without thinking about the other person, how would you choose? And so on. You need to be honest with yourself first. No one can influence your decision, and no one can criticize you for not truly loving her if you leave her, or praise you as a good guy if you stay by her side. Set aside all external opinions, how would you make a decision? Maybe such a decision is the closest to your heart, whether it's beautiful or ugly. Don't sympathetically accept the other person because of pity, nor despise them because of their experiences. You can choose not to accept, but you cannot disrespect. After sorting out your true thoughts and feelings, be decisive and give yourself and the other person a straightforward answer, whether it's love or not love. Being together is not about one person saving the other or one person dominating the other. It is about equality, caring for each other, sincerely managing emotions, and solving problems. If you haven't figured it out yet, you can communicate with the other person well and give yourself some time to think it through. "Minding" and "unable to accept" cannot be faked. The other person can guess from your words and actions towards them. Don't lie to yourself and learn to respect the other person. Best wishes.

Feeling unsafe when appearing too eye-catching and being afraid to dress up, what is this psychological phenomenon?

Female college students are hesitant to dress up and are also afraid to wear nice clothes. They feel extremely uncomfortable when they finally wear a beautiful dress to class because they don't want to stand out or attract attention. They always worry that being too eye-catching might be unsafe or invite criticism. What should I do? Do I have a psychological problem?
output: Hello~ Such behavior indicates that you are relatively introverted and low-key. It is not a psychological problem, and it is also related to the "focus effect." The focus effect refers to the tendency for us to unintentionally magnify our own problems infinitely. When we embarrass ourselves, we always think that others will notice, but in reality, they may notice at that moment, but immediately forget afterwards. No one pays as much attention to you as you do to yourself. Its manifestation is that we generally overestimate how much others care about us. In other words, we care so much about the impression we leave on others that we tend to think that others care about us much more than they actually do. Returning to a specific scenario, it means that you think people will notice if you wear a beautiful dress, but it is very likely that only a very small number of people will actually notice, and others will not make too many comments about it. Of course, it also indicates that you have certain concerns and insecurities internally, but as far as clothing is concerned, as long as you dress appropriately and tastefully, there is no problem.

You mentioned that you are very anxious after giving birth to your baby, to the point where you can't sleep and experience hair loss. I am a junior female student. It seems that my parents haven't approved of me since high school. My grades in high school were fine, and teachers and classmates all thought I would easily pass the college entrance exam, but my parents never believed in me and always thought I was only capable of getting into a second-tier university. Even when I actually did pass the exam and received my admission letter, they were still worried that there might be a mistake in the scores. Today, a relative's child got their exam results and did really well. My mom said that on the day when I got my results, others would also think highly of me. I went along with it and said that I was just average, but my mom said, "You are indeed average, just a mediocre student." I always feel very uneasy about this. After all, I exceeded the minimum score for the top tier university by quite a bit and got into a prestigious one, surpassing many others. But in their eyes, I am still just average. Lately, I have been preparing for the postgraduate entrance exam and studying for long hours every day. When they found out about it, the first thing they said was, "Try your best and have no regrets." Even though I haven't started yet, they already believe I won't be able to pass. I envy those whose parents praise their children for being good-looking. From childhood to adulthood, my parents have never complimented me. Even if a classmate or their colleague says I'm good-looking, my mom would say, "They said you're good-looking, is that true? You're just average. This is how we look, where could you possibly be good-looking?"
output: Many Chinese parents believe that they can instil humility, diligence, and progress in their children by belittling them, which is a strange misconception. Sometimes they belittle their children just to prevent them from being too ambitious and unrealistic, but they fail to understand the psychological impact that this "belittling" can have on their children - not only does it not necessarily achieve the intended purpose, but it can also lead to other consequences such as low self-esteem and loss of self. In light of this, we must first understand that parents are just ordinary people, not some all-powerful figures, and their views, just like those of everyone else, have their limitations. We do not need to view their opinions as sacred authority. This is a matter of awareness. In the subconscious, it is important to cultivate a healthy self-esteem and replace the need for validation from parents with a sense of self-worth. This involves some personal psychological growth work. Finding something that you truly enjoy and deriving your own value from it, rather than seeking validation from your parents, is crucial. Seeking psychological counseling can also help you rediscover your core values and establish a connection between your inner confidence and worth. As you grow older, your parents' views will no longer have excessive influence, and you will be able to fully listen to your inner voice and make choices and decisions. Stop trying to prove yourself to your parents through your actions. That only leads to losing yourself. Moreover, no matter how much you do to prove yourself to your parents, the underlying subconscious suggestion is actually reinforcing the idea that "I need to prove myself because I am not good enough."

Want to know, what kind of therapist can be considered a good therapist? What aspects are included?
output: ■What kind of counselor is considered a good counselor? A good counselor can possess many excellent qualities, while a bad counselor can also have many disharmonious aspects. It is important to pay attention to subjective evaluations by the counselor or the visitors, as well as evaluations from the industry and supervisory evaluations. Perhaps the most important aspect for a mental health counselor is to maintain a good and accepting counseling relationship with the visitor. The visitor is the counselor's client, so as the host, the counselor should have good customer service skills and make the visitor feel that their money is well spent. This kind of psychological service is worth trying again and persisting in the long term. A long-term relationship must follow many ethical and logical guidelines. There are things that the visitor must know, and there are things that the visitor can choose not to know. There may also be lies in the counseling relationship, as visitors lie. This is already a very common and well-researched fact. We lie every day, even in the counseling room. Self-disclosure contains many pieces of information that one does not want others to know, and visitors may also not want counselors to know. Maintaining a certain good impression is also a potential need in the visitor's mind. The lies in the counseling room not only mean mistrust, but also represent the resistance to revealing information. Some very difficult and fragile aspects also need to be dealt with. How the counselor handles lies to a large extent affects the trust in the later stages of the counseling relationship. The counseling relationship requires subjective trust and experiential effects. We need to know who is the subject of counseling. Are visitors coming to the counseling room just for chatting and venting? Don't visitors have friends or anyone to confide in? The ego is located in the middle layer of the personality structure, differentiated from the id, and its function is to regulate the conflicts between the id and the superego, following the reality principle. 3. The superego is located at the highest level of the personality structure. It is the moralizing self. Its function is to suppress the impulses of the id, monitor the ego, and pursue a state of perfection, following the moral principle. Freud also divided psychological processes into preconscious, conscious, and subconscious. The subconscious includes a person's primal impulses and various instincts, as well as the desires generated by these instincts, which are not understood and suppressed by customs and moral values below the threshold of consciousness. Is the fee system included in the counselor's confidentiality agreement reasonable?

Recently, I have been receiving psychological counseling at a local consulting room. Last week, I signed a confidentiality agreement. However, there is a clause stating that if I cancel my appointment at short notice, I will be charged a corresponding fee. I'm wondering if this clause is reasonable.
output: Hello! Makes sense, but not perfect. This regulation mainly protects the interests of the counselor, and the core idea is: canceling a consultation would cause financial loss to the counselor, so the responsibility should be borne by the party who proposed the cancellation. In physical transactions, even if a product is returned, it can still be resold. However, counselors are selling "time," so objectively speaking, canceling an appointment can indeed cause financial loss to the counselor. If the cancellation is caused unilaterally by the visitor, it is reasonable for the visitor to bear the responsibility. The reason why it is not perfect is because this regulation does not consider the time cost of the visitor. In other words, if the consultation is canceled due to the visitor's reasons, and the visitor bears the counselor's loss as well as their own, then correspondingly, if the consultation is canceled due to the counselor's reasons, the counselor should also bear the potential loss of the visitor, but this aspect is missing in the regulation. Additionally, there is a problem of "difficult burden of proof." The counselor's time has a "clear price," while it is difficult to "value" the visitor's time. The economic loss caused by canceling an appointment with an ordinary person is obviously different from canceling an appointment with Jack Ma. This requires the industry to introduce specific standards to treat everyone equally. But in reality, it usually doesn't escalate to "this extent," and there is still a lot of room for negotiation and resolution between both parties. Generally speaking, the counselor would express understanding to the visitor and not make them bear this cost, but rather reschedule the appointment. Wish you a happy life!

They fear making eye contact with others and avoid speaking in social situations. They often believe that people are staring at them or talking about them. The main symptoms include nervousness, difficulty concentrating, obsessive thoughts and ideas, as well as accompanying negative emotions such as anxiety, depression, irritability, and fear. Many people with this condition have trouble with normal social interactions, greatly impacting their daily life and work. However, there is no need to worry excessively. Neurosis is essentially a temporary dysregulation of higher neural activity, and fear of eye contact is a common and prevalent condition during adolescence. It occurs due to the rapid physical development during puberty, which can be challenging to adapt to psychologically, compounded by the stress of education and work, resulting in poor adaptation of the nervous system. First and foremost, it is important to maintain a positive mindset and believe that you can overcome your current difficulties. Consciously engage in more social activities and start conversations with people you are familiar with, making sure not to deliberately avoid eye contact. Trust in yourself, you can do it! Keep going, keep going, keep going!

I hadn't experienced tinnitus for over a year, and I didn't expect their emotional reaction to trigger it again. I was too blindly confident. I've been consulting with a therapist for the past five months, and I thought my emotions had improved and stabilized, so I stopped going to the hospital and taking medication for about three to four months. Now I'm really anxious about this tinnitus, not knowing when it will return to normal.

Nonetheless, this is at least a good start. The family is beginning to accept it, and we can share some successful cases to let parents know that it is not incurable, but rather requires a relatively long time and enough patience. I am always afraid of other people being indifferent towards me. How can I become more confident?

I was a bit introverted when I was young, but it didn't affect my life. Later in fifth grade, I developed alopecia areata and lost all my hair, becoming an outcast in class. From then until junior high school graduation, I was constantly bullied in class. In high school, the classmates around me became more mature, and the situation improved a lot. However, there was still psychological bullying. I remember in my senior year, my best friend suddenly became cold towards me because he found out that I was trying to "quit masturbation" (I was confused at the time and deeply believed in the "quitting masturbation" theory I found online). Since then, I have been very concerned about what others think of me. I feel extremely frustrated when he treats me bad, and it feels like my brain is going to explode. Normally, I don't get angry with others because I'm afraid they will ignore me in the future, and I rarely refuse others' requests. I'm really distressed. How did I become like this? Now I'm in my sophomore year, and a few days ago, my next-door roommate suddenly became cold towards me, but in fact, he is still nice to me. But I always worry that he will ignore me and constantly seek confirmation. It's so tiring. I keep telling myself that I'm overthinking and need to be more confident, but it still feels uncomfortable. Is there something wrong with me psychologically? What should I do?
output: Author, hello. First of all, your description reminds me of the famous "Scar Experiment" in psychology. It tells the story of psychologists inviting makeup artists to draw blood and scars on the faces of 10 participants, and then letting them look in the mirror, remembering their terrifying appearance. Then, they took the mirrors away and told the participants that the makeup artists would add some powder to make the scars look more realistic and last longer. In reality, the makeup artists quietly wiped off the scars and bloodstains drawn on their faces with cotton swabs. Afterwards, the participants were taken to the hospital and dressed up as patients, pretending to wait for their turn, to observe and experience people's reactions. After the experiment, the participants described their feelings, and surprisingly, they all agreed that others showed disgust and lacked kindness towards their scarred selves, and their eyes were constantly fixed on their scars. Did you notice? It turns out that people's perceptions about themselves can profoundly affect and change their perceptions of the outside world. Sometimes, because of the "scar in their hearts", they perceive others in a completely different way than before. So, is it possible that for you, the "scars" from fifth grade have been retained all this time, making you extremely sensitive to people's reactions and labeling certain unintentional words and actions from others as "indifference," which are then repeatedly "confirmed" in your interactions, and then you truly face a "cold" world? As for what to do, you can try to keep some distance from the feeling of being "rejected and ignored," and become aware that others' reactions and the meanings they convey may differ from what you think. Awareness is paramount; once you have awareness, there is room to do something different and bring about change.

However, once we enter the realm of daily life, we have to consider very practical issues. Even if we know that two people who are similar in every way, even if they are twins, will still have differences, so we need to seek common ground while reserving differences. output: Hello there! From your description, I can sense that you care a lot about your appearance and clothing, and that it has been bothering you. Sending you a hug. It is common for people to have a desire to look beautiful, so this is not your fault. We all want to better ourselves, and this is a common psychological trait. As a student, it is important to dress appropriately within your means and not compare yourself to others. Within your financial capabilities, you can dress up appropriately. As the saying goes, "a well-read person has an air of elegance". I believe you are aware of this. So, first and foremost, start from within. Having a good personality and working on improving yourself inside and out is necessary. Therefore, start by studying more. This can be in many aspects, such as learning from watching TV shows and movies, observing the mannerisms of sophisticated individuals. On the other hand, read more books, especially those with depth, and spend time contemplating to deepen your understanding of various topics. You can also browse online shopping platforms or read fashion magazines to improve your taste. Enhancing your perspective will help address this issue. Secondly, the simplest way is to find someone with good taste and fashion sense to accompany you when buying clothes and help you with styling. Regarding makeup, it is not necessary to know everything. Simply apply a little BB cream and learn how to do your eyebrows. Adding a touch of lipstick when going out is enough. Next, focus on your outward appearance, starting with your hairstyle. Keep it fresh and clean, avoiding those overly exaggerated colors. As for clothing, it doesn't have to be expensive, but it should be simple, elegant, and clean. You can visit clothing stores, try on different outfits, but you don't necessarily have to buy them. Remember, it's not about being expensive, just find what suits you. Surround yourself with fashionable girls, the more you observe, the more you will naturally change any bad habits. Take regular showers, change clothes, and keep things clean and tidy. Over time, you will gradually become elegant and refined. Work on improving those aspects of your personality that need change. Show care and consideration towards others, and you will become beautiful because of your loveliness. Keep up the good work! The most important thing is to cultivate your inner character. Some people may have a good appearance, but still give off the impression of being unsophisticated, simply because they lack inner cultivation. A person with inner cultivation will possess an external temperament and an extraordinary image. Improving oneself internally means refining one's own cultivation. This refers to enhancing one's temperament through culture, reading more books, improving cultural literacy, and presenting oneself as extraordinary in interactions and behavior. Additionally, maintaining a positive mindset is essential. In modern society, where material possessions are relatively abundant, many people's desires tend to expand, and the tendency to compare oneself with others is strong. It is challenging for someone with a negative mindset to have a good appearance and demeanor, so a positive mindset is also a treasure for enhancing one's own temperament. It is common for people to desire beauty, as everyone wants to improve themselves. Of course, pursuing a westernized aesthetic excessively and always striving for a westernized appearance might make people think that you are trying too hard and come across as unsophisticated.

If there were indeed some misunderstandings causing distance between you, making you feel uncomfortable, after thinking about it calmly, you could take the initiative to have a good chat with them. Whether through text messages or meeting in person, communicate and address the issues, and maybe you can rebuild a friendly relationship. There is no need to feel inadequate or unworthy of having friends because of misunderstandings or because of them. Negative thoughts like these are not helpful. Many times, when we are not recognized, it is easy to develop a sense of inferiority or self-doubt. Feeling that among them, we have lost our value and have been excluded because of our own problems, constantly doubting ourselves and leaving ourselves in a state of isolation. I can sense that deep down, you may lack a sense of security. I'm not sure about your childhood upbringing and your experiences that have shaped you. Perhaps you have been rejected, not recognized, or not valued before, which has made you sensitive and easily feel that others treat you unfriendly, leading you to constantly think that you are "targeted" or "disliked." First of all, you need to break free from this mindset and cycle. You are studying abroad, excelling in computer science, proficient in both Chinese and English, well-read, knowledgeable... these are your shining points and reflect your worth. You should acknowledge and accept these strengths, as they are the result of your hard work. Don't let others' lack of understanding or lack of support make you negate or bury yourself. At the same time, learn to understand yourself. At this stage, you may have a relatively shallow self-identification and your own recognition is built upon others' values. You are very concerned about others' evaluations and opinions of you, making it easy for you to lose yourself. You need to strengthen your subjective awareness and focus less on others, but rather on yourself. Accept your strengths and weaknesses. You have a strong learning ability, but you don't get along well with some classmates. Everyone needs to constantly learn and grow in relationships. When facing difficulties and problems, if you can firmly stand by your principles and beliefs while also being able to tolerate, understand, accept, and make progress with each other, that would be a healthy, friendly, and positive relationship worth cherishing and salvaging. We can still get to know more like-minded friends and companions. As long as we are sincere and genuinely want to be friends with others, they will feel it and treat us with sincerity. The most important thing is not to restrict ourselves and not to get trapped, which will only cause internal conflict. Lastly, I want to say that loneliness is a normal state for humans. It may be related to how well you get along with others. The main thing is to rely on yourself to regulate, learn to be alone with yourself, which is an important and necessary lesson in relationships. Keep up the good work and believe that you are always awesome!

How can I forget the person I love after breaking up?

I am deeply in love with a girl. We were very happy together. After knowing each other for 7 months, I started to doubt her. For example, I expected her to respond to my messages instantly, and if it took too long, I would think she was chatting with someone else. At the beginning of our relationship, our meetings were normal and she was always happy when we met. But later on, our meetings became fewer and even when I suggested meeting up, she didn't seem very enthusiastic. Sometimes she would even say she had something else to do and would meet next time. I feel like she was just placating me. Does this mean she doesn't love me anymore? We have broken up now, but I still can't forget her. Even if I tell myself to forget her and be resolute, I just can't do it. We haven't contacted each other for a week now. She hasn't reached out to me, and I haven't reached out to her either. But every day, I think of her, and I miss her so much, especially the time we spent together. I can't focus on anything and I feel terrible mentally. I can't let go, and every day feels so exhausting. Please, is there any way to relieve this emotional burden?
output: You love the girl very much and pay a lot of attention to her. However, love often makes people worry and doubt, causing them to have uncontrollable thoughts. These thoughts will unconsciously affect your behavior and attitude, causing cracks in the relationship. Why do we always remember past love affairs? From your description, I see that the previous relationship between you and her was mostly based on your own speculation and doubt, with a lot of "I think", but without deep communication and feedback from her or a definite answer. Therefore, you carry a lot of regrets and unwillingness in your heart, unable to find peace due to this unknown answer. Psychologically, there is a phenomenon called "Zeigarnik effect", which refers to an unfinished emotional attachment. We often worry about and cannot let go of things that are unfinished or without results, attracting a great deal of attention. For example, if we don't end up with our first love, getting married and having children, we will always remember it and give it many beautiful imaginations and speculations, so many people regard first love as the most wonderful emotional experience of their lives. For example, if we start doing something or performing a task, but halfway through we stop and have to do something else, we will inevitably still have concerns about the previous thing, unable to let go and constantly thinking about going back to finish it, resulting in the current task being affected and unable to be done properly. Your current state is because this relationship did not have a satisfying ending, and you didn't get a definite answer. So you carry a lot of regrets and speculations in your heart. This relationship, this girl will continue to occupy a space in your mind until you can find a way to put an end to it. How to have an effective farewell? Numerous speculations and imaginations are not as effective as a real action. Does she not love me? How does she view our relationship? How is she doing now? Do we still have a chance?... Many of your doubts can only be answered by her, and only she can write the complete ending for you. If you are willing, try to gather up the courage to contact her and have an open conversation, express your thoughts and understand her thoughts and attitude, let her answer your questions. Then both parties can part ways amicably. Whether there is still a possibility between you two, whether there is a chance to start again, or whether you can continue as friends, or say goodbye to each other and stop contacting each other, it depends on your own thoughts. Even if she firmly rejects you and does not want to continue contact and communication, it means that she has a clear attitude and response, and you have also obtained a definite answer. Perhaps then you can let go and move on. This is not a form of entanglement, but a responsible attitude, being responsible for her and for yourself. Perhaps she also has many speculations and regrets in her heart. A love affair can begin because of a mysterious fate, but only by parting on good terms and writing a complete ending will there be no regrets. You can also perform some ritualistic acts to bid farewell to this love affair in your heart. For example, pack up items related to her and put them away or throw them away; go on a trip to say goodbye; write down your thoughts and farewell words on paper, then seal them in an envelope; if she is willing, you can go to a place you used to frequent together, spend some time there to properly say goodbye, and then go your separate ways... How to move forward and live for yourself? After bidding farewell to this previous relationship, you need to keep moving forward --① Face your previous emotional experience bravely, review and summarize the lessons you have learned, and see in which aspects you didn't do well enough that led to problems in the relationship, and whether you can change in the future. ② Focus on your own life, pay attention to the people and things around you, and connect with those around you, discovering new opportunities for love in the process. ③ Cultivate your own interests and hobbies, do things that make you happy, and play with people who share the same interests. ④ Think carefully about your life goals and directions, and consider what you need to do to achieve them. Live for yourself and not in the shadow of someone else's past. Then, leave everything to time and let time heal your regrets. Love can make people grow, strive to become better, and you will also find new emotions.

"People say that even if it is advice, it is difficult to have a positive attitude to face it."

During the meeting, I happened to overhear something that wasn't of much use to me. I glanced at my phone, and at that moment, my aunt didn't purposely lower her voice and said, "Playing with your phone is better than not attending the class at all." I felt extremely embarrassed internally and had a particularly awkward feeling, but I couldn't express it. I remembered that whether there were many or few people, I found it difficult to not care about other people's "negative comments" about me. Even if it was advice, I felt very upset about this hurdle. After hearing it before, I felt like I was in an "ice cellar," and it lasted for a long time. Do I have a psychological problem?
output: We can start by understanding what negative evaluation means. Negative evaluation, in most cases, refers to others evaluating the methods of others from their own perspective, without considering the feelings of the individuals involved or trying to see the problem from the other person's point of view. Sometimes, their own perspective is also unfounded. Therefore, negative evaluations that we receive may not necessarily be true or useful. For example, when the questioner attends a meeting, we all know that people can get distracted. If we happen to look at our phones when the content doesn't concern us, the person might say that we should not come to class if we're just going to play with our phones. But where is the person's attention focused then? If the person is truly paying attention or if we are genuinely disrupting them, it's reasonable for them to remind us. However, if the person reacts so strongly simply because we glanced at them, it indirectly shows that they are not paying attention themselves. Moreover, they fail to take into account the emotions and reactions of the questioner and those around them. They don't make any effort to lower their voice. Wouldn't their behavior affect those around them? If the questioner were to tell the person to be more considerate and mindful of their impact, the person might respond with even more aggressive words and actions. In their worldview, everything they do is right, and any actions we take must meet their expectations to be considered correct. Therefore, we don't need to argue with them too much, and it's okay to selectively ignore some things they say. It's normal to care about others' evaluations of us. For example, when we go out, people may comment on our clothing and appearance. Some may say we look cool, others may say we look unconventional, some may even ask us for fashion advice, while others may gossip on the side. With so many evaluations, which one is correct? In fact, many things are not strictly right or wrong, but rather vary depending on people's perspectives. Therefore, the way we perceive things will also differ, making it difficult to determine who is right. We need to have a certain ability to discern, to know what truly benefits us and to differentiate between others' thoughtless comments. We need to find what is truly useful for ourselves. When faced with evaluations, we can consider the basis for why the other person said what they did, whether they truly considered our perspective, or if they genuinely have our best interests at heart. If the person is making baseless evaluations, regardless of whether they are positive or negative, we can simply ignore them. However, if the person is genuinely considering us and our feelings, we can humbly accept their input because these are the people who truly understand and love us. The world and I love you.

output: After reading the question, I have three "don't understand" in my mind: your parents don't understand you, you don't understand that boy, and that boy doesn't understand you (if the environment you mentioned that only brings you pressure includes that boy). It is not uncommon for parents to misunderstand their children, and the child is especially distressed, but I have also heard parents complaining that they cannot communicate with their children. I am not sure about the specific situation in your family, nor how you communicate with your parents. If I were in the middle, I would play a role as a bridge between the child and the parents to some extent, but as an outsider, I generally suggest seeking someone in the family who can convince the parents to do the job of influencing their mindset. You don't understand that boy, it may be more accurate to use the word "understand". He asked, "Are your parents strict?" I don't know how you replied, but you can express your feelings here that the chat seems to reveal pressure, indicating that you haven't confirmed with the other person why he would think so. I don't know how you define this boy, a friend? Acquaintance? An acquaintance who may develop into a friend? No matter which kind, if the communication is not smooth, the relationship will become distant. For example, maybe he just wants to know if the reason why you study seriously is because your parents are strict? I don't know as an outsider, but as the person involved, and with the opportunity to know it, you still don't know, so this matter can't be expanded. In addition, you said you have feelings for him. That boy doesn't understand you, because there is not enough information, so it is impossible to judge how much he wants to understand you. Doing so may be telling ourselves to distance ourselves from the past and constantly remind ourselves to become outstanding and confident. Reminding ourselves repeatedly does not necessarily mean that we have obsessive thoughts. Just like some people, they are afraid of forgetting to drink water, so they remind themselves through alarm clocks, sticky notes, and repeatedly reminding themselves in their minds. Obsessive thoughts refer to thoughts, images, emotions, or intentions that repeatedly enter the patient's conscious domain. These thoughts, images, emotions, or intentions are meaningless, unnecessary, or redundant for the patient. The patient realizes that these are his own mental activities and wants to get rid of them, but is powerless and therefore feels very distressed. So, for you, do these suggestions bring you trouble? Secondly, combining actual actions and self-reminders may achieve better results! When we remind ourselves to be confident at all times, we can also demonstrate it through actual actions. Gradually, we can develop a habit, so even if we don't remind ourselves, we may still exude confidence. Finally, when obsessive thoughts occur frequently, it may cause you certain troubles. output: Hello, thank you for inviting. I understand your sensitivity to money and the emotions and interpersonal reactions that may arise from it—times are tough, and not repaying debts is a form of interpersonal violation. You mentioned that sometimes forgetting to repay debts is normal, which demonstrates your tolerance. A 5-year-old boy refuses to write and always says he doesn't know how to write. What methods can be used to motivate him?

A five-year-old boy only knows how to write the number 1. He always says he can't write the homework assigned by the teacher. His family patiently teaches him to write, but he still can't do it, and more often than not, he doesn't want to write and just wants to play. The teacher also tells the parents that the child is the last one in the class and needs to practice writing more, otherwise he won't be able to keep up. Since he started kindergarten, he has been more active and can't sit still for long on a chair. He has a cheerful personality and many classmates like to play with him. He is polite, hygienic, and likes to share, but he does not like to study. When he doesn't want to write his homework, I tell him that he can go out and play after finishing it, but he says he won't go out then. He even says he doesn't want to go to kindergarten anymore. I don't know what methods can motivate such a young child. Do any teachers have any good ideas?
output: Hello. You are too anxious... Of course, what the kindergarten teacher said is also a source of pressure for you. And you are worried about the fear of your child "falling behind others". This layer upon layer of pressure and anxiety, when conveyed to the child, the child will instinctively resist. And the "I just can't write, I'm always last" and other labels, evaluations from others (especially from you), internalize into his own cognition and evaluation, this is the most worrying. So, what needs to change is your mindset. I suggest you read children's picture books: "Little Seed," "An's Seed," the poem "Take a Snail for a Walk," read books like "Good Mothers are Better than Good Teachers" by Yin Jianli, and "Positive Discipline," etc. Calm down your comparison, anxiety, and worry, and then learn the wisdom of being a parent. For example, don't label children, shield them from external pressures and evaluations (such as from teachers). Oh, the attitude of the mother of Little Bean in "Little Bean by the Window" and Mr. Ba in the Baidu Academy is worth learning from. Finally, only when your mindset is good, not "utilitarian," not impatient, can you "teach children". The so-called education should be fun, taking your child to nature, a twig that he picks up is like a 1, the little duck swimming in the lake is like a 2, the handcuffs opened in the boy's police uniform is like a 3, two round cakes put together is like 8. When he eats a bag of snacks, goes up stairs, you can teach him to count. The buttons on a straight elevator, the license plate of a parked car on the roadside, you can read them together. Why do you have to make him sit there and write stroke by stroke, so boring and tiring? Give him the impression that learning is boring and uninteresting, and even if he remembers and learns, will the result be good without interest? I personally am not an advocate of advanced education, my husband and I are ordinary people, and our child cannot have exceptional intelligence. My child only started holding a pen and learning to write in first grade. Before that, her hands were just used to play casually... Everything is difficult at the beginning, in first grade, she adapted to school slower than the kids who started practicing writing in kindergarten and wrote worse. Naturally, the homeroom teacher took the initiative to call me after the mid-term exam, gently and patiently complaining that my child was dragging down the class, had many "bad study habits," etc. As a qualified parent in modern society, of course, I didn't forget to smile and hurriedly thank the teacher for her concern, promising to cooperate with the school to urge the child to make progress. However, after hanging up the phone, I still adjusted my mindset and respected the child's development law. I did what I needed to do. Now, in second grade, the gap between her and those "early mature" children is no longer very obvious. This is what I think, if even I, as a mother, don't trust and appreciate my child, just blindly conform to the world's constant urging for her to fly high, fly fast, and fly far, then when she gets tired of flying, where can she find a place to rest? Where is the shelter for her to seek refuge? Look further ahead, when she turns 30, will you still care, and be entangled in whether she could write numbers from 1 to 10 at 5 years old or write numbers at 7 years old? Is such a trivial matter important? At that time, what ability will you care about the most? In the marathon of education, grasping the child's general direction is the right approach. You have to believe that sometimes being "slow" is really "fast".
